3510.05 A. All members of the AFDC assistance unit are registered for employment and training when the application for assistance is signed.

B. Future mandatory members of the assistance unit are considered to be registered by the signature on the original application.

C. Future non-mandatory members of the assistance unit are registered by signature on the request to be added to the assistance unit.

D. All members of the assistance unit must participate in employment and training requirements:

1. unless specifically exempted under 3510.10; and

2. provided the Department guarantees payment for child care necessary for participation.

E. Only members of the assistance unit may participate.

3510.07 A. Net loss of income occurs when the assistance unit's total monthly income prior to employment is greater than the unit's total monthly income after employment.

B. For the purpose of the net loss determination, total monthly income includes:

1. the AFDC grant amount:

a. after application of appropriate disregards and deductions; and

b. before recoupment is subtracted; and

2. gross unearned income; and

3. gross earned income minus actual employment expenses.

C. Actual employment expenses include reasonable work-related expenses, such as, but not limited to:

1. federal withholding tax;

2. FICA deductions;

3. mandatory payroll deductions;

4. transportation expenses;

5. out-of-pocket childcare expenses.

B. Such parents who are eighteen (18) and nineteen (19) years of age are required to participate in training or work activities, not to exceed twenty (20) hours per week, instead of educational activities, if the Department determines that:

1. the parent fails to make good progress in completing the educational activity; or

3510.15 A. The following members of a Food Stamp assistance unit must be registered for employment and training and meet the other employment and training requirements unless they are specifically exempt:

1. adults who are under 60 years of age; and

2. individuals who are age 16 or over. Individuals who become age 16 within a certification period must register at the time of recertification.

B. Only active members of the assistance unit may participate in employment and training.

C. Each mandatory registrant in the assistance unit must be registered:

1. at the time of application; and

2. once a year if the unit has had uninterrupted benefits;

3. at the time a change is reported which affects exemption status;

4. at recertification if a child became either age 6 or age 16 in the previous certification period, thereby removing an exemption.

D. Any assistance unit member can provide the information necessary to complete a registration form for all mandatory registrants in the unit.

E. An exemption may be claimed at the time of:

1. application; and

2. reapplication; and

3. a reported change; and

4. the yearly registration.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCEPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-89 Transmittal: UP-89-23 3510.23 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment and Training Requirements FS _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Exemptions from Participation Requirements _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.23 A. Exemptions from Participation

1. General Provisions

a. The case manager grants exemptions from participation in employment and training on a categorical and individual basis.

b. Individuals who are exempt from participation must be registered.

c. Categorical exemptions are granted to individuals when participation would be non-productive.

d. Individual exemptions are granted to persons with certain barriers to participation.

2. Categorical Exemptions

The following individuals are categorically exempt from employment and training:

a. a woman in the third trimester of pregnancy;

b. persons receiving General Assistance payments except those determined to be employable but not participating in the General Assistance Workfare Education and Training Program.

3. Individual Exemptions

The following individuals are considered to have barriers to participation and are exempt from employment and training. These individuals are registrants who:

a. are ill or who are caring for an ill child; or

b. have applied for or are receiving extensive social services from the Departments of Children and Youth Services, Rehabilitation Services or Human Resources Prevention Services; or

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-89 Transmittal: UP-89-23 3510.23 page 2 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment and Training Requirements FS _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Exemptions from Participation Requirements _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.23 A. 3. Individual Exemptions (continued)

c. require the use of dependent care and it is unavailable, inaccessible or unaffordable; or

d. currently reside in emergency housing, shelters for the homeless or shelters for victims of domestic violence; or

e. are currently in receipt of an eviction notice; or

f. have no access to public or private transportation and would have to walk more than 2 miles one way to the designated site; or

g. would incur non-reimbursed transportation costs greater than $25.00 per month; or

h. have temporary illnesses or imfirmaties which restrict their ability to interact in the labor market.

B. Review of Participation Exemptions

1. Categorical exemptions must be reviewed at the time of each registration.

2. Individual exemptions must be reviewed every 6 months.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 02-13-01 Transmittal: UP-01-04 3510.25 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Employment and Training Requirements FS _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Employment and Training _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.25 A. Pre-Employment - AFDC and FS

A non-exempt individual must do all of the following, unless there is good cause not to do so (Cross Reference: 3510.45, 3510.50):

1. provide additional information as needed by the Department or by an employment service agency designated by the Department; and

2. participate in job search when appropriate; and

3. be available for work; and

4. cooperate with the Department in efforts to secure employment, provide education, and job training or support services, and

5. report for an interview with an employer to whom referred for potential suitable employment; and

6. accept a bona fide offer of employment unless such employment is unsuitable, as described in 3510.40; and

7. attend either group or individual orientation sessions if requested by the case manager to do so; and

8. appear at an assessment interview when requested by the case manager to do so; and

9. cooperate in the assessment process; and

10. participate in all employment and training requirements without disrupting the employment or training activity; and

11. sign a Job Connection Plan; and

12. show a pattern of participation in activities consistent with the Job Connection Plan by keeping appointments, attending classes, and fulfilling other similar requirements detailed in the Plan.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-92 Transmittal: UP-92-33 3510.25 page 2 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Employment and Training Requirements FS _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Employment and Training _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.25 B. Employment Requirements - AFDC

1. An individual who is employed must continue in suitable employment, unless there is good cause for leaving, until:

a. it is no longer suitable; or

b. the individual becomes exempt.

2. In addition, an individual who is employed must maintain the level of earnings, unless earnings are reduced for reasons beyond the individual's control.

C. Comparable Work Requirements - FS

1. An individual who is exempt from FS employment and training requirements because of participation in the AFDC employment and training program or due to receipt of UCB must comply with all of the AFDC or UCB employment and training requirements when they are comparable to FS requirements.

2. For an AFDC requirement to be considered comparable, it must be specified in 3510.25, A, 1-6.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCEPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-13 P-3510.30 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements PROCEDURES _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirements _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Applying Penalties _______________________________________________________________________________

P-3510.30 1. When a mandatory FSE&T participant fails to comply with an employment and training requirement, determine if the individual has good cause.

2. Determine whether the individual's noncompliance affects the individual's eligibility or the entire assistance unit's eligibility.

3. Send the appropriate adverse action notice immediately after the determination in step 1 is made.

4. If the assistance unit or unit member is also being disqualified for reasons other than an employment and training requirement, send out the adverse action notice listing all reasons for disqualification.

5. Remember that the employment and training penalty continues for the minimum penalty period even if the individual complies or leaves the assistance unit before the end of the minimum penalty period.

6. Remember the following when applying penalties:

° each time a client does not comply and does not have good cause, an offense exists;

° count all offenses to determine what is the correct penalty period to impose.

7. If a Fair Hearing is requested, notify the FSE&T contractor of the scheduled time and place. An FSE&T staff member or another representative of the employment and training program may be requested to write a summary and be present at the hearing.

8. Set an alert for the end of the penalty period.

9. For FS, consider compliance to exist when the client has agreed to comply and has been sanctioned for the minimum penalty period stated in policy.

10. At the end of the penalty period, contact the assistance unit to see if any changes regarding the disqualified individual have not been reported.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCEPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-13 P-3510.30 page 2 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements PROCEDURES _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirements _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Applying Penalties _______________________________________________________________________________

P-3510.30 11. If at the time the employment and training penalty period ends you have not heard from the assistance unit or, based on the information reported, the disqualified individual is still eligible, add the individual back to the assistance unit.

12. Determine the effect on FS eligibility when a penalty is imposed for failure to comply with the requirements of the TFA or UC employment and training requirements.

13. Send appropriate adverse action notice if FS eligibility is adversely affected.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 2-1-92 Transmittal: UP-93-29 P-3510.35 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements PROCEDURES ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirements _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Determining the Designated Provider ______________________________________________________________________________

P-3510.35 Application and Recertification

1. Explain that the entire assistance unit is ineligible if the head of the assistance unit fails to comply without good cause with employment and training requirements.

2. Explain that if the assistance unit fails to select a head, the Department will choose the designated provider as head based on policy.

3. Explain that the designated provider at the time a violation of an employment and training requirement occurs is always the principal source of the greatest amount of earned income.

4. Explain that when there has been no principal source of earned income in the 2 months prior to the violation or if two individuals have the same amount of income, the Department considers the head of the assistance unit at the time of the violation to be the designated provider, and that person would remain as head.

5. Explain that the designated provider cannot be an assistance unit member who is a minor living with a parent or parental figure as described below in 3.

At Time of Violation

When the assistance unit has failed to select its head, proceed as follows:

When there is a violation, see if anyone had earned income of 20 hours per week or more or the equivalent in wages, in the 2 months immediately prior to the violation. If "yes" go to step 2. If "no", go to step 5.

If there is a principal source of earned income at the time of the violation, compare the gross earnings in that period of members of the assistance unit and any excluded household members.

Consider the individual with the highest amount of earned incom to be the designated provider unless this individual is one who is omitted from consideration because of dependence on parental authority. Make sure that the parent meets one of the conditions in policy (3510.50 B.1.b.) before continuing to #4.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 2-1-92 Transmittal: UP-93-29 P-3510.35 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements PROCEDURES ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirements _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Determining the Designated Provider ______________________________________________________________________________

P-3510.35 At Time of Violation (continued)

4. If two individuals have exactly the same amount of income, consider the head of the assistance unit at the time of the violation the designated provider, which means he or she will remain the head of household.

5. If there is no principal source of earned income at the time of the violation, consider the head of the assistance unit at the time of violation the designated provider, which means he or she will remain the head of household.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCEPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-92 Transmittal: UP-92-33 3510.45 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment and Training Requirements AFDC _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - AFDC _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.45 A. Nature of Penalty

The Department penalizes any individual who is a mandatory participant and who fails to comply without good cause.

1. An individual who fails to comply with participation requirements is ineligible and his or her needs are not considered in determining eligibility.

2. If the eligibility of the assistance unit is based on the unemployment of a parent and the unemployed parent fails to comply:

a. the needs of the unemployed parent are not considered in determining eligibility; and

b. the needs of the spouse are not considered if he or she is also not participating in employment and training requirements, even if the spouse is exempt.

3. If the only dependent child fails to comply with work requirements his or her needs will not be considered in determining eligibility (cross-reference: 2505).

B. Beginning Date of Penalty

1. The penalty period begins the first day of the month following the month in which the ten day notice of adverse action expires.

2. The beginning date of the penalty period for an applicant is no earlier than the first day on which all other eligibility requirements are met.

C. Length of Penalty

1. The length of the penalty may not extend beyond the following periods:

a. for the first offense:

(1) until the individual's failure to comply has ceased; or

(2) the date the individual becomes exempt;

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-92 Transmittal: UP-92-33 3510.45 page 2 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment and Training Requirements AFDC _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - AFDC _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.45 C. 1. Length of Penalty (continued)

b. for the second offense:

until the individual's failure to comply has ceased or 3 months, whichever is longer; or

(2) 3 months, if the individual becomes exempt during the penalty period;

c. for any subsequent offense:

(1) until the individual's failure to comply has ceased or 6 months, whichever is longer; or

(2) 6 months, if the individual becomes exempt during the penalty period.

2. The Department determines when the individual's failure to comply has ceased.

3. If an individual does not comply but agrees to comply before a penalty is imposed, an offense is considered to have occurred.

4. Before AFDC eligibility is reinstated, the Department may require a person to participate in Job Connection Plan activities for a trial period up to two weeks, to demonstrate compliance.

D. Notification Requirement

The Department provides written notification to every individual whose penalty has continued for 3 months regarding the length of his or her penalty period:

1. An individual being penalized for a first or second offense is notified that he or she may end the penalty period by complying with participation requirements.

2. An individual being penalized for a third or subsequent offense is notified that:

a. his or her penalty will continue for 3 more months; and

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-89 Transmittal: UP-92-33 3510.45 page 3 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment and Training Requirements AFDC _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - AFDC _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.45 D. 2. Notification Requirement (continued)

b. after 6 months have elapsed, he or she may end the penalty period by complying with participation requirements.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 02-13-01 Transmittal: UP-01-04 3510.50 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirements ________________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - FS _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.50 A. General Provision

Penalties for non-compliance with Food Stamp employment and training requirements are applied:

1. to the assistance unit up to a maximum of 180 days, if the individual causing the penalty is the head of the assistance unit; or

2. only to the individual causing the penalty if this person is not the head of the assistance unit.

B. Determination of Designated Provider

1. If the assistance unit fails to select a head for any reason, the Department must select one using the following procedures.

2. If there is a principal source of earned income in the two months immediately preceding the month of non-compliance with an employment and training requirement, the designated provider is the individual who earned the most income in that period, subject to the following qualifications:

a. Earned income of the following individuals is compared for this purpose:

(1) members of the assistance unit; and

(2) individuals excluded from the assistance unit who would otherwise be mandatory members because of:

(a) an intentional program violation; or

(b) ineligible non-citizen status; or

(c) lack of a SSN.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 02-13-01 Transmittal: UP-01-04 3510.50 page 2 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirements _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - FS _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.50 B. 2. Determination of Designated Provider (continued)

b. Regardless of earnings, the income of an individual living with a parent or parental figure is not used in the comparison when the parent or parental figure is any of the following:

(1) registered for employment and training; or

(2) exempt from employment and training registration because of participation in the AFDC employment and training program; or

(3) receiving unemployment compensation; or

(4) registered for work as part of the application process for unemployment compensation; or

(5) employed or self-employed working at least 30 hours per week or the Federal minimum wage x 30.

c. A principal source of earned income is an individual who is employed 20 hours per week or more or earning the equivalent of the Federal minimum wage x 20.

3. The designated provider is the person who was head of the assistance unit as of the time of the violation if, within the two months immediately preceding the month of non-compliance with an employment and training requirement:

a. two or more assistance unit members earn equal wages; or

b. there is no principal source of earned income.

C. Penalties

Penalties for non-compliance without good cause vary according to the number of occurrences. This is determined taking into consideration all employment and training violations as well as any voluntary quits on or after September 21, 1996.

1. Failure to Register

For those individuals required to comply with employment and training requirements, failure to register constitutes non-compliance.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-13 3510.50 page 3 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirement _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - FS _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.50 C. 1. Failure to Register (continued)

b. There is no good cause provision for non-compliance with employment and training registration.

c. Penalties are applied as follows:

(1) if the head of the assistance unit fails to register, the entire assistance unit is ineligible up to a maximum of 180 days. The head of the assistance unit continues to be ineligible beyond the 180 days if this is the head of the assistance unit’s third violation;

(2) if an assistance unit member who is not the head of the assistance unit fails to register, only that individual is ineligible.

d. The length of the penalty is:

(1) For the first violation, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) three (3) months after the date the individual became ineligible.

(2) For the second violation, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) six (6) months after the individual became ineligible.

3) For the third and subsequent violations, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) six (6) months after the individual became ineligible.

e. If the individual who caused the penalty becomes exempt, the penalty is canceled.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-13 3510.50 page 4 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirement _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - FS _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.50 C. Penalties (continued)

2. Failure to Comply With the Assessment Interview

a. Failure to respond to a request to appear for the assessment interview without good cause results in application of penalties as follows:

if the head of the assistance unit fails to comply, the entire assistance unit is ineligible up to a maximum of 180 days. The head of the assistance unit continues to be ineligible beyond the 180 days if this is the head of the assistance unit’s third violation;

if an assistance unit member who is not the head of the assistance unit fails to comply, only that individual is ineligible.

b. The penalty period begins with the first month after expiration of the adverse action notice.

c. The length of the penalty is:

(1) For the first violation, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

three (3) months after the date the individual became ineligible.

(2) For the second violation, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) six (6) months after the individual became ineligible.

(3) For the third and subsequent violations, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) six (6) months after the individual became ineligible.

d. If the individual who causes the penalty moves to another assistance unit and is not the head of that assistance unit, ineligibility continues for the remainder of the penalty period for that individual.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 02-13-01 Transmittal: UP-01-04 3510.50 page 5 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirement _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - FS _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.50 C. 2. Failure to Comply With the Assessment Interview (continued)

e. If the individual who causes the penalty moves to another assistance unit and is the head of that assistance unit, that unit is ineligible for the remainder of the penalty period up to a maximum of 180 days. The head of the assistance unit continues to be ineligible beyond the 180 days if this is the head of the assistance unit’s third violation.

f. If the individual who caused the penalty becomes exempt, the penalty is canceled.

3. Failure to Comply with Employment and Training Requirements Subsequent to the Initial Assessment

a. Failure to comply without good cause with employment and training requirements results in application of penalties as follows:

if the head of the assistance unit fails to comply, the entire assistance unit is ineligible up to a maximum of 180 days. The head of the assistance unit continues to be ineligible beyond the 180 days if this is the head of the assistance unit’s third violation.

if an assistance unit member who is not the head of the assistance unit fails to comply, only that individual is ineligible.

b. The penalty period begins with the first month after expiration of the adverse action notice.

c. The length of the penalty is:

(1) For the first violation, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) three (3) months after the date the individual became ineligible.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-13 3510.50 page 6 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirement _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - FS _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.50 C. 3. Failure to Comply with Employment and Training Requirements Subsequent to the Initial Assessment (continued)

c. (2) For the second violation, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) six (6) months after the individual became ineligible.

(3) For the third and subsequent violations, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) six (6) months after the individual became ineligible.

d. If the individual who causes the penalty moves to another assistance unit and is not the head of that assistance unit, ineligibility continues for the remainder of the penalty period for that individual.

e. If the individual who causes the penalty moves to another assistance unit and is the head of that unit, that unit is ineligible for the remainder of the penalty period up to a maximum of 180 days. The head of the assistance unit continues to be ineligible beyond the 180 days if this is the head of the assistance unit’s third violation.

f. If the individual who causes the penalty becomes exempt the penalty is canceled.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-13 3510.50 page 7 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirement _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - FS _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.50 C. 4. Refusal to Accept a Bona Fide Offer of Suitable Employment

There is no good cause provision for refusing a bona fide offer of suitable employment to which referred. Refusal to accept a bona fide offer of suitable employment results in application of penalties as follows:

if the head of the assistance unit refuses a bona fide offer of suitable employment, the entire assistance unit is ineligible up to a maximum of 180 days. The head of the assistance unit continues to be ineligible beyond the 180 days if this is the head of the assistance unit’s third violation;

if an assistance unit member who is not the head of the assistance unit refuses a bona fide offer of suitable employment, only that individual is ineligible.

The penalty period begins with the first month after expiration of the adverse action.

c. The length of the penalty is:

(1) For the first violation, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) three (3) months after the date the individual became ineligible.

(2) For the second violation, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) six (6) months after the individual became ineligible.

(3) For the third and subsequent violations, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) six (6) months after the individual became ineligible.

d. If the individual who causes the penalty moves to another assistance unit and is not the head of that assistance unit, ineligibility continues for the remainder of the penalty period for that individual.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 02-13-01 Transmittal: UP-01-04 3510.50 page 8 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirement _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - FS _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.50 C. 4. Refusal to Accept a Bona Fide Offer of Suitable Employment (cont.)

e. If the individual who causes the penalty moves to another assistance unit and is the head of that assistance unit, that unit is ineligible for the remainder of the penalty period up to a maximum of 180 days. The head of the assistance unit continues to be ineligible beyond the 180 days if this is the head of the assistance unit’s third violation.

f. If the individual who causes the penalty becomes exempt the penalty is canceled.

5. Failure to Comply with a Comparable AFDC or UC Employment and Training Requirement

a. Individuals who are exempt from Food Stamp employment and training requirements because of participation in the AFDC employment and training Program or due to receipt of or application for UCB and fail without good cause to comply with comparable AFDC or UC employment and training requirements are subject to penalties as follows:

(1) if the head of the assistance unit fails to comply, the entire assistance unit is ineligible up to a maximum of 180 days. The head of the assistance unit continues to be ineligible beyond the 180 days if this is the head of the assistance unit’s third violation.

(2) if an assistance unit member who is not head of the assistance unit fails to comply, only that individual is ineligible.

b. The penalty period begins with the first month after expiration of the adverse action notice.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-13 3510.50 page 9 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: FS Employment and Training Requirement _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance - FS _______________________________________________________________________________

3510.50 5. Failure to Comply with a Comparable AFDC or UC Employment and Training Requirement (cont.)

c. The length of the penalty is:

(1) For the first violation, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) three (3) months after the date the individual became ineligible.

(2) For the second violation, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) six (6) months after the individual became ineligible.

(3) For the third and subsequent violations, the later of:

(a) the date the individual complies with the requirement; or

(b) six (6) months after the individual became ineligible.

d. If the individual who causes the penalty moves to another assistance unit and is not the head of the assistance unit, ineligibility continues for the remainder of the penalty period for this individual.

e. If the individual who causes the penalty moves to another assistance unit and is the head of that assistance unit, that unit is ineligible for the remainder of the penalty period up to a maximum of 180 days. The head of the assistance unit continues to be ineligible beyond the 180 days if this is the head of the assistance unit’s third violation.

f. If the individual who causes the penalty becomes exempt the penalty is canceled.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 11-22-96 Transmittal: UP-96-20 3512 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Work Requirements FS ____________________________________________________________ Subject:

_______________________________________________________________________________

3512 This chapter describes the work requirements that an able-bodied adult without dependents must meet as a condition of eligibility for the Food Stamp program. It outlines the exemptions to the requirements and describes the time limits to participation.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 11-01-06 Transmittal: UP-07-04 3512.05 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Work Requirements FS _______________________________________________________________ Subject: General Principles ______________________________________________________________________________

3512.05 A. Unless exempt, Food Stamp recipients are ineligible to continue receiving benefits if they received Food Stamps for three full months in the preceding thirty-six month period and are not:

1. working at least 80 hours per month; or

2. participating in an approved employment and training program as described in section 3512.05 D. for at least 80 hours per month; or

participating in a workfare program which meets the requirements of the Food Stamp Act or a comparable program established by the state or a municipality.

If an individual works less than 80 hours per month, the work requirement is still satisfied if all of the following conditions are met:

the absence is temporary;

the individual retains the job; and

the individual has good cause.

Good cause shall include circumstances beyond the individual's control, such as, but not limited to:

illness, or

illness of another household member requiring the presence of the individual, or

a household emergency, or

the unavailability of transportation. (Cross reference: 3510.35)

D. An approved employment and training program includes those:

1. under the Job Training Partnership Act;

2. under section 236 of the Trade Act of 1974;

3. meeting the following standards approved by the Governor:

a. programs funded, sponsored or approved by either federal, state or local government or by a regional workforce development board;

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 11-01-06 Transmittal: UP-06-30 3512.05 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Work Requirements FS _______________________________________________________________ Subject: General Principles ______________________________________________________________________________

(continued)

b. programs not funded by a government entity or a regional workforce development board, including community work experience programs, approved by the Commissioner of Social Services or her designee;

c. vocational, technical or educational programs designed to enhance an individual’s employability and prepare that individual to secure employment.

E. Job search and job search training, even if part of an approved Employment and Training program, do not fulfill the work requirement.

F. Recipients may combine work and participation in an approved employment and training program to comply with the 80-hour monthly requirement.

G. Failure to comply with the work requirements results in ineligibility of only the individual who fails to comply, even if that individual is the head of the Food Stamp assistance unit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 11-01-06 Transmittal: UP-06-30 P-3512.10 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements PROCEDURES _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Work Requirements FS ____________________________________________________________ Subject: Exemptions _______________________________________________________________________________

P-3512.10 1. Check to see if the applicant or recipient is required to register for Employment and Training in the FS program.

2. If the client is required to register, check to see if he or she meets any of the exemptions for the work requirements.

3. Do not exempt from the ABAWD work requirement anyone who is registered for but exempt from participation in Food Stamp Employment and Training unless he or she meets one of the exemptions for the ABAWD work requirements listed under 3512.10.

If an applicant or recipient requests a medical exemption, and the reason is observable:

Eligibility Worker: Write observations of person's condition in the EMS narrative, e.g., person is wearing a cast on right leg. Include in narrative entry this statement: "Based on these observations, it is evident that this person is unable to work at the present time and is therefore exempt from the work requirement." Give to your supervisor to review.

Supervisor: Review worker's narrative. Approve/disapprove Narrate

If the applicant or recipient requests a medical exemption and the reason is not observable:

Obtain written verification from a physician, physician's assistance, nurse, nurse practitioner, designated representative of the physician's office, a licensed or certified psychologist, a social worker, or any other appropriate medical personnel that the individual is physically or mentally unfit to work.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-04 Transmittal: UP-04-26 P-3512.10 page 2 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements PROCEDURES _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Work Requirements FS ____________________________________________________________ Subject: Exemptions _______________________________________________________________________________

P-3512.10 (continued)

6. If the applicant or recipient does not request a medical exemption, but it is easily observable that the person is unable to work, explain to the individual that he or she can be exempted from the work requirement because he or she is medically unable to work, and ask the individual if he or she chooses to be exempted.

7. If the applicant or recipient is a member of a Food Stamp assistance unit that also includes a child under age 18, grant the exemption regardless of whether the individual cares for the child or whether the child is eligible for Food Stamps.

8. If both parents are residing with a child under 18, grant exemptions for both parents.

9. If the applicant or recipient requests an exemption due to pregnancy, obtain written verification from a physician with the anticipated date of delivery. Once the applicant or recipient has the child, she is no longer an ABAWD and is not subject to the work requirement as long as she lives with the child.

10. Remember that being exempt from the Food Stamp work requirements does not necessarily exempt an individual from the employment and training requirements. (Cross Reference 3510)

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 11-01-06 Transmittal: UP-06-30 3512.15 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Work Requirements FS _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Time Limits _______________________________________________________________________________

3512.15 A. Determining the 36 Month Period

1. The 36 month time limit is determined by looking at a fixed 36 month period, as defined by the Department.

Under no circumstances can the Department look back prior to December 1, 1996.

The Department uses the same 36 month period for all individuals subject to the time limit.

An individual begins a new 36 month period when the old period ends.

B. Three Month Time Limit

1. Any individual who is not exempt and who fails to comply with the work requirements can only receive Food Stamp benefits for three full months in each 36 month period.

2. The three full months of Food Stamp assistance received by an individual failing to comply with the work requirements do not have to be consecutive.

C. Regaining Eligibility

1. An individual who is denied eligibility because he or she has received three full months of Food Stamp benefits and has not complied with the work requirement, can become eligible again if, during a thirty day period he or she:

a. works 80 hours or more; or

b. participates in and complies with the requirements of an approved employment and training program for 80 hours or more; or

c. participates and complies with workfare.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 11-01-06 Transmittal: UP-07-04 3512.15 page 2 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Work Requirements FS _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Time Limits _______________________________________________________________________________

3512.15 C. Regaining Eligibility (continued)

An individual who regains eligibility as noted in section 3512.15 C. 1. above, remains eligible as long as he or she works or participates in an approved employment and training program for 80 hours per month, or participates in workfare.

D. One-Time Extension

1. If an individual who regained eligibility loses employment, completes or terminates participation in an approved employment and training activity or an approved workfare program, he or she can remain eligible for up to an additional three consecutive months without working or otherwise meeting the work requirements during the thirty-six month period.

2. The three month extension can only be given if the first three full months of benefits, during which the work requirements were not met, have been exhausted.

3. The three month extension begins on the date the individual first notifies the Department that he or she is no longer meeting the work requirements and extends for three full months after that date.

4. Only one extension is allowed in a thirty-six month period.

P-3512.15 The 36-month period is used to measure if an able-bodied adult without dependents (ABAWD), who is not exempt or meeting the work requirements, has received 3 full months of food stamp assistance in a 36-month period.

The 36-month periods are:

February 1, 2006 to January 31, 2009.

February 1, 2009 to January 31, 2012.

February 1, 2012 to January 31, 2015.

A new 36-month period will begin on the same three-year cycle as indicated in A. above.

Review the case, for the months within the 36-month period, to determine if the ABAWD is:

Exempt from the time limit as specified in section 3512.10; or

Meeting the work requirement, as specified in 3512.05

Each month that the individual is not exempt or meeting the work requirement, counts towards the time limit.

When the individual has received three full countable months of Food Stamps, as determined in D above, discontinue him/her and send the appropriate letter advising that they are no longer eligible for food stamp assistance.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCEPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 5-1-91 Transmittal: UP-91-20 3515.05 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support AABD _______________________________________________________________ MA Subject: Who is Liable for Support _______________________________________________________________________________

3515.05 A. Certain relatives are required by law to provide financial support to the assistance unit.

1. Spouses (AFDC, AABD, MA)

Husbands and wives are legally liable for each other whether they live together or apart.

2. Parents (AFDC, FMA)

Both parents are equally liable for the support of minor children.

a. Mother includes:

(1) natural; or

(2) adoptive;

b. Father includes:

(1) natural;

(2) adoptive;

(3) one whose paternity is established.

B. The applicant or recipient is responsible for supplying accurate and complete information about the legally liable relatives of each member of the assistance unit.

C. When paternity is not established for a minor child, an applicant or recipient is responsible for supplying accurate and complete information about a putative father.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-87 Transmittal: UP-87-2- 3515.05 page 2 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support AABD _______________________________________________________________ MA Subject: Who is Liable for Support _______________________________________________________________________________

3515.05 D. Parents are relieved from the obligation to support minors who are emancipated by either:

1. a court adjudication; or

2. the minor's legal marriage. Dissolution of the marriage does not cancel emancipation.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-93 Transmittal: UP-93-26 P-3515.05 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements PROCEDURES ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support AABD _______________________________________________________________ MA Subject: Initiating Support ______________________________________________________________________________

P-3515.05 Eligibility Worker

1. Explain that signing the application form assigns all rights to support from legally liable relatives of all present and future members of the assistance unit. 2. Describe the function of the Bureau of Child Support Enforcement as the division responsible for all continuing contacts with absent parents of recipient children.

3. When appropriate, describe the function of the Bureau of Child Support Enforcement in establishing paternity and follow steps 4 through 8. Otherwise, skip to step 9.

4. If the individual is an applicant or recipient of Medicaid under the Pregnant Women Under 185% of Poverty or Pregnant Woman Extension coverage groups, inform her that she is not required to cooperate in establishing paternity to be eligible.

5. Further advise the client that she is not required to cooperate in obtaining support from the father of any child born out of wedlock to be eligible. However, continue to accept any voluntary offers of cooperation.

6. Remember, the client is required to cooperate in obtaining support for any other child for whom assistance is requested, including, the absent parent of a minor caretaker relative.

7. If the applicant or recipient described in step 4, above chooses not to cooperate, set an alert for the end of the 59 day period.

8. For determining ongoing eligibility of the mother under other coverage groups following expiration of the 59 day period, go back to step 1 to begin the process for initiating support.

9. Emphasize that cooperation with a DSS worker in regard to support matters is an eligibility requirement.

10. For AFDC explain the obligation to report to the Support Unit support received from an absent parent and the requirement to turn it over to the Support Unit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-93 Transmittal: UP-92-30 P-3515.05 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements PROCEDURES ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support AABD _______________________________________________________________ MA Subject: Initiating Support ______________________________________________________________________________

P-3515.05 Eligibility Worker (continued)

11. For AABD explain that direct support must be reported to the eligibility worker or the Resource worker.

12. Send relative forms W100 and W35 to an assistance unit member's absent spouse who is not a parent of a child in the assistance unit.

13. For every legally liable relative, complete a W348A with the applicant's assistance. Retain a copy in the case record.

° For child support cases, route the original to the Support Unit.

° For absent spouse cases, route the original with a W109 to the Resource Unit.

14. Do not delay granting assistance pending investigation of good cause claims, or because support is being evaluated.

15. Refer to 7520 in the Recovery Section for policy regarding the method and amount of recovery from legally liable relatives' support.

16. Route returned W100's and W35's to the Resource Unit.

17. Notify the Support Unit or the Resource Unit as appropriate when assistance is discontinued.

Resource Worker

1. When a W109 is received indicating an absent spouse, set an alert for the return of the W100 and W35.

2. Contact the relative.

3. Decide the support amount.

4. Either file a voluntary agreement with the court or, in lieu of a voluntary agreement, refer to the Attorney General for court action.

P-3515.07 1. Follow steps 1 through 9 for the EW contained on page P-3515.05.

2. Make a referral to the Bureau of Child Support Enforcement for the collection of medical support regarding an absent parent of any child receiving Medicaid benefits.

3. Do not make a referral for medical support collection if:

a. the child is age 18 or over; or

b. the child is legally emancipated; or

c. the child is institutionalized, but was living with both parents prior to institutionalization; or

d. the child is receiving community-based services and is living with both parents.

4. In situations described in 3c and 3d, make a referral to the Bureau of Child Support Enforcement regarding any parent who was absent from the home prior to the child's institutionalization, or who is currently absent from the home if the child is receiving CBS (Cross reference: 7520.10).

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 3-15-06 Transmittal: UP-06-20 3515.10 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support AABD _______________________________________________________________ MA Subject: Assignment of Rights to Support _______________________________________________________________________________

3515.10 A. As a condition of eligibility, each applicant for AFDC, AABD or MA shall assign to the Department any rights to past, present and future support from legally liable relatives for each member of the assistance unit.

B. Assignment of rights to support applies to all cases in which at least one legally liable relative of an assistance unit member is absent from the home for any reason.

Except as described below, assignment is completed by signature on the application for assistance.

In long-term care cases under the Medicaid program, the assignment of spousal support rights pursuant to section 17b-285 of the general statutes and in undue hardship situations (Cross Reference: 4025.68) is accomplished by a separate assignment other than the assignment described in paragraph A, and is effective only upon receipt by the Department (cross references: 1507.05, 3520.05, 4025.69, 7520.07).

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-93 Transmittal: UP-93-26 P-3515.10 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements PROCEDURES _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support AABD _______________________________________________________________ MA Subject: Establishing Paternity _______________________________________________________________________________

P-3515.10 1. For a child for whom paternity has not been established, explain to the caretaker relative that cooperation in establishing paternity is an eligibility requirement, unless the conditions in step 2 are met.

2. If the individual is an applicant or recipient of Medicaid under the Pregnant Women Under 185% of Poverty or Pregnant Woman Extension coverage groups, inform her that she is not required to cooperate in establishing paternity to be eligible.

3. Further advise the client that she is not required to cooperate in obtaining support from the father of any child born out of wedlock to be eligible. However, continue to accept any voluntary offers of cooperation.

4. If the applicant or recipient described in step 2, above chooses not to cooperate, set an alert for the expiration of the 59 day period.

5. For determining ongoing eligibility of the mother under other coverage groups following expiration of the 59 day period, go back to step 1 to begin the process for establishing paternity.

6. Tell the caretaker what constitutes cooperation (refer to Policy 3515.20) and the consequences of failure to cooperate.

7. Give the caretaker a W595 Good Cause Form and explain good cause.

8. Ask the caretaker to give you as many details as possible about the putative father, including:

° his name;

° his current address, or if his current address is unknown, his last known address;

° his employer and the employer's address.

9. Complete the affirmation portion of the HUM161 when appropriate.

Enter the information on the W348A.

10. Route the W348A to the Support Unit worker who may request additional information and an interview with the caretaker.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-93 Transmittal: UP-92-30 P-3515.10 page 2 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements PROCEDURES _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support AABD _______________________________________________________________ MA Subject: Establishing Paternity _______________________________________________________________________________

P-3515.10 11. If the caretaker does not cooperate and claims good cause, notify the Support Unit to suspend paternity action pending an investigation of the claim. Skip the following steps and proceed to P-3515.15.

12. If good cause is not claimed, and the caretaker has not refused or failed to cooperate, give her 15 days to choose an attorney to represent her in paternity action. Note that failure to choose an attorney is not failure to cooperate.

13. If she has not chosen an attorney at the end of 15 days, refer to the Support Unit to choose one for her.

14. If good cause is not claimed, but the caretaker fails or refuses to cooperate, follow adverse action procedures and determine eligibility and calculate benefits without including the needs of the caretaker relative.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-93 Transmittal: UP-93-26 3515.15 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support AABD _______________________________________________________________ MA Subject: Cooperation in Securing Support _______________________________________________________________________________

3515.15 A. Requirement to Cooperate

An individual who requests assistance from the Department is required to cooperate in securing support from legally liable relatives for all members of the assistance unit, except under the following conditions:

1. when it is determined that there is good cause for failure to do so (cross reference 3515.25); or

2. for purposes of establishing paternity when paternity has not previously been established, when the applicant or recipient receives Medicaid under the Pregnant Women Under 185% of Poverty or Pregnant Woman Extension coverage groups (cross references: 2540.45, 2540.48).

B. Specific Requirements

Cooperation is required in the following areas:

1. identifying and locating all legally liable relatives, and

2. obtaining any of the following when due:

a. support payments;

b. medical or other benefits;

c. property.

C. Demonstration of Cooperation

The individual demonstrates cooperation by the following actions:

1. providing known information and documentary evidence at hand or readily obtainable; and

2. appearing as a witness in court or in any other proceedings related to obtaining support, and providing information or attesting to the lack of information in such proceedings under oath; and

3. transferring to the Department while in receipt of benefits from a money program any direct support payments received after assigning rights to support;

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-93 Transmittal: UP-93-26 3515.15 page 2 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support AABD _______________________________________________________________ MA Subject: Cooperation in Securing Support _______________________________________________________________________________

3515.15 C. Demonstration of Cooperation (continued)

4. entering into a repayment agreement with DSS, Bureau of Child Support Enforcement, for reimbursement of any support payments received and kept after assignment of rights to support;

5. maintaining the payment schedule specified by the terms of a repayment agreement.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCEPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-87 Transmittal: UP-87-2 P-3515.15 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement PROCEDURES _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support AABD _______________________________________________________________ MA Subject: Evaluating Good Cause Claims _______________________________________________________________________________

P-3515.15 1. When good cause for not cooperating is claimed give the caretaker a Good Cause Form.

2. Tell the caretaker what evidence is necessary, help her to gather evidence if she requests help and review the evidence gathered in conjunction with policy.

3. Advise the caretaker that support may be pursued without her cooperation even if good cause is found, if the Department considers there will be no risk to her or the child.

4. Keep a copy in the record of all evidence submitted.

5. Decide whether the good cause claim is valid.

6. If it is valid, evaluate the possibility of the absent parent or putative father inflicting harm on the caretaker or the child if the caretaker does not participate in the Support Unit action.

7. Asks the Support Unit to review:

° the evidence which has been submitted; and

° the reason for your decision; and

° your decision.

8. Get a recommendation from the Support Unit.

9. Make a final decision based on all of the processes in # 5 through #8 above.

10. Notify the caretaker in writing of your decision and the reasons for it.

11. Follow adverse action procedures when appropriate.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-93 Transmittal: UP-93-26 3515.20 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirements POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support FMA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Establishing Paternity _______________________________________________________________________________

3515.20 A. Condition of Eligibility

As a condition of eligibility, an applicant for or recipient of AFDC or FMA must cooperate with the Department to establish the paternity of any child for whom assistance is requested or received when paternity has not previously been established, except under the following conditions:

1. when it is determined that there is good cause for failure to cooperate (cross reference: 3515.25); or

2. when the applicant or recipient receives Medicaid under the Pregnant Women Under 185% of Poverty or Pregnant Women Extension coverage groups (cross references: 2540.45, 2540.48).

B. Specific Requirement

When paternity has not previously been established cooperation with the agency is required to obtain either:

1. voluntary acknowledgment of paternity, or

2. adjudication of paternity by legal action.

C. Cooperation

Cooperation in the legal process is demonstrated by the following actions:

1. documenting the name of the child's father, if known, in an affirmation of paternity signed by the mother; and

2. assisting an attorney in the filing of a petition to establish paternity; and

3. appearing as a witness in court or any other proceedings related to paternity; and

4. providing information or attesting to the lack of information in such proceedings under oath.

P-3515.20 1. Use the following guidelines to determine whether a time limit extension can be granted if documentary evidence necessary for a good cause investigation is not available within policy limits.

2. Extend the time limit of 20 days for the caretaker or 45 days for the Department only for a reason beyond the control of the individual.

3. Accept such reasons as:

° a delay in receiving an answer to a vital request for medical, police or agency records; or

° the unavailability of a critical witness such as an agency worker or medical specialist; or

° serious illness, death or natural disaster affecting any of the concerned individuals.

4. If the 20 days is extended for good cause, add the amount of time granted in the extension to the 45 day limit the Department has to make a decision.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCEPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-87 Transmittal: UP-87-2 3515.25 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support FMA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Good Cause _______________________________________________________________________________

3515.25 A. Claim of Good Cause

An applicant or recipient may claim good cause for not cooperating in either pursuing support or in paternity actions when it is not in the best interests of the individuals involved.

B. Basis for Claims

Circumstances considered sufficient basis for claiming good cause include the following:

1. anticipation of serious physical harm, or emotional harm to:

a. an applicant or recipient; or

b. the caretaker relative of an applicant or recipient child which is of such severity as to interfere with that person's ability to care for the child; or

2. a child for whom support is sought was conceived as a result of incest or rape; or

3. court proceedings for adoption of the child are pending; or

4. a public or private agency has been working with a parent for less than three months in regard to releasing the child for adoption and there is a possibility of physical or emotional harm to the child or the child's caretaker relative.

C. Time Limits

1. A claimant is given an opportunity to establish the claim as follows:

a. The claimant has 20 days in which to substantiate the claim of good cause;

b. An extension may be granted in exceptional cases, when failure to obtain documentation is outside the claimant's control.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF INCOME MAINTENANCE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 1-1-88 Transmittal: UP-88-7 3515.25 page 2 _______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Securing Support FMA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Good Cause _______________________________________________________________________________

3515.25 D. Time Limit (continued)

2. The Department is responsible for acting on the claim as follows:

a. Assistance is not delayed, denied or discontinued pending a decision on the claim;

b. Within 45 days of the claim the Department must issue a decision in writing, unless obtaining documentary evidence is delayed for good reason.

E. Decisions on Claims

1. If the Department denies the claim of good cause the caretaker relative has three options:

a. to cooperate and continue to receive assistance in which case the Department will pursue support through contact with the absent parent, or putative father;

b. to have the entire case discontinued or to withdraw the application rather than have the Department contact the absent parent, or putative father;

c. to be ineligible for AFDC and removed from the assistance unit in the determination of income and asset eligibility and the calculation of benefits. (Cross reference: 5020 for method of payment for remainder of assistance unit).

2. If the Department finds that there is good cause, the Department has two options:

a. to continue to pursue paternity and/or support without the participation of the caretaker, if such action can be taken without risk of harm to the caretaker or child; or

b. to cease paternity and/or support activity.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 3-15-06 Transmittal: UP-06-20 3520.05 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Procedural Eligibility Requirement POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: AFDC Assignment AABD _______________________________________________________________ MA Subject: What Must be Assigned ______________________________________________________________________________

3520.05 There are certain assignments which are conditions of eligibility. Real property is not assignable, but is subject to liens and mortgages. Assignment secures the Department's legal claim. Assignment requirements for each program are as follows:

A. AFDC and AABD

1. In order to qualify for AFDC or AABD the assistance unit shall assign:

a. an interest in a decedent estate;

b. the net proceeds of a cause of action.

2. These assignments are not released until the Department's claim is settled.

B. MA

In Medicaid, except for spousal assignments in long-term care cases that require a separate assignment (Cross Reference: 3515.10), an assignment is made by signing the application for assistance which contains language explaining this assignment. This assignment covers:

1. the rights to payment from medical insurance:

a. of every member of the assistance unit; and

b. from all sources of third party coverage except Medicare; and

2. the net proceeds of causes of action when both:

a. a lawsuit has been instituted to collect damages for injuries sustained in an accident; and

b. the Department has paid medical bills in connection with the accident; and

medical support rights. Medical support rights refer to support in the form of medical coverage or payment for medical expenses (Cross Reference 3515.10).
