body:
CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.05 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Application Process ______________________________________________________________________________ 8520.05 A. Agency Responsibilities The Department gives or mails application materials to anyone who requests assistance on the day that assistance is requested. B. Who Can File an Application--General Principles 1. Any individual regardless of age, sex, or other consideration is allowed to request assistance from the Department and file an application, unless the person has been declared incompetent by a court of competent jurisdiction. 2. A person declared incompetent, as described in 1, above, may have an application filed on his or her behalf by a fiduciary. 3. Applicants may apply for and be granted assistance on their own behalf or, under certain conditions, be represented by other qualified individuals who act responsibly for them. 4. The Department recognizes the right of an applicant to be represented by a responsible individual, but maintains the authority to determine whether or not the person is acting responsibly on behalf of the assistance unit prior to granting assistance. 5. Applicants may be assisted, if so desired, by individuals of their choice in various aspects of the eligibility process. They may be accompanied by such individuals in contact with the Department, and when so accompanied may also be represented by them. C. Filing Application Form 1. All applicants are required to complete an application form. The formal request must be made in writing on the application form. At a minimum, the following information must be presented: a. the full name and address of the applicant; and b. the signature of the applicant, caretaker relative or other individual who is requesting assistance on behalf of the applicant.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.05 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Application Process ______________________________________________________________________________ 8520.05 C. Filing an Application Form (continued) 2. The application may be submitted in person or by mail. 3. Telephone contacts or other requests for aid which are not written or are not made on the prescribed application form are considered inquiries and do not constitute an application. 4. Individuals who appear in person to request assistance must be given an opportunity to file an application for any desired program on the day they personally appear. 5. The Department has designated Regional Offices which serve as contact sites for specific geographical regions of the State. Each Regional Office is responsible for applications made by individuals that reside in the geographic region served by such office. 6. The date of application is considered to be the date that a signed application form is received by any office of the Department. D. Completing the Application Form Applicants who fail to complete the application form within a reasonable time, are denied assistance. E. Interviewing the Applicant 1. A face-to-face interview is required as described below: a. A face-to-face office interview is conducted as a condition of eligibility, unless waived by the Department. b. At the Department's discretion, face-to-face, office interviews are waived by the Department when factors exist which prevent the assistance unit from appearing for an office interview. Such factors may include a client being homebound. c. When the Department waives an office interview, a home interview, telephone interview, or mail interview may be required. If an office interview is waived, alternative methods of contact may be used, as determined by the Department.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.05 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Application Process ______________________________________________________________________________ 8520.05 E. Interviewing the Applicant (continued) 2. Applicants must appear at the appropriate Regional Office, or subdivision of that office which serves their town of residence, to complete the office interview. 3. The purpose of the application interview is to review the application form and any other relevant information or documents for accuracy and completeness and to ascertain pertinent information relating to the current circumstances of the assistance unit. 4. The Department conducts an interview on the same date the application is filed or within a reasonable period of time, as determined by the Department. 5. The Department schedules a second interview only if requested by the applicant. F. Application Processing Standards 1. Prompt Action a. The Department processes applications within a standard period of time as follows: (1) The standard of promptness for applications for an extension made during receipt of TFA during the time limit or an extension is thirty (30) days from the application date, except as described in F. 2, below; (2) The standard of promptness for all other applications of TFA is forty-five (45) days of the application date, except as described in F. 2, below. b. The first day of the processing begins on the day following the date of application. 2. Use of the Standard of Promptness a. The Department determines eligibility within the standard of promptness unless verification needed to establish eligibility is delayed due to the action or inaction of the client and there was good cause for the client’s delay in supplying the requested verification. CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 3-1-06 Transmittal: UP-06-07 8520.05 page 4 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Application Process ______________________________________________________________________________ 8520.05 F. 2. Use of the Standard of Promptness (continued) b. An assistance unit may request a Fair Hearing if the Department exceeds the standard of promptness. If it has been determined that the Department has exceeded the standard of promptness, it will be directed to take prompt action to determine eligibility. Assistance units are not automatically determined to be eligible based solely on the Department's failure to determine eligibility within the standard of promptness. G. Eligibility Determinations 1. The Department determines eligibility when enough information has been supplied by the assistance unit to allow the Department to make a judgment regarding eligibility. 2. A Fraud Early Detection (FRED) investigation is done on TFA applications that meet an error prone profile. Conditions that would cause a case to meet this profile include, but are not limited to: a. a previous fraud overpayment; b. children under the age of six; c. the household is suspected of living above its means; d. the case was denied or closed within three months; e. application is inconsistent with prior case history; f. questionable absent parent information; g. no income for two consecutive months; h. questionable verification;

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 3-1-00 Transmittal: UP-00-2 8520.05 page 5 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Application Process ______________________________________________________________________________ 8520.05 G. Eligibility Determinations (cont.) 2. i. living in Connecticut for less than three months; j. household composition appears different than reported; k. assets appear to be greater than reported. 3. The Department may require verification and information from assistance units within designated time periods necessary to process the application within the standard of promptness. 4. When an applicant does not provide required verification without good cause by the designated date, described in 2, above, a penalty is imposed as described at 8520.40. 5. Except when an applicant has good cause for the delay, verification received after the date that an incomplete application is processed: a. is used only with respect to future case actions; and b. is not used retroactively to change an action that was correctly taken based on the information that was available to the Department at that time. Eligibility determinations are not delayed pending confirmation of Social Security numbers unless there is a discrepancy between a Social Security number given for an assistance unit member and information from a source used by the Department which raises a question of identity.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 3-1-06 Transmittal: UP-06-07 8520.05 page 6 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Application Process ______________________________________________________________________________ 8520.05 G. Eligibility Determinations (continued) Within the eligibility processing standards, as described in F, above, eligibility determinations are not made until the Department has determined whether or not the applicant has cooperated in securing child support as described in 8540.65. 8. Eligibility determinations are not delayed beyond the standard of promptness pending the attendance at the Jobs First Employment Services (JFES) assessment interview and participation in the development of the employment services plan if the department failed to schedule an appointment for the JFES assessment interview by the tenth business day after the application for TFA. (cross reference 8520.05 F) H. Good Cause Good cause is considered to exist when circumstances beyond the control of the client reasonably prevent him or her from complying with a Department requirement.

body:
CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.10 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Redetermination Process ______________________________________________________________________________ 8520.10 A. General Requirements 1. In order to assure continuous participation, the Department processes redeterminations with reasonable promptness. 2. Redeterminations may be conducted on either a regularly scheduled basis or conducted on an unscheduled basis because of known, questionable, or anticipated changes in assistance unit circumstances, as long as the assistance unit is given reasonable advance notice as determined by the Department. 3. In general, eligibility is redetermined through the same methods by which eligibility is initially determined at the time of application. 4. At the Department's discretion, redeterminations may be changed from an in office, face-to-face interview to a redetermination done by mail or home visit. When determining whether to change the redetermination to a mail or a home visit review, the Department takes into consideration factors that will prevent a person from attending an in-office interview. Such factors include a client being homebound and to the extent possible, the work schedule of the client. 5. The Department does not schedule a second redetermination interview if an applicant fails to appear for the interview and fails to contact the Department to reschedule. Failure to appear for the interview and call the office results in discontinuance of TFA benefits. 6. TFA benefits are continued until the redetermination is processed if the assistance unit has caused a delay in processing the redetermination and has good cause for failure to timely complete the redetermination. This provision does not apply to exit interviews. 7. TFA benefits are continued until the redetermination is processed if the Department has been unable to process the redetermination by the end of the redetermination period. This provision does not apply to exit interviews. 8. Good cause exists when, in the opinion of the Department, circumstances beyond the control of the client reasonably prevents him or her from complying with a Department requirement.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.10 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Redetermination Process ______________________________________________________________________________ 8520.10 B. Who Can File a Redetermination The rules regarding individuals qualified to complete the redetermination are the same as those established for making an application. (cross reference: 8520.05). C. Redetermination Forms 1. Assistance units are required to complete a redetermination form at each redetermination. 2. Assistance units that do not complete the redetermination form within the specified time limits without good cause, may be subject to discontinuance or an interruption in benefits. 3. The redetermination form must be signed by someone qualified to complete the redetermination on behalf of the assistance unit. 4. The redetermination form must contain a legible name and address. D. Types of Redeterminations Different types of redeterminations are conducted for different reasons and have different requirements. When two different types of redeterminations become due in the same month, the Department consolidates them into one. The different types of redeterminations and their specific requirements are listed below: 1. The Six (6) Month Counter Review a. The Six Month Counter Review is held only for time limited assistance units at the end of six months of time limited assistance. b. The Six (6) Month Counter Review is conducted for time limited assistance units when at least one (1) mandatory Employment Services participant in the assistance unit meets both of the following criteria at the end of six (6) months of time limited assistance: (1) is not taking part in a structured Employment Services activity as specified in his or her Employment Plan; and (2) has not become employed.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.10 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Redetermination Process ______________________________________________________________________________ 8520.10 D. 1. The Six (6) month Counter Review (continued) c. The Six (6) Month Counter Review requires an in office, face-to-face interview. d. The Six (6) Month Counter Review is mandatory for assistance units described in a, above. If the assistance unit does not complete a Six (6) Month Counter Review without good cause, the entire assistance unit is discontinued. e. The Work Test is administered at the Six (6) Month Counter Review for any recipient who has been in Self-Directed Job Search, who did not already pass a Work Test. (cross reference: 8530.25) 2. The Periodic Income Review a. The Periodic Income Review is held based on actual months of receipt of TFA benefits without regard to whether the assistance unit is subject to the time limit or exempt. b. Periodic Income Reviews may be conducted every six (6) calendar months for both assistance units subject to and those exempt from the time limit. Periodic Income Reviews may be conducted simultaneously with any other scheduled redetermination. c. The purpose of the Periodic Income Review is to gather information about the assistance unit's income, to emphasize the importance of employment, update the case file, and to make any necessary changes regarding eligibility. d. The Periodic Income Review is mandatory. If the assistance unit does not complete a Periodic Income Review without good cause, the entire assistance unit is discontinued. The Periodic Income Review may require either an in office interview, or the completion of a review form through the mail, at the discretion of the Department.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8520.10 page 4 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Redetermination Process ______________________________________________________________________________ 8520.10 D. 3. The Twelve (12) Month Redetermination a. The Twelve (12) Month Redetermination is conducted every twelve (12) calendar months for both assistance units subject to and those exempt from the time limit. b. The Twelve (12) Month Redetermination requires an in office, face-to-face interview. c. The purpose of the Twelve (12) Month Redetermination is to determine the assistance unit's ongoing eligibility for assistance, gather information about the assistance unit, review employment efforts of mandatory Employment Services participants, review the exemption status of assistance units which are considered exempt from the time limit, and to update the case file. d. The Twelve (12) Month redetermination is mandatory. If the assistance unit does not complete a Twelve Month Redetermination without good cause, the entire assistance unit is discontinued. 4. Exit Interviews at the end of Twenty-One Months and Extensions a. An exit interview is scheduled for all time limited assistance units in the twentieth month of the twenty-one month time limit and the fifth month of an extension period. This exit interview is mandatory. If the assistance unit does not complete an exit interview without good cause, the entire assistance unit is discontinued at the end of the twenty-one month time limit or extension. The exit interview requires the appearance of the caretaker relative for an in-office, face-to-face interview. The purpose of this exit interview is to inform the assistance unit of services that may continue to be available to the family. This includes, but is not limited to, benefits that may be available through the Department, as well as information and referrals to Safety Net Services, the Transitionary Rental Assistance Program, the Earned Income Tax Credit, rental subsidies, emergency housing, employment services, and energy assistance programs.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8520.10 page 5 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Redetermination Process ______________________________________________________________________________ 8520.10 D. 4. Exit Interviews at the end of Twenty-One Months and Extensions A redetermination of Food Stamps and Medicaid program eligibility may also be conducted at the exit interview when appropriate. However, if the client does not appear for the exit interview, Medicaid eligibility may be redetermined through the mail or by an ex parte review. (cross reference: 1545) Assistance units that appear for an exit interview are given an opportunity to apply for an extension of benefits. Exit Interviews at the End of the Sixty Month Time Limit a. An exit interview is scheduled for all time limited assistance units in the fifty-eighth month of the sixty month time limit. b. This exit interview is not mandatory. The client may refuse to take part. However, the Department makes every effort to contact the client to conduct the exit interview. c. The exit interview is conducted through a face-to-face interview with the caretaker relative. The interview may be conducted in the office or at the client’s home. The purpose of this exit interview is to inform the assistance unit of services that may continue to be available to the family. These include, but are not limited to, benefits that may be available through the Department, as well as information and referrals to the Transitionary Rental Assistance Program, the Earned Income Tax Credit, rental subsidies, emergency housing, employment services, and energy assistance programs. Exemptions and exceptions to the time limit are also explained and the client is given an opportunity to apply for an exemption or exception as appropriate.

body:
CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-01-16 P-8520.10 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First PROCEDURES ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _____________________________________________________ Subject: Completing the Sixty-Month Exit Interview ______________________________________________________________________________ P-8520.10 1. Identify cases approaching month fifty-eight. Use the approved standard letter to schedule the appointment for the exit interview. Send the appointment letter at least ten days before the scheduled appointment. Send the standard reminder letter (L079, L080) five days before the scheduled appointment. Place a telephone call one working day before the interview appointment to remind the participant of his or her appointment. If the client appears, conduct interview. Use form W-1081 as a guide and checklist to ensure that you cover all the appropriate areas: explain the purpose of the interview and; explain that the participant is reaching sixty months of TFA eligibility and cannot continue to receive benefits without an exemption or hardship (if the participant disagrees with the counter, review the case file to ensure that the case has been coded correctly so that the counter is correct) and; review extension criteria and have the client sign a form W-1084 and; redetermine eligibility for any other programs that may be due for review and; inform the participant of programs and services for which he or she may be eligible and; complete the checklist and have the participant sign and date it and; provide the participant with any appropriate referrals and the resource information packet. If the client does not appear, send a second appointment letter (L085, L086). Send the letter no later than the end of month fifty-nine. Schedule the appointment no later than the beginning of month sixty. If the client responds to the appointment letter and informs the Department that he or she does not wish to come to the appointment, the worker should note this in the case narrative on EMS. No further follow up is necessary. Place a reminder call one working day before the interview appointment. If the client appears, complete the review as directed in step six (6).

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-01-16 P-8520.10 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First PROCEDURES ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _____________________________________________________ Subject: Completing the Sixty Month Exit Interview ______________________________________________________________________________ P-8520.10 10. If the client does not appear for the second appointment, send a home visit appointment letter (L081, L082). Whenever possible, a FIRep and Social Worker should conduct the visit together. Place a reminder call one working day before the home visit appointment. If the client is at home at the time of the visit, complete the interview as directed in step six (6) as long as the client agrees and the FIRep and Social Worker feel that the environment is conducive to interviewing. Otherwise, schedule an in-office appointment with the client. Also explore the following: the reasons that the client has not attended previous appointments; determining the existence of barriers or hardship. If the client is not at home or does not answer the door, leave the information packet as close to the door as possible. Document the EMS narrative on the following points: date and time of visit; whether or not client was home; content of the interview relative to reasons the client did not appear for first two interviews; barriers that exist for the client and his or her family; any other information that the client shares regarding eligibility; the need, if any, for a follow up appointment.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.15 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Authorized Representative ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.15 A. General Requirements

1. In accordance with the following provisions, an assistance unit may be represented in various aspects of the eligibility process by a responsible individual who has been authorized to act as the assistance unit's representative:

a. The Department may determine that an authorized representative is needed to act as protective payee when financial mismanagement has been determined. (cross reference: 8570.10)

b. A minor parent who is required to live with an adult relative or in an adult-supervised supportive living arrangement must have an authorized representative, unless the minor parent is living with a parent. (cross reference 8540.35)

c. An authorized representative may be appointed when the applicant or recipient is unable or incapable of acting on his or her own behalf.

2. The Department must approve the need for an authorized representative.

3. The Department may limit the duties of an authorized representative.

4. An authorized representative must be designated in writing by the caretaker relative of the dependent child unless the caretaker relative is a minor parent. In the case of minor parents, the Department designates the authorized representative.

5. An assistance unit is limited to one authorized representative at a time.

6. There is no limit to the number of assistance units that an authorized representative may represent.

7. The appointment of an authorized representative does not relieve the assistance unit of any responsibilities. Both the assistance unit and the representative may be held responsible for assistance improperly obtained through action by the authorized representative.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.15 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Authorized Representative ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.15 A. General Requirements (continued)

8. Except for minor parents, an assistance unit may withdraw its authorization at any time through a written statement.

9. Minor parents may request that the Department remove or change their authorized representative. The Department makes the final determination on such a request when made by a minor parent.

10. The Department retains the right to determine who may be an authorized representative.

B. Who Can Be an Authorized Representative

1. In order to be an authorized representative a person must be a responsible individual who is eighteen years of age or older and sufficiently familiar with the circumstances of the assistance unit.

2. Employees of the Department involved in the eligibility process or issuance of benefits may not act as authorized representatives without the specific written approval of the Commissioner or the Commissioner's designee.

3. Those who have been disqualified from TFA are not allowed to be authorized representatives.

C. Role of the Authorized Representative

The authorized representative's duties are limited and must be designated in accordance with the following:

1. An authorized representative designated by the Department when financial mismanagement has been determined, acts as protective payee as described at 8570.25.

2. An authorized representative named by the Department for a minor parent, acts on behalf of the minor parent in the eligibility process as described in this chapter and as protective payee as described at 8570.20.

3. An authorized representative for a person unable or incapable of acting on his or her own behalf, may perform only the duties allowed by the Department and designated by the assistance unit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.15 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Authorized Representative ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.15 D. Agency Requirements

1. The Department does not take action based on information provided by an authorized representative until the authorized representative provides verification of his or her identity.

2. Except in the case of minor parents, whenever possible, the Department requires the head of the assistance unit, caretaker relative, custodian or court appointed fiduciary to review the actions of the authorized representative.

3. The Department conducts home visits, makes collateral contacts or uses other means at its disposal to confirm actions of an authorized representative if the appropriateness of the action is questionable or requires further exploration.

E. Signature on Documents

1. Appointment of an authorized representative does not relieve the applicant, or where appropriate his or her caretaker relative, custodian or court appointed fiduciary, from the responsibility of signing documents related to the eligibility process.

2. The authorized representatives are required to sign documents prepared by them or in their presence on behalf of the applicant. However, the application is not complete until the signature of the applicant, caretaker relative, custodian or court appointed fiduciary is obtained.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.20 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Interim Activity ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.20 A. What must be reported

1. Assistance units are required to report any changes which may affect eligibility, benefit level, time limited status, or other program requirements to the Department.

2. Special requirements related to employment are as follows:

a. assistance units must report all new employment;

b. assistance units must report changes of earnings when the total family earnings reach or exceed the Federal Poverty Level corresponding to the assistance unit's size;

c. assistance units must report termination of employment;

d. changes of earned income or other information about employment must be reported by the assistance unit if requested by the Department.

B. When changes must be reported

1. Except when it becomes known that a child will be absent from the home for more than ninety (90) days, assistance units are required to report changes within ten calendar days of the date of the change unless there is good cause.

2. If a child is absent from the home for more than ninety (90) days, the parent or caretaker relative of the assistance unit must notify the Department within five (5) days from the date it became clear that the child would be absent for more than ninety days. (cross reference 8540.30)

C. How changes must be reported

1. When assistance units are requesting the addition to the unit of a non-mandatory member, the request must be made in writing. All other changes may be reported in person, in writing, or by telephone.

2. An assistance unit is considered to have reported a change on the day that any office of the Department receives notification of the change.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.20 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Interim Activity ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.20 D. Processing Changes

The Department acts promptly to determine the effect on eligibility or benefit level whenever changes become known to the Department.

E. Effective Date of Change

Specific requirements for the inclusion or deletion of assistance unit members are established in the subject of this chapter dealing with beginning and ending dates. (cross reference: 8520.30, 8520.35)

1. Changes Resulting in Ineligibility or a Decrease in Assistance

a. If the change was reported timely, the change affects benefits beginning with the month following the month in which the ten day advance notice period ends.

b. If the change was not reported timely, the change affects entitlement to, or the amount of benefits beginning with the month following the month the ten day notice period would have ended if the change was reported timely. Any benefits paid incorrectly as a result of client delay in reporting are subject to recoupment as described at 8580.

c. No overpayment exists when changes are reported and acted upon in a timely fashion in accordance with this policy.

d. An overpayment does result if a change is reported in a timely manner to the Department, but is not acted upon in a timely manner by the Department. Such overpayments are subject to recoupment as described at 8580.

2. Changes Resulting in Increased Benefits

a. Changes that result in an upward adjustment of benefits are made in the month the change occurs, provided that the change is reported in a timely manner and also verified within agency standards, or good cause is established if the change was not timely reported or verified within agency standards.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.20 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Interim Activity ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.20 E. 2. Changes Resulting in Increased Benefits (continued)

b. Changes reported or verified in an untimely manner result in an upward adjustment of benefits as described below if good cause is not established:

(1) effective the reporting month if verification is provided within agency standards; or

(2) effective the month of verification if the verification is not provided within agency standards.

c. Changes in basic or special needs reported later than the month following the month that the need is incurred are not considered in the total need determination until the month the change is reported.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.25 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Cooperation with Quality Control Reviews ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.25 A. General Requirement

As a condition of eligibility, members of the assistance unit are required to cooperate with Quality Control reviews.

B. Specific Review Process Requirements

At any Quality Control review, members of the assistance unit must cooperate unless there is good cause for non-cooperation by:

1. completing and signing any necessary review forms; and

2. responding to a scheduled appointment for an interview; and

3. reporting changes and verifying information as required.

C. Penalties

1. The entire assistance unit is ineligible when a member of the assistance unit does not cooperate with the Quality Review process and does not have good cause for not cooperating.

2. Ineligibility continues until the individual cooperates or until 95 days after the end of the annual review period, whichever is first. The Quality Control annual review period is the twelve month period from October 1 through the following September 30.

3. If the household reapplies after the 95 day period, the previous noncooperation cannot be used as a factor of eligibility.

D. Good Cause

Good cause is considered to exist when circumstances beyond the individual's control reasonably prevent him or her from complying with Quality Control.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.30 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Beginning Dates of Eligibility ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.30 A. Beginning Dates for Assistance Units

The beginning date of eligibility is the date the Department receives a signed application, or the date all eligibility factors are met, whichever is later, as follows:

1. The date the application is received is used as the beginning date of eligibility when:

a. financial eligibility exists for the month of application; and

b. the following non-financial eligibility requirements are met during the application process:

(1) the caretaker relative does not supply the Social Security numbers of all assistance unit members as required by 8540.60; and

(2) the assistance unit cooperates in securing support from an absent parent as required by 8540.65; and

(3) the assistance unit cooperates with the digital imaging process as required at 8540.70; and

c. all other non-financial requirements are met as of the application date.

2. The date all eligibility factors are met is used as the beginning date of eligibility when:

a. the assistance unit has excess assets at the time of application, but the amount is reduced to within eligibility standard levels during the application process in accordance with policy; or

b. a non-financial eligibility requirement other than those listed at A. 1. b, above, is met at a later date during the application process.

3. The first day of the month following application is used as the beginning date of eligibility when:

a. income eligibility does not exist in the month of application; and

b. income eligibility does exist in the month following application; and

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.30 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Beginning Dates of Eligibility ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.30 A. 3. Beginning Dates for Assistance Units (continued)

c. all other eligibility requirements are met.

B. Beginning Dates for Additions to the Assistance Unit

1. For a new member whose addition to the household is reported within ten (10) days of the individual's arrival, the beginning date of eligibility is as follows:

a. the date of the report, if all non-financial eligibility requirements are met on the date or within other deadlines set by the Department; or

b. the date on which all non-financial requirements are met if eligibility does not exist on the date of the report, or within other deadlines set by the Department.

2. For a new member whose presence is not reported within ten (10) days of arrival in the household, the beginning date of eligibility for the new member is the date that all eligibility requirements are met, but not earlier than the date of report, unless good cause exists for not reporting timely.

body:
CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.40 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA Subject: Verification 8520.40 A. Assistance Unit Responsibilities 1. The verification of information pertinent to an eligibility determination or calculation of benefits is the responsibility of the assistance unit. 2. The assistance unit may submit any evidence which it believes will support the factor of eligibility which is subject to verification. B. Department Responsibilities 1. The Department assists in obtaining verification on behalf of the assistance unit when one of the following conditions exist: a. The Department has the internal capability of obtaining the verification needed through such means as case files, microfiche records, or direct access to other official records; or b. The Department has the capability to obtain the verification needed without undue administrative hardship, and the assistance unit has been unable to obtain the needed verification after making a bona fide effort, and the assistance unit has requested help; or c. The evidence necessary can only be obtained by payment of a fee, and the Department is able to obtain the evidence. 2. The Department considers all evidence submitted by the assistance unit or received from other sources. C. Verification Standard A statement made by an applicant or a recipient is considered by the Department to be verified when the available evidence indicates that it is more likely to be true than not.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.40 page 2 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA Subject: Verification 8520.40 D. Verification Requirements 1. The Department requires verification of information when specifically required by federal or State law or regulations, or when the Department considers it necessary to corroborate an assistance unit's statements pertaining to an essential factor of eligibility. 2. The Department does not require applicants or recipients to provide documentary evidence to verify the nonexistence of any factor. E. Penalties The penalty for failure to provide required verification depends upon the nature of the factor or circumstance for which verification is required. 1. If the eligibility of the assistance unit depends directly upon a factor or circumstance for which verification is required, not providing verification results in ineligibility for the assistance unit, unless there is good cause for not providing the verification. 2. If the eligibility of an individual assistance unit member depends directly upon a factor or circumstance for which verification is required, not providing verification results in ineligibility for that individual member, unless there is good cause for not providing the verification. 3. If the eligibility of the assistance unit does not depend directly on a factor or circumstance for which verification is required, but the benefit level could be affected by it, not providing verification results in non-consideration of the factor or circumstance, unless there is good cause for not providing the verification. 4. Ineligibility of the assistance unit may result indirectly from failure to provide verification of a factor or circumstance described in 2, above, if the factor or circumstance leads to ineligibility of the unit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.40 page 3 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA Subject: Verification 8520.40 F. Methods of Verification 1. The Department determines the adequacy and appropriateness of the method of verification. 2. Documents are the primary sources of verification whenever such evidence can be acquired. 3. In the absence of available documentary evidence, the Department verifies information through contacts with persons who are not members of the assistance unit and are approved by the Department. 4. Home visits are made to facilitate verification when the Department regards it as necessary to determine eligibility or calculate benefits and the unit agrees to being interviewed at home. 5. In addition to other methods of verification, the Department also uses the Income Eligibility Verification System (IEVS) to obtain and utilize information on income. a. IEVS is used for assistance unit members or individuals whose income or assets are counted in determining eligibility or benefit amount. b. All information obtained through IEVS is verified whenever the information is not being obtained from its primary source. 6. a. The Department uses the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlement (SAVE) system to obtain information from the Immigration and Naturalization Service regarding the status of all individuals who are not citizens, except those ineligible aliens applying for emergency medical treatment. b. In addition to the initial process, aliens with temporary or conditional status will be subject to SAVE when their temporary status expires, and until permanent status is granted by INS.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL Date: 7-1-04 Transmittal: UP-04-14 8520.40 page 4 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA Subject: Verification 8520.40 F. Methods of Verification (continued) 7. Affidavits are accepted for review by the Department. When an affidavit is reviewed by the Department, it is evaluated along with all other evidence relative to the eligibility factor. The Department considers all the available evidence, including the affidavit and the reasonableness of the explanation as to why documentary verification is not available, to determine whether it is more likely than not that the eligibility factor has been established. The Department generally expects documentary verification to be provided when documents are customarily available for that purpose unless a satisfactory explanation is provided as to why the documents are not available. G. Verification of Domestic Violence The verification standard for a report of domestic violence is as follows: 1. The Department accepts a signed sworn statement by the client as verification of domestic violence when a member of a time limited assistance unit makes a credible report of domestic violence at any time prior to the twenty month exit interview. Also, the Department accepts a signed sworn statement by the client as verification of domestic violence any time a member of an assistance unit that is exempt from the time limit makes a credible report of domestic violence. 2. If a member of a time limited assistance unit makes a credible report of domestic violence at the twenty month exit interview or any time thereafter, the Department requires a signed sworn statement from the member and at least one additional corroborating statement from any credible source including, but not limited to, a friend, neighbor, relative, or an established organization which deals with issues of domestic violence. 3. When the Department has a reasonable basis to find that the applicant or recipient's report of domestic violence is not credible, the Department requires a signed sworn statement by the applicant or recipient and one corroborating piece of evidence from an organization which normally deals with issues of domestic violence. Such evidence includes, but is not limited to, police reports, government agency or court records, or documentation from a member of the clergy, a shelter worker, or a legal, medical or other professional from whom the person has sought assistance in dealing with domestic violence.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.45 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Notice Requirements ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.45 A. General Notice Requirements

1. Assistance units are provided with a written notice of eligibility as follows:

a. at the time that assistance is granted or denied; and

b. to schedule a redetermination and upon the completion of a redetermination; and

c. whenever a change is made that affects eligibility or benefit level, including a mass modification of all or a portion of the general caseload.

2. Generally, notices contain information about benefits, eligibility, program requirements, and appeal rights to the assistance unit.

3. A member of an assistance unit who alleges to be a past or present victim of domestic violence, or who alleges to be at risk of further domestic violence is notified of the available community services which assist victims of domestic violence and how to voluntarily and confidentially access these services.

4. A member of an assistance unit who alleges to be a victim of domestic violence, or who alleges to be at risk of further domestic violence is confidentially notified of the following:

a. the Department's determination of whether or not he or she has been denied good cause for not complying with an Employment Services requirement when the denial is related to his or her claim of victim status; and

b. the Department's determination of whether or not he or she is exempt from child support requirements when the decision on exemption is based on his or her claim of victim status and fear of reprisal; and

c. the Department's determination of whether or not he or she has been denied an extension of benefits when the denial is related to his or her claim of victim status.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.45 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Notice Requirements ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.45 A. General Notice Requirements (continued)

5. The Department notifies the assistance unit that when the assistance unit receives benefits, the Department will provide law enforcement officials upon their request, the address of assistance unit members in accordance with the requirements found in 8510.20.

B. Adverse Action Notice Requirements

Assistance units are provided with notice of adverse action when a change in assistance unit circumstances results in denial, discontinuance, termination, suspension, or a reduction in benefits.

C. Timely Notice Requirements

The Department mails or sends adverse action notice at least ten days prior to the date of the intended adverse action, except as listed in D, below.

D. Exceptions to Timely Notice Requirements

The Department mails a notice no later than the date of the action if the action is based on any of the following circumstances:

1. when the Department has factual information that all members of the assistance unit have died; or

2. when the Department has factual information that an assistance unit member has died, or that the caretaker relative has died and there is no relative available to serve as the caretaker relative; or

3. when the Department receives a clear, written statement signed by the assistance unit stating that:

a. the assistance unit no longer wishes to receive benefits; or

b. the assistance unit is giving the Department information which requires that the Department terminate or reduce benefits, and that the assistance unit understands that this must be the result of supplying that information; or

4. when the affected individual has been admitted to or committed to an institution, and the individual is not eligible for assistance while living there; or

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8520.45 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Eligibility Process TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Notice Requirements ______________________________________________________________________________

8520.45 D. Exceptions to Timely Notice Requirements (continued)

5. the assistance unit's whereabouts are unknown and the post office returns Departmental mail directed to the assistance unit indicating no forwarding address; or

6. when the Department verifies that the assistance unit has been granted benefits under a similar program in another state; or

7. when a child in receipt of financial assistance is removed from the home as a result of a judicial determination, or voluntarily placed in foster care by his or her caretaker relative or legal guardian; or

8. when the Department grants the assistance unit a benefit for a specific period of time and informs the unit in writing at the time of grant that the benefit automatically terminates when the specific period ends; or

9. when the Department determines that the payee has mismanaged the unit's finances and that the Department should issue a restricted method of payment (cross reference: 8570); or

10. when benefits are reduced due to child support payments being passed through directly to the assistance unit; or

11. when an application for benefits is denied.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8525.05 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: TFA Fair Hearings ES ___________________________________________________________________________ Subject: General Provisions ______________________________________________________________________________

8525.05 A. Basic Provisions

Administrative Fair Hearings are conducted by the Department in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 54 of the Connecticut General Statutes and the Department's rules of practice, Regulations of Connecticut Agencies (Social Services) Section 17-311-11 through 17-311-40, as supplemented by the procedural rules stated in this chapter which apply specifically to the Temporary Family Assistance and Employment Services programs.

B. Right to a Fair Hearing

Subject to the conditions described in this chapter, the requester has the right to a Fair Hearing if:

1. the Department denies the assistance unit's application for benefits; or

2. the Department does not take action on the assistance unit's application within the time limits specified in Section 8520.05, without good cause; or

3. the requester alleges that the Department has either failed to take a required action or has taken an erroneous action. Such actions may include:

a. denying, suspending, reducing, discontinuing, or terminating benefits; or

b. imposing conditions upon eligibility; or

c. issuing benefits in an incorrect manner; or

d. taking any other action adversely affecting the receipt of benefits, such as an incorrect computation of the amount of benefits; or

e. erroneously counting time limited months of eligibility; or

4. the requester claims to be a victim of domestic violence who was incorrectly denied a good cause exception for not complying with a program requirement; or

5. the requester claims that the Department failed to adhere to random assignment assignment procedures and as a result the assistance unit was incorrectly assigned to either Jobs First or the control group; or

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8525.05 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: TFA Fair Hearings ES ___________________________________________________________________________ Subject: General Provisions ______________________________________________________________________________

8525.05 B. Right to a Fair Hearing (continued)

6. the Department determines that a recipient has failed the Work Test, which may affect eligibility for extensions; or

7. the Department determines that an applicant or recipient is mandatory for Employment Services requirements or mandatory for the time limited program and the requester disagrees with the determination.

8. the Department rules that an individual has not successfully complied with the requirements of an Individual Performance Contract. (cross reference: 8540.05)

C. Who Can Request a Fair Hearing

Any member of the assistance unit, as well as the unit's authorized representative, or conservator of a unit member, has the right to request a Fair Hearing on behalf of the assistance unit.

D. Informing the Assistance Unit

At the time of the Department's action granting, denying or modifying an application for assistance and at the time of subsequent adverse actions affecting the assistance unit's benefits, the Department informs the assistance unit, in writing, of the following:

1. the unit may request a Fair Hearing; and

2. the method by which the assistance unit obtains a Fair Hearing; and

3. that the assistance unit may represent themselves, may use legal counsel, a relative, friend, or other spokesperson; and

4. the availability of Legal Aid services and the toll free telephone number of Statewide Legal Services.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8525.05 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: TFA Fair Hearings ES ____________________________________________________________________________ Subject: General Provisions ______________________________________________________________________________

8525.05 E. Time Limits for Requesting a Fair Hearing

1. The request for a Fair Hearing must be made within sixty (60) days from the date that the Department mails its notice of action.

2. Subject to the conditions described in this chapter and stated at 8520, the requester has ten (10) days from the date the Department mails a notice of action to request a Fair Hearing in order to prevent termination or reduction of benefits before the Fair Hearing decision is rendered.

3. If the dispute involves a delay in action on an application, the assistance unit has the right to request a Fair Hearing as of the date the action becomes overdue and there is not good cause for the delay. The requester's right to a Fair Hearing is only valid sixty (60) days from the date the Department mails a notice to the client indicating that the delay in processing is without good cause. (cross reference: 8520.05)

4. If the dispute involves a delay or refusal to make a requested change in benefits, the requester has the right to request a Fair Hearing as of the date the change should have been made. The requester's right to request a Fair Hearing is only valid sixty (60) days from the date the Department fails to make the requested change. (cross references: 8520.10 and 8520.20)

F. Request for a Hearing

The request for a Fair Hearing must be in writing and contain a statement as to the reason for the request.

G. Scheduling

The Department schedules the Fair Hearing to be held:

1. during Department business hours; and

2. within thirty (30) days from the date the request was received; and

3. for emergency housing issues, within three (3) business days from the date the request is received.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _____________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8525.05 page 4 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: TFA Fair Hearings ES ___________________________________________________________________________ Subject: General Provisions ______________________________________________________________________________

8525.05 H. Attendance at Fair Hearing

1. If client confidentiality requirements are implicated, and client confidentiality is not waived, the attendance at Fair Hearings is restricted to:

a. the Fair Hearing Official;

b. the representative from the Department;

c. the assistance unit member and/or conservator if the requester is incapable of representing himself or herself;

d. witnesses;

e. others required or permitted by the Hearing official.

2. Witnesses called by a party may have their attendance at the hearing restricted by the Fair Hearing Official to the extent necessary to maintain confidentiality and/or ensure that his testimony is not tainted by attendance at the hearing.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _____________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8525.07 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: TFA Fair Hearings ES ______________________________________________________________________________ Subject: Limitations to Scope of Hearings ______________________________________________________________________________

8525.07 A. Limits on the Scope of Hearings at the End of Twenty One (21) Months

The only claims that can be raised in a Fair Hearing held as a result of the Department's proposed termination of benefits at the end of the twenty-one (21) month period are claims that are relevant and pertinent to that proposed action, including whether the Department properly calculated the expiration of the twenty-one (21) month limit and whether the assistance unit should have been considered to be exempt from the time limit. The claim that the Department may have erred in denying an application for an extension of benefits may not be raised in a Fair Hearing requested, and held in response to notice being issued of the Department's determination to terminate benefits as a result of expiration of the twenty-one (21) month limit. (cross reference 8540.05)

B. Limits on the Scope of Hearings When an Extension is Denied

Only claims that are pertinent to the determination of whether the Department may have erred in denying an application for an extension of benefits may be raised in a Fair Hearing on that issue. The assistance unit cannot raise claims that are only relevant to the discontinuance of benefits upon the expiration of the twenty-one (21) month time limit in a Fair Hearing that is held in order to allow the assistance unit an opportunity to contest the denial of an application for an extension. (cross reference: 8540.10)

C. Consolidated Hearings

Notwithstanding the provisions of A, and B, above, a Fair Hearing Official may decide to hold a consolidated hearing on both the issue of the termination of benefits due to the expiration of time-limited benefits and a denial of an application for an extension. Both issues, however, are treated as separate and discrete appeals that are taken from separate and distinct eligibility determinations, notice of which is provided by separate and distinct notices of action.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8525.10 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Fair Hearings TFA ES _______________________________________________________________________ Subject: Continuing Benefits Pending Fair Hearing _______________________________________________________________________________ 8525.10 A. Decision 1. The Department continues the assistance unit's benefits at the level existing immediately preceding the Fair Hearing request until the Fair Hearing decision is reached if the unit requests a Fair Hearing within ten (10) days from the mailing date of the notice of adverse action as described in 8520.45, unless the situation is covered by the exceptions to continuation of benefits described in B. below. 2. Unless the assistance unit specifically waives its right to a continuation of benefits, the Department assumes that the unit's request for a Fair Hearing within the ten (10) day period, described in 1. above, is a request that the unit's benefits remain the same pending the Fair Hearing decision. 3. If the Department's proposed action is upheld by the Fair Hearing Official, the Department promptly implements the action and also takes action to recoup or recover any benefits that were incorrectly paid to the assistance unit as a result of the request for a hearing within this ten (10) day notice period, described in 1. above, and the Department's continuation of benefits pending the hearing. B. Exceptions to Continuation of Benefits 1. The Department reduces or terminates the assistance unit's benefits prior to the Fair Hearing decision on the date specified in the notice of action, whether or not the Fair Hearing request was received within the ten (10) day notice period, described in A.1. above, if: a. a change adversely affecting the assistance unit's grant occurs while the Fair Hearing decision is pending and the unit fails to request a Fair Hearing based on the new issue; or b. a change is made as a result of a change in law which affects all similarly situated assistance units and the change affects the unit's eligibility or benefit amount while the Fair Hearing decision is pending; or c. the Department’s action which is the subject of the Fair Hearing request is the termination of benefits as a result of the expiration of the twenty-one (21) month or the sixty (60) month durational limit; or

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8525.10 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Fair Hearings TFA _______________________________________________________________________ Subject: Continuing Benefits Pending Fair Hearing _______________________________________________________________________________ 8525.10 B. 1. Exceptions to Continuation of Benefits (continued) d. the Departmental action which is the subject of the Fair Hearing request is the denial of an application for an extension of benefits following the expiration of the twenty-one (21) month durational limit. 2. The Department reduces or terminates the assistance unit's benefits prior to the Fair Hearing decision even if the unit requests a Fair Hearing within the ten (10) day notice period, described in A. 1, above, if the sole issue is one of federal or State law or Departmental policy, and not one of incorrect grant computation or application of law or policy. 3. The Department does not continue special benefits pending a Fair Hearing. C. Reinstatement of Benefits 1. Provided all requirements are met for requesting a Fair Hearing, and the assistance unit is entitled to a continuation of benefits as described in A and B above, the Department reinstates the assistance unit's benefits if such benefits have been reduced or terminated pending a Fair Hearing decision if: a. the Department took an action without appropriately sending timely notice; and b. the assistance unit requested a Fair Hearing within ten (10) days of the Department's mailing of the notice. 2. If the Department reinstates the assistance unit's benefits pending the Fair Hearing decision, the unit continues to receive such benefits until the decision is rendered unless there is a subsequent change in the assistance unit's circumstances which affects their eligibility or benefit level. D. Notification of Assistance Unit The Department promptly notifies the assistance unit in writing if benefits are reduced or terminated pending the Fair Hearing decision.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8525.10 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Fair Hearings TFA _______________________________________________________________________ Subject: Continuing Benefits Pending Fair Hearing _______________________________________________________________________________ 8525.10 E. Corrective Action 1. If the Department does not reduce or terminate the assistance unit's benefits pending the Fair Hearing decision, and the decision upholds the Department, the Department recoups the overpayment which the assistance unit received during this period. 2. If the Department reduces or terminates the assistance unit's benefits pending the Fair Hearing decision, and the decision favors the assistance unit, the Department makes a prompt corrective payment to the assistance unit to correct the underpayment which occurred during this period.
