CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8530.05 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: General Service Provisions ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.05 A. Availability of Services

Applicants and recipients of Temporary Family Assistance (TFA) and others who are required to participate as described at 8530.10 may receive services provided through Employment Services to assist them in becoming employed, subject to the limitations and priorities of service discussed below.

B. Employment Services Activities

Employment Services activities are those activities which move TFA families towards independence from welfare by removing barriers to employment, preparing participants for employment, and by assisting in obtaining and retaining employment. Such activities include but are not limited to the following:

1. Educational activities below the post-secondary level including, but not limited to high school completion, preparation for general equivalency diploma, and English as a Second Language (ESL);

2. Job skills training including vocational training;

3. Job readiness activities in combination with other activities;

4. Job development and job placement activities in combination with other activities;

5. Job search activities, including Self-Directed Job Search, and Job Search Skills Training (JSST):

6. Alternative Work Experience;

7. Unsubsidized employment;

8. Drug or alcohol rehabilitation;

9. domestic violence counseling.

C. Limitations

1. Not every individual is entitled to receive Employment Services.

2. Provision of services is limited, based on the availability of resources.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8530.05 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: General Service Provisions ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.05 C. Limitations (continued)

3. The Department determines which individuals will receive Employment Services and which services are provided.

D. Basis of Provision of Services

The Department determines which services to provide based on its discretionary consideration of a variety of factors, including the service needs of the individual, the availability and suitability of a service, the service needs and availability of services for other participants, the goal of independence from TFA within twenty-one months, and the goal of the Department to meet federal TANF participation rates.

E. Priorities for Provision of Services

Priority for Employment Services and activities is given to TFA recipients who are mandatory Employment Services participants.

F. Post-Secondary Education

Except for individuals attending State community-technical colleges as specified by Job Connection or Self-Sufficiency Plans written prior to 7-1-95, the department does not include enrollment in higher education as an Employment Services activity and does not provide special benefits for those who enroll in higher education on their own.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8530.10 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Exemptions from Participation ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.10 A. General Provisions Except as specified below, Temporary Family Assistance applicants, recipients, and disqualified or ineligible parents of children who are TFA applicants or recipients are required to comply with Employment Services participation requirements. (cross reference: 8530.15) B. Categorical Exemptions 1. General Provision a. Categorical exemptions are considered and granted at any time the individual is receiving TFA benefits. b. When more than one member of the assistance unit qualifies for one or more exemptions based on caring for an incapacitated household member, or caring for a child under one, the exemption is given only to one individual unless there is a compelling reason that both individuals are needed to provide the care. 2. Exemption Criteria The following individuals are categorically exempt from participation in Employment Services: a dependent child under age 19; a minor parent except when; (1) the minor parent is the caretaker relative of a child in the home; or (2) the minor parent is the second parent of a child in the home and the other parent is the caretaker of the child. c. an individual determined by the Department to be incapacitated in accordance with conditions specified below at B.3.;

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8530.10 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Exemptions from Participation ______________________________________________________________________________ 8530.10 B. 2. Exemption Criteria (continued) d. an individual responsible for the care of an incapacitated household member and such care is needed and provided at either unpredictable times or on a substantially continuous basis effectively precluding employment under the following conditions: (1) the individual has been determined physically or mentally incapacitated by the Department in accordance with the provisions of B.3. below; and (2) no other household member can provide the care; and (3) the individual must be in the home but need not be a member of the assistance unit; e. an individual aged 60 or older; f. one individual in the household caring for a child under one year of age, if such a child is not subject to the family cap provision (cross reference: 8562.20); a pregnant or postpartum woman if certified by a physician to be unable to work; h. a woman whose pregnancy ended within the past six weeks. 3. Incapacity a. To be considered incapacitated an adult must have a physical or mental illness or impairment (or combination of impairments) of such debilitating nature that it eliminates the person's ability to engage in employment on a predictable basis with reasonable regularity. Such illness or impairment must be expected to last for at least thirty (30) days. b. To be considered incapacitated, a child must have a physical or mental illness or impairment (or combination of impairments) of such debilitating nature that such child requires parental care at unpredictable times with reasonable regularity or on a substantially continuous basis.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-99 Transmittal: UP-04-6 8530.10 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Exemptions from Participation ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.10 B. 3. Incapacity (continued) c. Receipt of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security benefits based on disability or blindness also establishes incapacity. C. Exemption Due to Unemployability 1. Mandatory participants who are not otherwise exempt are considered to be employable until the twentieth month of time-limited TFA eligibility. 2. After the receipt of twenty months of Temporary Family Assistance, the Department exempts otherwise mandatory participants for unemployability provided all of the following conditions are met: a. the individual is age forty (40) or older; and b. the individual is not employed at any level; and c. the individual meets all conditions necessary to grant an extension of time limited TFA benefits based on a good faith effort to obtain and retain employment. (cross reference 8540.10) and; d. the individual has not completed grade six; and e. the individual has not been employed more than six (6) months in the last five years. 3. The Department removes an individual's exemption due to unemployability if the individual enters and retains unsubsidized employment for a period of two consecutive months.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-99 Transmittal: UP-04-6 8530.15 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Participation Requirements ______________________________________________________________________________ 8530.15 Participation Requirements All mandatory Employment Services participants must comply with Employment Services requirements, unless there is good cause not to do so. Failure to comply in an Employment Services activity without good cause results in a penalty being imposed on the assistance unit. (cross reference: 8530.55 and 8530.60) Compliance includes the following: A. providing relevant information as needed by the Department or by an employment service agency designated by the Department; B. being available for work; C. cooperating with the Department in efforts to secure employment, provide education, and job training or support services; D. reporting for interviews with employers to whom referred for potential suitable employment; E. accepting bona fide offers of suitable employment as described at 8530.20 or increased hours of suitable employment and or wages; F. continuing in suitable employment and maintaining the level of earnings. Loss of employment for a reason other than wilful misconduct or voluntarily quitting does not result in an employment services penalty; G. attending either group or individual orientation sessions as requested by the Department; H. satisfactorily participating in employment and or assigned Employment Services activities for up to thirty-five hours per week as required by the Department; I. satisfactorily participating in services designed to remove barriers to employment, including, but not limited to, counseling and supportive services for victims of domestic violence and substance abuse treatment or counseling, when appropriate; cooperating in the assessment process; K. participating in all employment and training activities without disrupting the activities;

8530.20 The Department considers that any job is suitable if the employer is in substantial compliance with standards of employment prescribed in any applicable State statute or regulation and the job does not involve any illegal activity and it is within the capabilities of the individual or will be brought within the capabilities of the individual with reasonable accommodations made by the employer in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, unless one or more of the following is true:

A. A car or other reasonable transportation such as a bus, car pool or van pool is not available to the participant and the distance to the job is unreasonable in that it is not within walking distance; or

B. Commuting time is more than two hours per day, not including trips to provide child care.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-97-19 8530.25 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES ____________________________________________________________ Subject: Work Test/Assessment ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.25 A. Assessment Process

The assessment may involve one or two steps. Step one consists of a work test which is conducted only for individuals who are assigned to Self-Directed Job Search as their initial employability plan activity. Step two is the full assessment which is conducted for other participants, including those who complete the work test.

B. Work Test

1. The work test is an objective measurement of a participant's performance in Self-Directed Job Search.

2. The participant passes the work test by engaging in bona fide effort to obtain employment during Self-Directed Job Search which includes a minimum number of employer contacts made over a specified period of time.

3. The results of the work test are considered in the full assessment.

4. Work test results are also one factor in determining eligibility for an extension of time-limited Temporary Family Assistance benefits. (cross reference: 8540.10)

C. Full Assessment

1. The purpose of the full assessment is to determine the individual's level of employability in order to ascertain the need for education, training, job search or social services.

2. The full assessment may be conducted prior to or after participation in initial job search or substitute activities.

3. The full assessment includes a consideration of the individual's level of employability and relevant family needs which impact the ability to secure and maintain employment.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8530.30 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Employability Plan ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.30 A. General Principles

1. Participation in Employment Services activities in the Jobs First program is prescribed by an Employability Plan as set forth in this chapter. The Employability Plan which is developed for a participant may consist of one or two parts as described below:

a. Part I Employability Plans specify initial job seeking or preparation activities for individuals newly granted into Temporary Family Assistance.

b. Part II of the Plan is based on full assessment, as described at 8530.25, C, and specifies participation in further activities designed to enhance the participant's employability, if necessary, and secure unsubsidized employment to obtain the goal of independence from welfare.

2. All Employability Plans specify a goal of entry into unsubsidized employment or, for those employed, into more substantial employment.

3. The Department may require mandatory participants to engage in plan activities in any combination up to thirty-five hours per week.

4. Plan activities, including hours in unsubsidized employment, may exceed thirty-five hours per week if additional hours are required by the activity and agreed to by the participant.

5. Mandatory participants who fail to comply without good cause with their Employability Plan requirements, except for failure to pass the Work Test, are subject to penalties for non-compliance. (cross reference: 8530.55)

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8530.30 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Employability Plan ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.30 B. Prescribed Activities

1. The Department determines the specific sequence of plan activities or combination of activities for each participant based on the goal of the assistance unit being independent from welfare within twenty-one (21) months. Plan activities are assigned with consideration given to participant characteristics, the availability of services, and when applicable, the results of the assessment.

2. Notwithstanding B.1, above, participants may be assigned to activities which enable the State to meet participation rates pursuant to the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 (Public Law 104-193).

3. Mandatory participants must engage in job search activities prior to enrollment in education or training, unless initial job search is waived or substitute activities are approved by the Department.

4. Education or training activities are approvable for individuals under the following conditions:

a. Education through high school completion or GED, including necessary remedial or basic education is approvable for individuals under age 20 without a diploma or GED.

b. Following good faith job search efforts, as described in 3, above, education or training for other individuals is approvable at the discretion of the Department under the following circumstances:

(1) the assessment substantiates the need to enhance the individual's employability through education or training; and

(2) the education or training is consistent with the goal of unsubsidized employment; and

(3) the education or training activity is expected to end in job placement; and

(4) the individual is not employable at a level which allows family income to equal the Federal Poverty Level.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8530.30 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Employability Plan ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.30 B. Prescribed Activities (continued)

5. Except for individuals attending State community-technical colleges as specified by Job Connection or Self-Sufficiency Plans written prior to 7-1-95, the Department does not include enrollment in higher education as a Plan activity and does not provide special benefits for those who enroll in higher education on their own.

6. The Department may assign new or additional activities designed to increase family income, which may preclude continuation of existing employment or self-employment.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-97-19 8530.35 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES ______________________________________________________________________ Subject: General Principles For Special Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.35 A. Eligible Individuals

1. Subject to the limitations contained in this subject, special benefits are available to the following individuals:

a. Employment Services participants who are Temporary Family Assistance (TFA) applicants or recipients; and

b. others who are required to participate in Employment Services as described at 8530.10.

2. To qualify for special benefits, the individuals described above must meet the following criteria:

a. The individual must be participating in an Employment Services activity, other than unsubsidized employment, as specified by an approved Employability Plan (cross reference 8530.30); and

b. The individual must have an employability plan which authorizes the use of special benefits to support approved activities.

B. Benefits

1. Special benefits cover costs associated with participation in certain aspects of Employment Services which cannot be met by other resources.

2. If a participant is receiving Temporary Family Assistance and Food Stamps concurrently, he or she is only eligible for those special benefits available under TFA.

3. Individuals participating in Employment Services may receive the following special benefits, subject to the limitations specified in this subject:

a. Subject to the provisions at 8530.45, a participation allowance is provided for child care and transportation expenses for those taking part in Self-Directed Job Search.

b. Subject to the provisions at 8530.45, a participation allowance may be provided for child care and transportation expenses for individuals taking part in irregular, short term Employment Services activities.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-97-19 8530.35 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES ______________________________________________________________________ Subject: General Principles for Special Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.35 B. 3. Benefits (continued)

c. Subject to the provisions at 8530.40, transportation benefits are provided for a participant who takes part in ongoing Employment Services activities other than unsubsidized employment.

C. Benefit Payment Restrictions

1. Payment of special benefits are for costs associated with participation in Employment Services.

2. Participants must continue to satisfactorily take part in activities specified by their Employability Plans in order to continue to receive special benefits.

3. Benefits are not provided under the following circumstances:

a. when they are for items covered by TFA or other special benefits available under other State or federal or other assistance programs; or

b. when service or equivalent services are available free of charge; or

c. when they are not for Employment Services activities; or

d. when inconsistent with and not required by the Employability Plan.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-97-19 8530.40 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Transportation Special Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.40 A. Eligibility for Transportation Benefits

The Department pays for transportation expenses necessary for the individual to participate in Jobs First Employment Services activities, subject to the restrictions listed below.

1. Participants engaged in Self-Directed Job Search are subject to flat participation allowances. (cross reference: 8530.45)

2. Participants engaged in irregular, short term Employment Services activities may receive a participation allowance in lieu of regular transportation benefits. (cross reference: 8530.45)

3. Transportation benefits are provided if needed to allow a participant to take part in any other Employment Services activity, except for unsubsidized employment.

B. Types of Transportation Expenses Allowed

1. The Department only pays for bus fares or mileage for driving private automobiles.

2. Mileage driven in private automobiles is paid only when bus transportation is unavailable or inaccessible.

C. Private Automobiles

1. When public transportation is unavailable or inaccessible, the Department pays for private automobile transportation necessary for a participant to take part in an Employability Plan activity.

2. Payment is made for the round trip from the participant's home to the activity, including that portion necessary for child care.

3. This benefit is available to pay for the following;

a. transportation in an automobile owned or borrowed by a member of the assistance unit; or

b. reimbursement to someone not in the assistance unit who transports a participant with his or her own motor vehicle.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-97-19 8530.40 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Transportation Special Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.40 C. Private Automobiles (continued)

4. Payment is determined as follows:

a. 20 cents per mile is allowed;

b. up to a maximum of 50 miles per day;

c. a minimum payment of $2.00 per day is made for travel of ten miles or less.

5. No other costs related to private automobile transportation are allowed.

D. Bus Fares

The Department pays for bus fares at the cost charged, not to exceed $10.00 per day.

E. Method of Payment

1. Payments for mileage and bus fare are made directly to the participant.

2. At the discretion of the Department passes or tokens are provided for bus fares when available, in lieu of cash.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8530.45 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Participation Allowances ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.45 A. Purpose of Allowances

1. There are two types of participation allowances that may be issued by the Department as described below:

a. Self-Directed Job Search Participation Allowance

Employment Services participants assigned to Self-Directed Job Search may be eligible to receive a participation allowance and a supplement. The allowance and supplement assist with periodic baby sitting and transportation costs incurred when the participant attends employment-related appointments outside the home such as interviews or employment application inquiries. Periodic costs are those associated with fulfilling requirements of the Employability Plan which specifies that the participant must conduct a minimum number of employer contacts made over a specified period of time.

b. Special Participation Allowance

Employment Services participants required to participate in irregular, short-term activities specified by Employability Plans which last no longer than five (5) consecutive days may receive a special participation allowance in lieu of regular child care or transportation benefits.

2. Participants may not receive a participation allowance in a month that the Department provided, or will provide, child care benefits, as provided under Sections 17b-3-1 through 17b-3-6 of the Regulations of Connecticut Agencies, Child Care Subsidy program, or transportation benefits, as provided under 8530.40 for the same activity.

B. General Guidelines

1. The participation allowances are for the cost of baby sitting and/or transportation only.

2. Baby sitting is temporary, short term care of a child which is needed to allow an assistance unit member to look for work or take part in a short term Employment Services required by the Department. Baby sitting is distinguished from child care which is ongoing, formal daily care of a child.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8530.45 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Participation Allowances ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.45 B. General Guidelines (continued)

3. Eligibility for the baby sitting allowances are limited to families with children under six years of age only unless participation is required during periods when school age-children are not in school or such children otherwise need care in order for the individual to participate in assigned activities.

4. If eligible, families may receive combination allowances for both baby sitting and transportation.

5. Allowance usage may be subject to verification and recoupment if mismanagement of the allowance is determined to have occurred.

C. Self-Directed Job Search Participation Allowance Amounts

1. The baby sitting allowance is $55.00 per month.

2. The transportation allowance is $9.00 per month.

3. The combination amount is $64.00 per month.

D. Self-Directed Job Search Participation Allowance Issuance

1. Payments are issued prospectively.

2. Payments are not issued for more than three months at any one time.

3. Payments may be issued in the following methods:

a. lump sums;

b. recurring;

c. non-recurring.

4. If a participant requests and is eligible for a participation allowance at any time during the month, he or she is eligible to receive the entire month's allowance.

5. A written record of employer contacts is kept by the participant throughout his or her participation in Self-Directed Job Search. The written record must include information pertaining to each contact such as employer names, dates, and contact results. CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8530.45 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Participation Allowances ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.45 E. Supplements to Self-Directed Job Search Participation Allowances

1. The Department issues a supplemental payment in addition to the Self-Directed Jobs Search participation allowance for baby sitting and/or transportation under the following conditions:

a. for supplements to the transportation allowance, exceptional circumstances must exist to justify the need for a supplemental payment for the required face-to-face contact; and

b. for supplemental baby sitting allowance, the assistance unit must have more than one child who qualifies for and is in need of a baby sitter.

2. Supplemental payments are issued for costs associated with the required face-to-face contacts, but not for additional voluntary contacts.

3. The total of the supplement to the baby sitting participation allowance is the actual cost of the additional baby sitting (over the first $55 per month) not to exceed an additional $36.00 per month.

4. The total of the transportation participation allowance plus the transportation supplemental payment may not exceed the amounts allowed for transportation special benefits. (cross-reference 8530.40)

F. Special Participation Allowances for Irregular, Short-Term Activities

1. Employment Services participants required to attend irregular, short-term activities as specified by their Employability Plans, may receive a special participation allowance to cover the baby sitting and transportation costs associated with such participation.

2. An irregular, short-term activity is one that does not last more than five (5) consecutive days.

3. Participation allowances paid under these circumstances are $10.00 per day, not to exceed $50.00 in a month.

8530.50 A. Introduction

Conciliation is a process designed to allow the Department and the participant the opportunity to put forth a good faith effort to settle disputes, disagreements or misunderstandings related to Employment Services (ES) before an adverse action is taken.

B. General Principles

1. The conciliation process is used to settle disputes relating to Employment Services, except those regarding a voluntary quit of employment, reduction in the level of earnings or termination of employment due to willful misconduct.

2. The conciliation process must be completed within thirty (30) calendar days from the date conciliation is initiated, but may be ended earlier as described below under Section E.

3. The first day of the conciliation period is determined as follows:

a. When conciliation is initiated by the Department, the first day of the conciliation period is the date that a notice of conciliation is sent to the individual;

b. When conciliation is initiated by the individual, the first day of the conciliation period is the date the request is received by the Department.

4. Benefits will not be reduced, suspended or discontinued based on the issue being conciliated until the conciliation process is completed.

C. Initiating Conciliation

1. Conciliation is initiated by the Department when a preliminary determination has been made that an Employment Services participant has not complied with ES requirements without good cause and before sending the notice which imposes the penalty or increases a penalty for failure to comply.

8530.50 C. Initiating Conciliation (continued)

2. Conciliation may be initiated by the participant when he or she believes that the services offered or required are inappropriate or incorrect.

D. Conciliation Conferences

1. Conciliation conferences may be conducted by way of an in-office, face-to-face conference or, with the participant's consent, through a telephone conference.

2. The Department informs the individual about Employment Services requirements and the conciliation process.

3. The individual has the right to bring another person to the conference to act as his or her representative.

4. If a Department supervisor is involved, he or she may act as a mediator in the process.

5. All notices regarding conciliation shall include notice of the right to receive reasonable accommodation for disabling conditions that may be contributing to the alleged non-compliance.

6. The Department shall review the individual’s file, including their Service Needs Assessment and the Connecticut Works Business System, to determine if a disability that is reasonably indicated by documentation in the file may have contributed to alleged non-compliance.

7. During the conciliation meeting, the Department shall offer the individual the opportunity to be screened for mental health conditions, substance use disorders or learning disabilities.

8. The conciliation shall remain open as long as the individual is cooperating with the screening process.

8530.50 D. Conciliation Conferences (continued)

9. If the screening indicates that the individual is more likely than not to have a disability that contributed to non-compliance with an ES requirement, a finding of good cause will result.

As a result of the screening, additional professional evaluation and treatment may be recommended. Additional instances of good cause will not be granted based on the same screening if the individual does not cooperate with recommendations of professional evaluation and necessary treatment.

11. The Department shall inform the Department of Labor Jobs First Employment Services case manager of the determination.

12. The Department may also make a referral for future evaluation to the Bureau of Rehabilitation Services or to a participating provider in the Department’s medical assistance program.

13. The Department shall engage the individual in a conversation regarding the need for reasonable accommodations related to their participation in the program.

E. Terminating Conciliation

1. The Department may terminate the conciliation prior to the thirtieth (30) day under the following conditions:

a. when the participant does not appear at a scheduled conciliation conference without good cause, and does not contact the Department to reschedule;

b. when the participant, without good cause, does not meet a deadline to respond to a request to contact the Department to arrange a conciliation conference;

c. when the dispute between the Department and the participant is successfully resolved prior to the thirtieth (30) day;

8530.50 E. Terminating Conciliation (continued)

d. when it has been determined by the Department that the dispute cannot be resolved.

2. The participant may terminate the conciliation process at any time.

3. Good cause is considered to exist when circumstances beyond the participant's control reasonably prevent him or her from appearing at a conciliation meeting or responding to a request to contact the Department to schedule a conciliation conference.

F. Failure to Offer Conciliation

Failure by the Department to offer conciliation when it is appropriate does not confer any right to continued benefits.

G. Effect on Fair Hearings

The participant's right to a Fair Hearing is not impaired in any way as the result of participating in conciliation. (cross reference: 8525.05)

STEP ACTION 1 Client fails to comply with Employment Services requirements and does not have apparent good cause 2 JFES Case Manager makes a sanction referral in CTWBS

3 ESS Performs an initial evaluation of the situation. Determine whether good cause appears to exist for the client who failed to participate in Employment Services. If good cause appears to exist, no conference is necessary. If good cause does not appear to exist, proceed to next step. 4 (ESS) Notify the client that a conciliation conference is necessary. Send a conciliation letter L645 or L646 (Spanish version) to the client or, Contact the client by telephone. If there is no response to the telephone contact, send letter as indicated above. 5 (ESS) If the client does not respond to your request or fails to appear for the conciliation conference, evaluate for good cause. If good cause exists, reschedule conference. If good cause does not exist, pursue sanction as appropriate. 6 (ESS) During conference Inform the client about: The requirements of the Employment Services Program. The purpose of the conciliation. His or her rights in the process. The date the conciliation began. The date the conciliation will end. The date a decision is due. The client’s right to a fair hearing. The client’s right to accommodations and Offer the client an opportunity to be screened for a possible disability involving mental health conditions, substance use disorders or learning disabilities

P- 8530.50

P- 8530.50 (continued) STEP ACTION 7(ESS) If the client declines screening, complete the conciliation as usual. Complete BRS Referral Form W369 indicating that client declined screening. Email W369 to HYPERLINK "mailto:DSS-TFA-BRSProj@ct.gov" DSS-TFA-BRSProj@ct.gov

8 (ESS) If the client accepts screening and the conciliation interview is being performed in the office:

Complete W369 BRS Referral Form and send to BRS counselor to schedule the screening. If a BRS counselor is available, screening may take place immediately. If a BRS counselor is not available or the conciliation interview is being conducted by phone the BRS Counselor will schedule an appointment for the screening.

9 The BRS counselor will: screen the client within two weeks of referral provide the screening results to the ESS using BRS Referral form W369 provide screening results to JFES Case Manager via CTWBS

10 (ESS) If the screening indicates that no disabling condition exists, pursue sanction as appropriate. Complete Conciliation Save copy of W369 BRS Referral form in case record and complete narrative

11 (ESS) If screening indicates that a disabling condition is likely, grant good cause using CTWBS good cause reason “BRS evaluation for disability” Complete the conciliation. Update narrative.

12 The JFES case manager:

Creates a new JFES employment plan activity “BRS Assessment/Services” and enters the date of the screening as the actual start date. Refers the BRS Assessment/Services activity in CTWBS by selecting the BRS counselor from the dropdown list of BRS providers. Provides for special benefits to attend the assessment, if necessary 13 BRS Counselor reviews existing documents and may make referral for professional evaluation.

STEP ACTION 14 If evaluation results in a diagnosis that makes the client ineligible for BRS services BRS will consult with the JFES CM via email and provide input for the employment plan. 15 If evaluation results in a diagnosis that makes the client eligible for BRS services BRS will ask the client if he/she wants to apply for BRS services

16 If the client does not apply for BRS services. The BRS Counselor will notify the ESS and the JFES case manager via email and summarize the results and make employment recommendations by using the following format in CTWBS Private Notes: Format Issues: broad summary for examples – mental health, substance abuse, LD Recommendations: (related to employment)

17 If the results are that the participant should pursue a medical exemption from participation in employment services: The BRS counselor will notify both the ESS and the JFES case manager of the results. The ESS will issue the MRT packet to the participant and make a referral to ESP to assist with follow through of MRT packet. The ESS may grant a temporary exemption (if possible) and notify the JFES case manager via email (See UPM 8530.10 for determination of incapacity of an applicant or recipient.) P- 8530.50 (continued)

STEP ACTION 18 If the client applies for BRS services. The BRS counselor and the JFES case manager shall coordinate assigned activities and develop a joint plan for the participant. The BRS assigned activities take priority and the JFES activities are to support and complement the BRS activities. The JFES employment plans shall require that the client follow the instructions in the BRS plan. The BRS Counselor will document the client’s participation in BRS activities on the TFA-24 “Jobs First Employment Services Program Authorization for Disclosure of Information” form. The JFES case manager will continue to provide case management services including issuance of special benefits, monitoring and recording hours of participation on the CTWBS Attendance Record. 19 If the client does not comply with the new employment plan and does not have apparent good cause, the BRS Counselor will make a sanction referral using CTWBS 20 The ESS will perform an initial evaluation of the situation. Determine whether good cause appears to exist for the client who has failed to comply with employment services 21 If conciliation is necessary, the ESS will have a conference over the phone or set up an appointment. 22 During the conference the ESS will Inform the client about: The Employment Services Requirement. The purpose of the conciliation. His or her rights in the process. When the conference has begun. When the conference has ended. The date when a decision is due. The client’s right to a fair hearing. The client’s right to reasonable accommodations Offer BRS screening ONLY if there is evidence of a learning disability, substance use disorder or mental health issue that the client was not previously screened for by BRS.

23 (ESS) Determine good cause and complete the conciliation. 24 (ESS) Notify the client of the decision via the conciliation results letter (L629, or the Spanish version). 25 (ESS) Complete the CTWBS Sanction screen. 26 (ESS) Notify the JFES Case Manager if the case closes because a penalty was applied. P- 8530.50 (continued)

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8530.55 ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services TFA ________________________________________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ 8530.55 A. General Principles Failure of a mandatory participant to comply with Employment Services participation requirements without good cause may subject the assistance unit to a penalty. The final determination of good cause is made by the Department of Social Services. 2. The penalties for non-compliance with participation requirements without good cause differ for mandatory participants before and after the receipt of twenty-one (21) months of Temporary Family Assistance as described in C. below. 3. Failure to comply with Employment Services participation requirements without good cause is considered in the determination of eligibility for extensions of time-limited TFA benefits. (cross reference: 8530.15 and 8540.10) B. Individuals Who Subject an Assistance Unit to a Penalty 1. Any mandatory participant who fails to comply with or participate in any required Employment Services activity without good cause, subjects the entire assistance unit to a penalty. 2. Any mandatory participant who voluntarily quits employment, intentionally reduces his or her level of earnings, or engages in wilful misconduct which results in his or her termination from employment without good cause, also subjects the entire assistance unit to a penalty. Any applicant who has not exhausted the first twenty-one months of the twenty-one month time limit may subject the assistance unit to a penalty under the following conditions: The person is a mandatory Employment Services participant; and b. Within sixty days prior to the application and without good cause the person: voluntarily quit or reduced hours of suitable employment;

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8530.55 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services TFA _________________________________________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ 8530.55 B. 3. b. Individuals Who Subject an Assistance Unit to a Penalty (continued) (2) refused to accept additional hours (up to 40 hours per week) of suitable employment; (3) was fired from suitable employment for wilful misconduct; or did not accept a bona fide offer of suitable employment. Any member of an assistance unit applying for an extension, may subject the assistance unit to a penalty under the following conditions: The person is a mandatory Employment Services participant; and b. within 120 days prior to the date of application, and without good cause, the person: voluntarily quit or reduced hours of suitable employment; refused to accept additional hours (up to 40 hours per week) of suitable employment; was fired from suitable employment for wilful misconduct; or did not accept a bona fide offer of suitable employment. C. Nature of Penalty 1. Penalties Within Twenty-One Months of TFA Receipt When a mandatory participant associated with an assistance unit which is not in an extension of the twenty-one (21) month time limit does not comply without good cause with an Employment Services requirement, a penalty is imposed on the assistance unit as follows: a. For the first violation, the Temporary Family Assistance benefit is reduced twenty-five percent for a period of three (3) consecutive months.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8530.55 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services TFA _________________________________________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ 8530.55 C. 1. Penalties Within Twenty-One Months of TFA Receipt For the second violation, the Temporary Family Assistance benefit is reduced by thirty-five percent for a period of three (3) consecutive months. For a first or second employment services violation, when the assistance unit consists of only one recipient and such recipient fails to comply with an employment services requirement the assistance unit is not eligible for assistance for three consecutive months. d. For the third and all subsequent violations, the entire assistance unit is ineligible for Temporary Family Assistance for a period of three (3) consecutive months. To again receive assistance, the assistance unit must re-apply and re-establish eligibility for Temporary Family Assistance at the expiration of the three month period. 2. Penalty During Extensions of TFA When a mandatory participant associated with an assistance unit which is in an extension of the twenty-one (21) month time limit fails to comply with any Employment Services participation requirement, the penalty is applied as follows: a. The assistance unit is ineligible for cash assistance for the remainder of the extension and any future extensions based on a good faith effort to obtain and retain employment. The penalty is applied notwithstanding the provision at F.1.c. below, pertaining to substantially new or different requirements. 3. Penalties for Violations Prior to Receiving Assistance The penalty for violations committed prior to receipt of assistance by an applicant who has not used twenty-one months of time limited assistance, as described in B.3. above, is reduction of benefits as described at C.1. above.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8530.55 page 4 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance ______________________________________________________________________________ 8530.55 C. 3. Penalties for Violations Prior to Receiving Assistance (continued) The penalty for violations committed prior to receipt of assistance by a person applying for an extension, as described in B.4. above, is ineligibility for 120 days. D. Determining the Number of Violations 1. Violations are counted separately for each assistance unit member who is required to comply. 2. The record of the number of violations is carried with each individual beginning with violations committed on or after the assistance unit begins to receive Temporary Family Assistance. 3. Violations committed before the assistance unit enters Temporary Family Assistance are not counted when determining the number of violations committed by the individual. When the assistance unit includes more than one member who has not complied with an Employment Services requirement without good cause during the same period, the benefit reduction is applied based upon the highest number of violations of any non-compliant assistance unit member. 5. When the assistance unit includes more than one member who has not complied with an Employment Services requirement without good cause, and the penalty for the individual with the highest number of violations ends while other penalties continue, the penalty is applied based upon the next highest number of violations of any non-compliant assistance unit member. 6. If an individual does not comply with an Employment Services requirement without good cause, but agrees to comply or begins to comply before a penalty is imposed, a violation is still considered to have occurred and the full penalty will still be imposed.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8530.55 page 5 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance ______________________________________________________________________________ 8530.55 D. Determining the Number of Violations (continued) 7. If an individual has not demonstrated cooperation prior to the end of a penalty period or has not otherwise contacted the Department, another violation is recorded, and a new penalty appropriate for the number of the next violation begins. 8. If a Fair Hearing decision overturns the Department's decision to implement a penalty, the number of any subsequent violations is reduced accordingly and a corrective payment is issued, if appropriate. E. Beginning Date of Penalty 1. For recipients, the penalty period begins the first day of the month following the month in which the ten (10) day notice of adverse action expires. 2. For applicants, the beginning date of the penalty period is determined as follows: a. For voluntary quit, termination due to willful misconduct, and reduction in level of earnings, the beginning date of the penalty period is the first day of the month in which the offense occurred. b. For other Employment Services offenses, the beginning date of the penalty period is the first day of the month in which the effective date of assistance occurs. F. Changing the Length of the Penalty 1. The length of the penalties described in C.1. above, may be shortened only under the following circumstances: a. The person who did not comply becomes exempt from those requirements. b. The individual who caused the penalty leaves the assistance unit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8530.55 page 6 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Penalties for Non-Compliance ______________________________________________________________________________ 8530.55 F. 1. Changing the Length of the Penalty (continued) c. A mandatory participant commits a new offense during the penalty period by failing to comply without good cause with a substantially new or different Employment Services requirement. Under this circumstance, the current penalty period is ended and a new penalty period is established. d. A mandatory participant commits any offense without good cause during an extension to the twenty-one month time limit. Under this circumstance, the assistance unit is ineligible for cash assistance for the remainder of the extension and any future extensions based on a good faith effort to obtain and retain employment. 2. If an application is filed while a penalty period is in effect, the penalty continues. The penalty period cannot be shortened by reapplication.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-99 Transmittal: UP-04-6 8530.60 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Good Cause for Non-Compliance ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.60 A. Good Cause Defined Good cause is considered to exist when circumstances beyond the participant's control reasonably prevent him or her from complying with an Employment Services requirement. B. General Circumstances Good cause includes, but is not limited to, the following circumstances when such circumstances reasonably prevent the individual from participating in an Employment Services activity: 1. illness of the individual; illness of a family member that requires care to be provided by the individual; unavailability of child care; 4. unavailability of transportation; 5. a family emergency; 6. domestic violence; or unreasonable terms and conditions of employment. C. Victims of Domestic Violence Good cause for not complying with an Employment Services requirement exists when a participant cannot comply with an Employment Services requirement due to domestic violence or the risk of further domestic violence which is of such severity as to reasonably prevent compliance with the requirement. Good cause may be found in appropriate cases with consideration of the following factors:

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-99 Transmittal: UP-04-6 8530.60 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Good Cause for Non-Compliance ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.60 C. Victims of Domestic Violence (continued) 1. the participant has physical injuries caused by abuse or psychological effects of abuse prohibiting such participant to work or engage in other Employment Services activities; or 2. the Employment Services activity or employment is substantially disrupted due to domestic violence, including civil or criminal legal proceedings related to such domestic violence; or 3. the abuser actively interferes with the participant's Employment Services activity or employment, attendance at the Employment Services activity or employment, or child care arrangements; or 4. an Employment Services activity or employment location puts the applicant or recipient at risk; or 5. Employment Services requirements result in the inability or increased difficulty of the participant to escape domestic violence. Additional Good Cause Reasons - Failure to Maintain Earnings In addition to B. or C. above, the following good cause criteria may apply to a voluntary quit or reduction in hours or wages of employment: 1. The Department of Labor (DOL) determines that a person who quit his or her job had good cause to quit. If DOL determines that good cause does not exist for unemployment compensation purposes, a separate determination of good cause is made by the Department of Social Services; 2. A quit is part of an employment pattern in which workers frequently move from one employer to another, such as migrant farm labor or construction work; 3. The person quit a job or reduced hours to accept other employment which has the potential of leading to self-sufficiency;

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 2-1-03 Transmittal: UP-03-1 8530.60 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Good Cause for Non-Compliance ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.60 D. Additional Good Cause Reasons - Failure to Maintain Earnings (continued) 4. The person quit the job or reduced hours to accept other employment with earnings at or above the level of the previous employment; 5. The person quit employment or reduced hours in order that another assistance unit member may accept an offer of employment. This exemption is allowed only when the new employment provides a wage at or above the level of the previous employment of the person who quit; 6. The person occasionally reduces work hours to meet family obligations; or The person left a temporary employment agency which has not or cannot provide him or her with an appropriate work activity. E. Child Care Criteria Good cause exists for parents who leave employment, refuse to accept employment, or fail to take part in an Employment Services activity under the circumstances described below. 1. To qualify for good cause for lack of child care, the following circumstances must exist: a. A person must be the only parent in the home or the only parent in the home capable of caring for the child due to the physical or mental incapacity of the second parent; and The parent must be caring for his or her child who is under thirteen (13) years of age or who requires child care due to special needs. A person who meets the criteria described in 1. above, is determined to have good cause if he or she has demonstrated inability to obtain child care because appropriate child care is not available within a reasonable distance from the person's home or work site.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-99 Transmittal: UP-03-1 8530.60 page 4 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Good Cause for Non-Compliance ______________________________________________________________________________

8530.60 E. Child Care Criteria 3. A person who meets the criteria described in 1, above, is also determined to have good cause if appropriate and affordable formal child care is unavailable and informal child care by a relative or a friend is unavailable or unsuitable. 4. In determining if a person meets the requirements of this provision, the following definitions apply: Appropriate child care means care that meets the health and safety standards that are required for providers who receive payments under the provisions of the Child Care Assistance Program (CCAP), as mandated by Connecticut General Statutes 17b-749. b. Reasonable distance means care that can be accessed by public or private transportation that is available to the client without interfering with the parent's ability to maintain employment. If transportation is not available, child care must be within reasonable walking distance from the person's home. c. Unsuitable informal care means care that is exempt from the State's licensing requirements, but does not meet the health and safety standards described in a. above, or is otherwise shown to be unsafe or inappropriate for the child. d. Affordable formal child care means licensed child care that costs the parent (after subsidies) no more than ten percent of his or her total income.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-99 Transmittal: UP-04-6 8530.65 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Wilful Misconduct ______________________________________________________________________________ 8530.65 A. Wilful Misconduct - Defined The Department of Social Services (DSS) considers a person terminated from employment for wilful misconduct when he or she is terminated for any of the following reasons: the individual committed deliberate misconduct as described in C. below; the individual committed a single knowing violation of a reasonable and uniformly enforced rule or policy of the employer, when reasonably applied, as described in D. below; the individual was absent on three separate instances within an eighteen-month period under either of the following circumstances: the person did not have good cause as described at 8530.60 for the absence; or the person did not reasonably notify the employer and did not have good cause for not notifying the employer; the individual was tardy as described in F. below; the individual committed a felonious act as described in G. below; or the individual committed larceny as described in H. below. B. DOL Determinations A person was not fired for wilful misconduct under the following circumstances: DOL determines wilful misconduct did not exist; DOL determines that a person was fired for wilful misconduct, but DSS determines the person had good cause as described at 8530.60; or DOL does not determine whether there was wilful misconduct and DSS conducts a separate investigation and determines that wilful misconduct does not exist in accordance with the definition of wilful misconduct as described in this chapter.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-99 Transmittal: UP-04-6 8530.65 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Wilful Misconduct ______________________________________________________________________________ 8530.65 C. Deliberate Misconduct DSS considers that an individual was discharged for deliberate misconduct when all of the following exist: 1. The individual committed an act or made an omission which was contrary to the employer's interest, including any act or omission which is not consistent with the standards of behavior which an employer, in the operation of his business, should reasonably be able to expect from an employee. 2. The individual committed the act or made the omission intentionally or with reckless indifference to the probable consequences of such act or omission. 3. Deliberate misconduct is in wilful disregard of the employer's interest. Wilful disregard of the employer’s interest exists under the following conditions: a. the individual knew or should have known that the act or omission was contrary to the employer's expectation or interest; and at the time the individual committed the act or made the omission, he or she understood that the act or omission was contrary to the employer's expectation or interest and he or she was not motivated or seriously influenced by mitigating circumstances of a compelling nature. Mitigating circumstances include the following: (1) events or conditions which left the individual with no reasonable alternative course of action; or an emergency situation in which a reasonable individual in the same circumstances would commit the same act or make the same omission, despite knowing it was contrary to the employer's expectation or interest.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-99 Transmittal: UP-04-6 8530.65 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Wilful Misconduct ______________________________________________________________________________ 8530.65 D. Knowing Violation DSS considers that an individual was discharged for a knowing violation of a reasonable and uniformly enforced rule or policy when the following circumstances exist: the individual knew, or should have known, of the rule or policy, because it was effectively communicated to the individual. Evidence that the rule or policy was effectively communicated to the individual includes, but is not limited to, the following: posting of the rule or policy within the company at a place likely to be observed by the employees; explanation of the rule at a training or orientation session; verbal explanation of the rule to the individual; distribution of a document to the individual which contained the rule or policy; warnings or other disciplinary action; and evidence of the individual's receipt of any document containing the rule or policy; b. the individual's conduct violated the particular rule or policy; and c. the individual was aware that he or she was engaged in such conduct. DSS considers the rule or policy instituted by an employer is reasonable when the rule or policy furthers the employer’s lawful business interest. DSS considers that a rule or policy of the employer was uniformly enforced when similarly situated employees subject to the workplace rule or policy are treated in a similar manner when a rule or policy is violated.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-99 Transmittal: UP-04-6 8530.65 page 4 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Wilful Misconduct ______________________________________________________________________________ 8530.65 D. Knowing Violation (continued) 4. DSS considers that a rule or policy of an employer was reasonably applied, when: a. the action taken by the employer is appropriate in light of the violation of the rule or policy and the employer's lawful business interest; and b. there were no compelling circumstances which would have prevented the individual from adhering to the rule or policy. 5. DSS determines that wilful misconduct does not exist when the violation of a rule or policy of the employer is a result of the individual's incompetence. Incompetence exists when the individual was incapable of adhering to the requirements of the rule or policy due to a lack of ability, skills or training, unless it is established that the individual wilfully performed below his employer's standard and that the standard was reasonable. E. In the Course of Employment 1. In order to find deliberate misconduct, as described in C. above, or a knowing violation of an employer's rule or policy, as described in D. above, the act or omission must have occurred in the course of employment. In the course of employment includes the following: conduct that takes place during working hours, while the employee is reasonably fulfilling the duties of his employment or otherwise performing any service for the employer's benefit;

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-99 Transmittal: UP-04-6 8530.65 page 5 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Wilful Misconduct ______________________________________________________________________________ 8530.65 E. 2. In the Course of Employment (continued) off-duty misconduct committed by exploitation of the employment relationship, as described in E. 3. below; or c. off-duty misconduct committed by a public trust employee as described in E. 4. below. Exploitation of the employment relationship exists in cases where the individual engaged in off-duty misconduct which was accomplished by knowledge or access acquired through the employment relationship such as, but not limited to: an individual uses his knowledge that the employer’s recently installed security system was not yet operational to burglarize the premises; or an individual uses a company van after hours for his or her personal use. An individual may be found to be a public trust employee if: a. the individual’s primary role and job function is to serve as a guardian of the public trust and safety; b. the individual’s job effectiveness is expressly dependent upon the public's respect and confidence, both on and off-duty; c. the individual has explicit written notice of the expected standard of off-duty conduct; and d. the individual has agreed to the expected standard of off-duty conduct. 5. Public trust employees may include, but are not limited to, police officers, teachers and correctional officers. F. Tardiness Tardiness constitutes wilful misconduct only if the pattern of tardiness constitutes either wilful disregard of the employer’s interest, as described in C. 3. above, or a knowing violation of a reasonable and uniformly enforced rule or policy, as described in D. above.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-99 Transmittal: UP-04-6 8530.65 page 6 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Employment Services ES _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Wilful Misconduct ______________________________________________________________________________ 8530.65 G. Felonious Conduct Felonious conduct is any act by an individual in the course of his employment, as described in E. above, which would constitute a felony under the laws of the state of Connecticut or under federal law, regardless of whether or not criminal proceedings have been instituted. H. Larceny 1. DSS considers misconduct to exist if the individual was discharged for conduct in the course of his employment, as described in E. above, constituting larceny of property or services whose value exceeds twenty-five dollars, or larceny of currency, regardless of the value of such currency. 2. In determining whether the value of the property or services exceeds twenty-five dollars, DSS considers the market value of the property or services at the time of the larceny or, if such value cannot be ascertained, the cost of the replacement of the property or services within a reasonable time after the larceny.

8540 The chapter describes the non-financial eligibility requirements for the TFA program. These requirements involve the following areas:

° Time Limits

° Extensions of Benefits

° Eligible Children, Age Requirements, and Pregnant Women

° Convicted Felons, Probation, and Parole Violators

° Assistance Unit Composition

° Living with a Caretaker Relative

° Minor Parents

° Citizens and Eligible Non-Citizens

° Residency

° Concurrent Assistance

° Striker Status

° Social Security Numbers

° Securing Support

° Digital Imaging
