CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8540.03 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA

Subject: Exemptions from Time Limits 8540.03 A. Exemption Criteria An assistance unit is exempt from the time limits described at 8540.05 and 8540.12 if all of the adults in the assistance unit, all adults who are ineligible or disqualified parents who live with a dependent child in the assistance unit, and any non-parent caretaker relatives of a dependent child in the assistance unit meet at least one exemption criteria. In determining an exemption from the time limits, minor parents are treated as adults only under the following circumstances: the minor parent is the caretaker relative of a child in the home; or the minor parent is the second parent of a child in the home and the other parent is the caretaker of the child. Note: Minor parents are only allowed to be caretakers when they are exempt from the requirements of living with a responsible adult. (cross reference 8540.35) 3. To be considered exempt an individual described in 1. above, must be one of the following: a. incapacitated, as described in C. below; or b. age 60 or older; or c. responsible for the care of an incapacitated household member, as described in C. below, and such care is needed and provided at either unpredictable times or on a substantially continuous basis, effectively precluding employment, if no other person in the home can provide the care; or d. a non-parent caretaker relative who is not a member of the assistance unit; caring for a child under the age of one who is not subject to the family cap as described at 8562.20; f. pregnant or postpartum, if a physician has certified that she is unable to work; CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8540.03 page 2 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA

Subject: Exemptions from Time Limits 8540.03 A. 3. Exemption Criteria (continued) g. a woman whose pregnancy ended for the period described in B.5. below; or h. unemployable, as described in D. below. Minor parents attending and satisfactorily completing high school or high school equivalency programs and their children are exempt from the time limits regardless of the status of the assistance unit in which they live. However, the other members of the assistance unit are subject to the time limits unless exempt. B. Beginning and Ending Months of Time Limits 1. When an assistance unit loses an exemption from time limits, the time limits become effective the first full month after notice is provided. 2. When an assistance unit that is subject to time limits becomes exempt, the exemption from time limits becomes effective on the first full month after the change. Exemptions due to incapacity are effective on the date of the onset of the incapacity as determined by a health professional and approved by the Department. When an unemployable assistance unit loses the exemption due to employment for two consecutive months, the time limits become effective in the first month after the second consecutive month of employment. The pregnancy and postpartum exemption, described in A.3.f. above, begins and ends as indicated by the physician’s certification. The exemption for women whose pregnancy has ended, as described in A.3.g. above, begins on the date the pregnancy ends and continues until the end of the month that includes the sixth week after the pregnancy has ended.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 3-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-03 8540.03 page 3 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA

Subject: Exemptions from Time Limits 8540.03 C. Incapacity 1. To be considered incapacitated an adult must have a physical or mental illness or impairment, or combination of impairments of such debilitating nature that it eliminates the person's ability to engage in employment on a predictable basis with reasonable regularity. Such illness or impairment must be expected to last for at least thirty (30) days. 2. To be considered incapacitated, a child must have a physical or mental illness or impairment (or combination of impairments) of such debilitating nature that he or she requires parental care at unpredictable times with reasonable regularity or on a substantially continuous basis. Receipt of Supplemental Security Income or other Social Security benefits based on disability or blindness establishes incapacity. 4. Incapacity exemptions based on documented short-term, acute conditions (such as, but not limited to, a broken limb) are determined at the regional office level. Such exemptions are allowed for conditions expected to last no longer than three months. If the condition lasts beyond three months, the Department's Medical Review Team (MRT) must determine incapacity. 5. An adult is temporarily considered to be incapacitated if such adult claims to be incapacitated and has submitted documentation that such adult is unable to work for at least thirty days due to an incapacity and provided that the individual continues to cooperate with the Department in determining the incapacity. 6. The Department accepts documentation of a medical condition from any of the following sources within their scope of practice: licensed physicians; licensed osteopaths; licensed physician's assistants; licensed psychologists; licensed podiatrists; CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 3-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-03 8540.03 page 4 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA

Subject: Exemptions from Time Limits 8540.03 C. 6. Incapacity (continued) licensed optometrists: licensed chiropractors; licensed nurse practitioners; or licensed clinical social workers. Unemployability 1. Mandatory Employment Services participants who are not otherwise exempt from Employment Services are considered employable until the twentieth month of time-limited eligibility. 2. After the receipt of twenty (20) months of twenty-one month time limited benefits, the Department considers an individual to be unemployable if all of the following conditions are met: a. the individual is age forty (40) or older; and b. the individual is not employed at any level; and c. the individual meets all conditions necessary to grant an extension of twenty-one month time limited TFA benefits based on good faith effort (cross reference 8540.10); and d. the individual has not completed grade six (6); and e. the individual has not been employed more than six (6) months in the last five years. 3. An individual who has been determined to be unemployable in accordance with the criteria described in D.1. and D.2 above, is no longer considered to be unemployable if the individual enters and retains unsubsidized employment for a period of two (2) consecutive months.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8540.05 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Twenty-One Month Time Limit ______________________________________________________________________________

8540.05 A. General Provisions 1. Assistance units that have not reached the end of their sixty month time limit as described at 8540.12, are limited to twenty-one (21) months of TFA benefits, unless they are exempt from the time limits as described at 8540.03 or granted an extension to the twenty-one month time limit as described at 8540.10. This is a lifetime limit. 2. Any month in which an assistance unit is in suspended status is not counted toward the twenty-one month time limit. (cross reference 8565.15) 3. The number of time limited months used since January 1, 1996, by any TFA assistance unit count toward that unit's limit of twenty-one months of TFA benefits. 4. Except as provided below and described at 8540.10, adults, who have exhausted the twenty-one month time limit on benefits, do not qualify for additional benefits in a time limited assistance unit. 5. Expiration of the twenty-one month time limit does not preclude a person from receiving assistance as part of an assistance unit that is exempt from the time limit. Children who reapply as adults qualify for a new twenty-one month period of eligibility as adults. 7. For assistance units subject to time limits, the first month of twenty-one month time limited benefits is the first full month of eligibility for TFA, including time limited months used since January 1, 1996, pursuant to the AFDC waiver program (known as Reach for Jobs First). Any month in which an assistance unit received benefits in control group status is not counted.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8540.05 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Twenty-One Month Time Limit ______________________________________________________________________________

8540.05 B. Combining Assistance Units The following rules pertain to assistance units which are combined in accordance with assistance unit composition rules. (cross reference: 8540.25) 1. The following rules apply to individuals who join twenty-one month time limited assistance units: An individual who qualifies for assistance on her own, such as a pregnant woman, is treated as an assistance unit joining another assistance unit, rather than an individual joining an assistance unit. In this situation, rule number 2. below, which governs combining assistance units, is applied. b. An individual who does not qualify for assistance as an assistance unit on his or her own becomes subject to the twenty-one month time limit of the existing assistance unit except a non-parent who has exhausted the twenty-one month time limit. An individual who has exhausted the twenty-one month time limit is not eligible for benefits in the new assistance unit unless he or she is a parent of an assistance unit member. A parent who moves into an assistance unit containing his or her child and the other parent of the child, becomes subject to the twenty-one month time limit of that assistance unit. This rule even pertains when the parent who moves in has previously exhausted the twenty-one month time limit. e. When a parent moves into an assistance unit which contains his or her child and a non-parent caretaker relative, a new assistance unit is formed by the parent and child. The new assistance unit is subject to the twenty-one month time limit of the parent.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-01-16 8540.05 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Twenty-One Month Time Limit ______________________________________________________________________________

8540.05 B. Combining Assistance Units (continued) 2. When two assistance units combine into one, the following rules apply: a. If both assistance units were, or both assistance units were not receiving benefits in the month preceding the creation of the combined assistance unit, the new assistance unit assumes the twenty-one month time limit of the previous assistance unit with the longer time of eligibility of assistance remaining. b. If one assistance unit received benefits in the month preceding the creation of the combined assistance unit and one did not, the twenty-one month time limit of the active assistance unit applies to the new assistance unit. C. Assistance Units Which Separate If an assistance unit separates into two new assistance units in accordance with assistance unit composition rules, each with an adult from the previous assistance unit, the twenty-one month time limit of the original assistance unit applies to both of the new assistance units.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 1-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-02 8540.10 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Extension of Benefits Beyond Twenty-One Months ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.10 A. General Principles 1. In order to qualify for an extension of time limited benefits beyond twenty-one (21) months, an assistance unit must meet the income criteria in B. below, in addition to either the "good faith effort" provisions as outlined in D. below, or the "circumstances beyond one's control" provisions outlined in F. below. 2. In order to receive more than two extensions of time limited benefits beyond twenty-one (21) months, an assistance unit must meet the criteria listed in G. below, in addition to the provisions of A.1. above. 3. In order to be considered for an extension, assistance units must apply for an extension. 4. A request for an extension is a new application for benefits made in accordance with the rules of the Application Process except that when the extension request is made during the receipt of time limited benefits or during an extension, the standard of promptness for determining eligibility is thirty (30) days from the date of application. (cross reference: 8520.05) 5. Applications for extensions may be made no earlier than the twentieth (20) month of time limited assistance or the fifth (5) month of an extension. 6. The extension of benefits is not a continuation of the time-limited program, but rather a new, short-term benefit that begins only after the expiration of the twenty-one (21) month time limit or expiration of a previous extension. 7. Extensions are limited to periods of six (6) months at a time. 8. Extensions are ended prior to the sixth month of the extension when the assistance unit no longer meets all eligibility requirements for an extension. 9. In addition to the special eligibility provisions for an extension described in this subject, all other eligibility requirements of TFA must be met for an assistance unit to qualify for an extension. 10. Extensions need not immediately follow the end of the twenty-one (21) month period of eligibility or other extensions. They may be requested any time an assistance unit meets the criteria for qualifying for an extension, including after a period of time of not receiving benefits.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8540.10 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Extension of Benefits Beyond Twenty-One Months ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.10 B. Income Eligibility 1. To qualify for an extension, the total family income of all assistance unit members must be less than the appropriate Payment Standard that corresponds to the assistance unit's size. (cross reference: 8562.15) 2. In calculating the total family income of all assistance unit members, earnings of dependent children attending school is disregarded then, the total earned income minus $90 from the earnings of each employed person plus all other non-excluded income of the assistance unit is counted. 3. To calculate total family income of all assistance unit members, income is treated the same as in TFA, except income disregards do not apply. Income earned by an assistance unit member and total child support (including the disregard) is counted. 4. In calculating the amount of total family income, the amount of income deemed to the assistance unit, as provided by 8560.15, is included. 5. For each month of eligibility, the assistance unit must pass all other Income Eligibility tests that pertain to all TFA assistance units. (cross reference: 8565.10) C. Calculation of Benefits Once initial eligibility for an extension is determined, ongoing eligibility and benefits are calculated using the same method used for all other eligible time limited assistance units. (cross reference: 8565.15) D. Extensions Based on Good Faith Effort 1. Assistance units may satisfy the requirements for an extension upon demonstrating a good faith effort by substantially complying with all Employment Services requirements during the twenty-one (21) months of assistance and any time after twenty-one (21) months of time limited assistance, as provided in 2. below.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8540.10 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Extension of Benefits Beyond Twenty-One Months ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.10 D. Extensions Based on Good Faith Effort (continued) 2. Except as provided in E. below, a good faith effort to substantially comply with Employment Services requirements does not exist in any one of the following circumstances: a. Prior to the twenty-first (21) month of the time limit, but during receipt of time limited assistance, the assistance unit was penalized for failure to comply with Employment Services requirements more than one time; or b. During an extension a mandatory Employment Services participant failed to comply with any Employment Services requirement without good cause; or c. For active assistance units, in the last six (6) months of time limited assistance or during an extension, a mandatory Employment Services participant did not comply with program requirements without good cause in one of the following ways: (1) quit or reduced hours of suitable employment; or (2) refused to accept additional hours (up to 40 hours per week) of suitable employment; or (3) was fired from suitable employment for wilful misconduct; or (4) did not accept a bona fide offer of suitable employment. For inactive assistance units applying for an extension, within 120 days prior to the date of application, an assistance unit member who would not be exempt from Employment Services requirements in an active assistance unit, did not comply with one of the program requirements listed in c. above without good cause. 3. In determining eligibility for an extension as outlined in 2. a. above, only offenses committed without good cause after entry into the time limited program are considered.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-03-1 8540.10 page 4 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Extension of Benefits Beyond Twenty-One Months ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.10 E. Individual Performance Contracts 1. General Provisions a. Members of assistance units that become at risk of being ineligible for an extension during the first twenty (20) months of the twenty-one (21) month time limit as described in D, above, are given an opportunity to participate in an Individual Performance Contract (IPC), as described below. b. The IPC is a signed agreement between the participant and the Department designed to bring the recipient back into compliance with Employment Services requirements. c. IPCs may be offered at any time during the twenty-one month time limit. d. Based on an assessment, the Department develops the IPC with components that will lead to independence from TFA. The assessment will determine whether compliance can be met through the requirements of the existing Employment Services Plan or with new, revised or additional requirements. e. Components of the IPC include intensive short-term case management and may also include job training, job search, volunteer work, participation in parenting programs, counseling or any other requirements that will lead to independence from TFA benefits. f. The IPC is offered to the assistance unit as a method of restoring good faith effort. Assistance units are not required to take part in an IPC. An additional penalty is not imposed on an assistance unit for failing to comply with the terms of the IPC or refusing to take part in an IPC. g. An assistance unit member who has put the family at risk of being ineligible for an extension may restore good faith effort by securing and maintaining employment with income at or above the Payment Standard and complying with an IPC. For this purpose, the IPC may include a requirement of continued employment and removing barriers of continued employment.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-03-1 8540.10 page 5 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA Subject: Extension of Benefits Beyond Twenty-One Months ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.10 E. 2. Successfully Meeting the Requirements of an IPC a. If, by the end of the twenty-one (21) month time limit, the assistance unit is successfully meeting the requirements of the Individual Performance Contract and does not incur an additional penalty for non-compliance with Employment Services, the assistance unit is considered to meet the good faith effort criteria for qualifying for an extension. b. If an IPC cannot be completed by the end of the twenty-first month of time limited assistance, a determination is made as to whether the individual is making a good faith effort to successfully meet the requirements of the IPC: (1) as long as the individual is meeting the requirements of the IPC, he or she is considered to have restored good faith effort; (2) if the individual is not meeting the requirements, he or she has not restored good faith effort; c. For individuals who have not completed the IPC by the end of the twenty-first month, a good faith effort to successfully meet the requirements of the IPC means attaining specific goals of the IPC by a deadline specified in the IPC. Individuals granted an extension based on the presumption of restoration of good faith effort as described in b, above, must complete the requirements of the IPC during the first extension. If the individual does not complete the requirements, he or she has not restored good faith effort and does not qualify for an extension based on good faith effort. The current extension is ended immediately upon a determination that the individual has not successfully met the requirements of the IPC. The assistance unit does not qualify for any further extensions based on good faith effort Extensions Based on Circumstances Beyond One's Control 1. Subject to the conditions described below, regardless of past good faith efforts, assistance units may qualify for an extension if, due to circumstances beyond their control, all mandatory Employment Services participants are currently unable to obtain or maintain employment which, when combined with other family income, is at least the level described in B. above.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 1-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-02 8540.10 page 6 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Extension of Benefits Beyond Twenty-One Months ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.10 F. Extensions Based on Circumstances Beyond One's Control (continued) 2. Circumstances beyond one's control include special, unexpected events that happen to assistance unit members or other immediate family members. These circumstances may include, but are not limited to domestic violence or physical harm to the family's children. The events must be of a sufficient magnitude that they, in the opinion of the Department, reasonably prevent a mandatory Employment Services participant from working or working more hours when an extension is requested. 3. Circumstances beyond one's control do not include circumstances that may affect the general public as well as the assistance unit. These circumstances include, but are not limited to the following: a. a poor economy; b. lack of marketable job skills. 4. An assistance unit which qualifies for an extension based on circumstances beyond one's control must take steps, as determined by the Department, to overcome the barrier to employment caused by the circumstances which led to the extension. For victims of domestic violence, such steps may include seeking an order of protection, attending counseling or taking other actions to escape or prevent further violence, unless such actions would further the risk of continued or renewed violence. In order to qualify for an extension based on circumstances beyond one's control, the assistance unit must provide proof that such circumstances exist and that those circumstances prevent the person from maintaining or obtaining employment. G. Criteria to Receive More than Two (2) Extensions In addition to the criteria listed in A. through F. above, to receive more than two (2) extensions, each adult in the assistance unit who is a mandatory Employment Services participant must meet one or more of the following criteria:

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _____________________________________________________________________________ Date: 1/1/05 Transmittal: UP-05-02 8540.10 page 7 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Extension of Benefits Beyond Twenty-One Months ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.10 G. 1. Criteria to Receive More than Two (2) Extensions (continued) be precluded from obtaining or maintaining employment due to domestic violence or other circumstances beyond his or her control as defined in F. above; or b. be working thirty-five (35) or more hours per week, earning at least the minimum wage, and, after deducting $90 for employment expenses, earning less than his or her family’s Temporary Family Assistance payment standard; or be employed and working less than thirty-five (35) hours per week due to either of the following causes: (1) a documented medical impairment that limits the adult’s employment, provided he or she works the maximum number of hours that his or her medical condition permits; or the need to care for a disabled member of the adult’s household, provided the adult works the maximum number of hours that his or her care-giving responsibilities permit; or d. have two or more substantiated barriers to employment. A barrier to employment is a circumstance that reasonably interferes with a person’s ability to obtain or retain employment with earnings at or above the TFA payment standard. A barrier is substantiated when it is supported by documentation or, if documentation is not available, a credible statement from the client. Barriers to employment include the following: the lack of available childcare as defined in 8530.60 E.; substance abuse or addiction; serious mental or physical health problems; one or more learning disabilities; domestic violence; unavailability of transportation;

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _____________________________________________________________________________ Date: 1-1-05 Transmittal: UP-05-02 8540.10 page 8 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Extension of Benefits Beyond Twenty-One Months _____________________________________________________________________________ 8540.10 G. 1. d. Criteria to Receive More than Two (2) Extensions (continued) low English literacy (below the level of “Low Adult Secondary Education” as defined by the Department of Education); the existence of an open Department of Children and Families (DCF) case plan that requires the adult to engage in activities that are either in contradiction to his or her required employment services plan activities or that makes the adult unavailable to participate in his or her required employment services plan activities; a court order from juvenile or another court that requires parental involvement to such degree that it prevents the parent from complying with his or her required employment services activities; a child in the home who has a serious physical or behavioral health problem; or any other circumstance that reasonably interferes with the person’s ability to obtain or retain employment. Third or greater extensions shall not be ended prior to the end of the sixth month of the extension when the qualifying criteria listed in 1.a. through 1.d. above, cease to exist during the extension. Non-citizen status is not, by itself, considered a barrier to employment. H. Non-Cooperation During an Extension If, during an extension period, a mandatory Employment Services participant fails to comply with any Employment Services requirement without good cause: 1. the assistance unit becomes ineligible for the remainder of the extension; and 2. the assistance unit does not qualify for additional extensions based on good faith effort to comply.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8540.12 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________________ Subject: Sixty-Month Time Limit _______________________________________________________________________________ A. General Principle Assistance units that are not exempt from time limits as described at 8540.03 are subject to the sixty-month time limit regardless of how many months they received assistance under the twenty-one month limit as described at 8540.05 and extensions as described at 8540.10. Except as provided in D. below, when an individual described in B. below, has received sixty-months of time limited assistance, any time limited assistance unit they are part of is no longer eligible for TFA benefits. B. Assistance Units Subject to the Sixty-Month Time limit Except as provided in D. below, the sixty-month time limit is applied when a time limited assistance unit includes any of the following individuals who have received sixty months of time limited TFA assistance: an adult recipient; a minor parent who is the caretaker relative and who is not attending or has not completed high school or its equivalent; a minor parent who is the second parent of an eligible child in an assistance unit and who is not attending or has not completed high school or its equivalent. (This applies only when the other parent is the caretaker relative); an ineligible parent, including an ineligible minor parent as described in 2. and 3. above; or a disqualified individual, including a disqualified minor parent as described in 2. and 3. above. Counting Months of Assistance toward the Sixty-Month Limit Only benefits received on or after October 1, 1996 by time limited assistance units are counted toward the sixty-month time limit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8540.12 page 2 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _____________________________________________________________________ Subject: Sixty-Month Time Limit _______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.12 C. Counting Months of Assistance toward the Sixty-Month Limit (continued) Any month in which a benefit was received by a time limited assistance unit counts as a month of time limited assistance for any of the individuals described in B. above, who were part of the assistance unit when the benefit was received. Any month of benefits paid to an assistance unit that is exempt from the time limit is not counted toward the sixty-month time limit. When more than one person in the assistance unit is subject to the time limit as described in B. above, the number of time limited months of the person who received more months of time limited assistance is applied to the assistance unit. A month is counted toward the sixty-month time limit under the following circumstances: a. a TFA benefit is paid directly to the assistance unit; b. no direct TFA payment is made, but a payment to a third party is made on behalf of the assistance unit; c. no TFA payment is made, but an underpayment is used to reduce an overpayment to the assistance unit by the offset method; no TFA payment is made due to the recoupment of an overpayment to the assistance unit; or a benefit is paid from another state, U.S. territory or tribal nation if that benefit was counted by that other locality toward the sixty month limit of federal Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) benefits as required by the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 (PRWORA).

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-01-16 8540.12 page 3 Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _____________________________________________________________________ Subject: Sixty-Month Time Limit _______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.12 D. Exception to the Sixty-Month Time Limit 1. Assistance units experiencing domestic violence may receive benefits beyond the sixty-month time limit. An individual has experienced domestic violence if she or he has been subjected to any of the following: physical acts that resulted in, or threatened to result in, physical injury; sexual abuse; sexual activity involving a dependent child; being forced as the caretaker relative of a dependent child to engage in nonconsensual sexual acts or activities; threats of, or attempts at, physical or sexual abuse; mental abuse; or neglect or deprivation of medical care. To receive assistance beyond sixty months, domestic violence must, in the opinion of the Department, reasonably prevent or limit hours of employment of a mandatory Employment Services participant. 3. When, in the opinion of the Department, domestic violence is no longer a barrier to employment, the assistance unit no longer qualifies for time limited assistance beyond sixty months.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8540.15 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Eligible Children, Age Requirements and Pregnant Women ______________________________________________________________________________

8540.15 A. Eligible Child

1. In order to be eligible to receive TFA, an assistance unit must contain an eligible child or consist of a pregnant woman.

2. Children receiving SSI who would otherwise qualify for TFA are considered to meet this requirement and may allow a caretaker relative to qualify for assistance as described at 8540.25, C.

B. Ineligible Children

The following children are not eligible for the TFA program:

1. a child for whom federal, state or local foster care maintenance payments are made;

2. a child whose minor parent is a recipient of federal, state or local foster care maintenance payments;

3. a child who receives SSI benefits.

C. Age

The child meets the eligibility requirements of age if the child meets the following conditions:

1. has not attained 18 years of age; or

2. has not attained 19 years of age and is a full-time student in a secondary school or in the equivalent level of vocational or technical training.

D. Pregnancy

In order to qualify for assistance, a woman with no children receiving assistance must:

1. be pregnant; and

2. meet the eligibility factors which would be required if her child were already born and were living with her.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-2-12 Transmittal: UP-12-05 8540.20 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________________________ Subject: Convicted Drug Felons, Fleeing Felons, and Probation and Parole Violators _______________________________________________________________________________

8540.20 A. Convicted Drug Felons

1. An individual who has been convicted of any drug-related felony under federal or state law after August 22, 1996, is disqualified from TFA until the individual meets any of the following requirements:

a. such individual has completed a sentence imposed by any court of competent jurisdiction;

b. such individual is satisfactorily serving a sentence of probation; or

c. such individual is in the process of completing, or has completed, a court sentence of mandatory participation in a substance abuse treatment or testing program.

2. For purposes of this section, a drug-related felony means a felony that has as an element the possession, sue of distribution of a controlled substance, as such term is defined in 21 USC 802.

B. Fleeing Felons

1. Individuals who are fleeing to avoid prosecution for a crime, or attempt to commit a crime, which is a felony under the laws of the place from which they are fleeing are disqualified from TFA.

2. Individuals who are fleeing to avoid custody or confinement after conviction of a crime which is a felony under the laws of the place from which they are fleeing are disqualified from TFA.

3. The disqualifications established in this subsection shall not be applied to any individual beginning in the month after the President of the United States pardons the offense that led to the prosecution or conviction of such individual.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-2-12 Transmittal: UP-12-05 8540.20 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Convicted Drug Felons, Fleeing Felons, and Probation and Parole Violators

_________________________________________________________________________

8540.20 C. Parole and Probation Violators

1. If a parole officer, probation officer or court of competent jurisdiction determines that an individual is in violation of a condition of probation or parole imposed under state or federal law, such individual shall be disqualified from TFA.

2. The disqualification established in this subsection shall not be applied to any individual beginning the month after the President of the United States pardons the offense that led to the imposition of probation or parole or such individual.

D. Income and Assets of a Disqualified Parent

The needs of the disqualified parent are not considered in the determination of eligibility or the calculation of benefits for the remaining members of the assistance unit. However, assets and income are deemed from a disqualified drug- related felon, fleeing felon or parole or probation violator who is a parent of an eligible child on TFA. (Cross reference: 8550.20 and 8560.15)

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-04 Transmittal: UP-04-25 8540.22 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: No Show for Assessment Appointment or Interview ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.22 A. Requirement to Attend Assessment Appointment or Interview 1. All applicants and recipients who are mandatory employment services participants must appear for all scheduled assessment appointments or interviews related to the establishment of an employment plan. The penalty for failing to appear without good cause for any appointment or interview related to the establishment of an employment plan is ineligibility of the entire assistance unit. B. Ending the Penalty for Applicants 1. Applicants who are denied because they failed to appear, without good cause, for an appointment or interview at the Department of Labor related to assessment and completion of an employment plan may reapply for benefits at any time. However, the individual must attend the assessment interview and participate in the development of an employment plan before benefits are granted to the assistance unit. If a person reapplies within sixty (60) days of the most recent face-to-face intake interview, a new application must be completed, but a new face-to-face interview is not required. If a person reapplies after sixty (60) days from the most recent face-to-face intake interview, a new application must be completed and a new face-to-face interview is required. C. Ending the Penalty for Recipients 1. An assistance unit that was closed because they failed to appear, without good cause, for an appointment or interview at the Department of Labor related to assessment and completion of an employment plan may submit a new application for benefits at any time after the termination of benefits has occurred. However, the individual must attend the assessment interview and participate in the development of an employment plan before benefits are granted to the assistance unit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-04 Transmittal: UP-04-25 8540.22 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: No Show for Assessment Appointment or Interview ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.22 C. Ending the Penalty for Recipients (continued) If the individual completes the employment plan within thirty days from the date the department issued an adverse action notice the effective date of eligibility will be the month following the month of discontinuance providing all eligibility requirements are met. A new application is not required. If the individual does not attend a subsequently scheduled interview within thirty days from the date of the adverse action notice, a new application is required. The effective date of eligibility is the date of the new application if all eligibility requirements are met.

body:
CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES PRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8540.25 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Assistance Unit Composition ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.25 A. Mandatory Inclusions An assistance unit is a group of individuals who apply for or receive TFA together. The assistance unit must include certain individuals who reside together. It also may include certain other individuals who are in the home if they meet the eligibility requirements of TFA. The following are the rules of who must be members of an assistance unit. 1. The primary member of the TFA assistance unit is the child for whom assistance is requested or received. 2. Parents of an eligible child who live with the child must also be included in the child's assistance unit unless they are ineligible to be part of the assistance unit or disqualified from TFA. This is true even if assistance has not been requested for them. Income and assets of ineligible or disqualified parents are deemed to the assistance unit in accordance with deeming policy; however, the needs of the ineligible or disqualified parent are not considered in determining eligibility or calculating the benefits for the remaining members of the assistance unit. (cross reference: 8560.15 and 8550.20) 3. Siblings, adoptive siblings and half siblings who reside together and who meet the requirements of an eligible child, must be included in the same assistance unit unless the caretaker relative specifically chooses not to apply for such children. Siblings, adoptive siblings and half siblings who reside together and who are eligible children, cannot receive assistance in a separate assistance unit. (cross reference: 8540.15) B. Others Who May Be Included in the Assistance Unit 1. Other children in the household who are not siblings, adoptive siblings or half siblings of an eligible child who meet the eligibility requirements of the program have the option of being members of the same assistance unit or a separate assistance unit. 2. Other individuals in the household who are not mandatory inclusions in the child's assistance unit may choose to be included in the child's assistance unit or may choose to form their own assistance unit providing they meet the eligibility requirements for the program.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-01-16 8540.25 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Assistance Unit Composition ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.25 C. SSI Recipients 1. Recipients of Supplemental Security Income (SSI), are excluded from the assistance unit. 2. A child who receives SSI may be the basis of a TFA assistance unit even though this child is not eligible to be a recipient. If there are no other eligible children in the home for whom assistance is requested, the parent of that child is included as an assistance unit of one. D. Minor Parents 1. An eligible child who is also a parent or who is pregnant may not receive assistance as the caretaker relative of a separate assistance unit while living in his or her parent's home. He or she must be included as an eligible child in his or her parent's assistance unit. An eligible child who is also a parent or who is pregnant and who lives with a non‑parent caretaker relative may receive assistance in assistance units consisting of one of the following: If he or she has no siblings, adoptive siblings or half siblings in the home who are eligible children: he or she may receive assistance in an assistance unit that is separate from the caretaker relative’s assistance unit; or, he or she and her child may remain as members of the non‑parent caretaker's unit. If there are siblings, adoptive siblings or half siblings in the home, the non-parent must be the caretaker relative. 3. If the minor parent or minor pregnant woman chooses to create an assistance unit that is separate from the non-parent’s assistance unit, the non-parent must be the caretaker relative in the minor parent’s assistance unit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-01-16 8540.25 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Assistance Unit Composition ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.25 E. Non-Parent Caretaker Relatives 1. A non-parent caretaker relative may choose whether to apply for assistance on his or her own behalf as part of the assistance unit. Also, in order to be included in the assistance unit, the non-parent caretaker relative must be considered needy in accordance with the following: a. Income which would be excluded from an assistance unit member is excluded from the non-parent caretaker; b. A deduction for self-employment expenses is given; c. A deduction of $75 for personal expenses is allowed; d. The remainder is added to any unearned income, (including income deemed from the spouse); e. If the total exceeds the Standard of Need for one person, the non-parent caretaker is not included in the assistance unit; f. If the total is less than or equal to the Standard of Need, the non-parent caretaker may be added to the assistance unit and his or her income is counted the same as any other assistance unit member in determining eligibility and calculating the amount of benefit for the assistance unit. 2. Non-parent caretaker relatives who do not meet the requirements of 1, above, are not included in the assistance unit. Their needs are not taken into consideration, and their income and assets are not counted in determining eligibility or calculating benefits of TFA.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 9-1-03 Transmittal: UP-03-27 8540.30 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Living With a Caretaker Relative ______________________________________________________________________________

8540.30 A. Degree of Relationship

1. To be eligible for TFA, a child must be living with a caretaker relative who is a blood relative of any degree, adoptive relative, or a spouse or former spouse of a blood relative, or an individual appointed as the guardian of a minor by the court, or an individual who has applied for guardianship and is working with the court or the Department of Children and Families to be appointed the guardian of a minor.

2. The spouse of a blood relative is considered to be an acceptable degree of relationship even after the marriage is terminated by death or divorce.

3. Blood relatives are considered to be an acceptable degree of relationship even when the child is subsequently adopted by someone else, but lives with the blood relative.

B. Basic Provisions of the Requirement to Live With a Caretaker Relative

1. The child is meeting the requirement of living with the caretaker relative, provided the following conditions are met:

a. The caretaker relative is exercising responsibility for the continuous care and supervision of the child, even though the child or caretaker relative may be temporarily absent from the home; and

b. Such absence is no longer than ninety (90) consecutive days.

2. The child is considered to be living with the caretaker relative when the child continues to reside with the caretaker relative but is under the jurisdiction of the court, such as when the child is receiving probation services or protective supervision.

3. The child is considered to be living with the caretaker relative when the child continues to reside with the caretaker relative but legal custody is held by another agency.

4. The child is not considered to be living with the caretaker relative if either the child or the caretaker relative is absent from the home for longer than ninety (90) consecutive days, regardless of whether the caretaker relative is exercising responsibility for the continuous care and supervision of the child.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8540.30 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY

Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA

Subject: Living with a Caretaker Relative

8540.30 C. Requirement to Notify Department of Absence of a Child 1. If the child is absent from the home for more than ninety (90) days, the parent or caretaker relative must notify the Department of this within five (5) days from the date it becomes clear that the child will be absent for more than ninety (90) days.

If the parent or caretaker relative does not comply with the reporting requirement and does not have good cause for failing to report, he or she is disqualified from receiving benefits for six (6) months.

Good cause is considered to exist when circumstances beyond the individual’s control reasonably prevent him of her from complying with this requirement.

Determination of the Caretaker Relative

1. The parent is considered by the Department to be the caretaker relative if she or he is an adult living in the home with the child, except as provided in 2, below.

2. When both a parent and another relative who has been named guardian by a court of competent jurisdiction live in the home, the guardian is the caretaker relative. The parent is included on the award as a second adult.

3. When two adult parents are living in the home, either one may be the caretaker relative.

4. If more than one adult resides in the home, each of whom is related to the child but neither of whom is the parent, the caretaker relative is that relative who is most responsible for the day-to-day care and supervision of the child.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date:7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8540.35 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Minor Parents ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.35 A. General Requirements 1. To be eligible for assistance, a minor parent must live in the home of a parent, stepparent or legal guardian unless exempt from this requirement due to meeting any of the conditions listed in item C, below. 2. A minor parent who is exempt from living with his or her parent, stepparent or legal guardian, must live in other suitable living arrangements as described in E, below, unless exempt from this requirement as described in F, below. 3. A minor parent who is exempt from both the requirement to live with a parent, stepparent or legal guardian and the requirement to live in other suitable living arrangements may receive benefits on his or her own behalf. However, an authorized representative must be appointed to complete the eligibility process and act as representative payee for benefits paid to the assistance unit. B. Description of Minor Parent For the purposes of this subject, minor parent means an individual who: 1. is under age 18; and 2. is unmarried, or if married, is not living with his or her spouse; and 3. is living with his or her dependent child or is pregnant. C. Residing with a Parent, Stepparent or Legal Guardian To be eligible for TFA, a minor parent must live in the home of a parent, stepparent or legal guardian, unless exempt as described below: 1. The minor parent does not have a living parent, stepparent or legal guardian; or 2. The whereabouts of the minor parent's parent, stepparent or legal guardian are not known; or

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8540.35 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Minor Parents ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.35 C. Residing with a Parent, Stepparent or Legal Guardian (continued) 3. No parent, stepparent or legal guardian will allow the minor parent and/or the dependent child to live in his or her home; or 4. No parent, stepparent or legal guardian will assume or exercise responsibility for the care and control of the minor parent; or 5. The physical or emotional health or safety of the minor parent or dependent child would be jeopardized if they lived in the same residence with a parent, stepparent or legal guardian. D. Other Suitable Living Arrangements Minor parents and their children who are determined exempt from living with a parent, stepparent or legal guardian may still qualify for assistance if they live in other suitable living arrangements described in E, below, unless exempt as stated in F, below. E. Description of Other Suitable Living Arrangements 1. Other living arrangements, which are considered suitable, are limited to the following: a. an adult-supervised supportive living arrangement; or b. the home of an adult relative of the minor parent or dependent child. 2. Adult-supervised supportive living arrangements include the following: licensed facilities, such as foster homes and maternity homes; and b. family settings in which there is satisfactory evidence that demonstrates that the adult in the family assumes the primary care of the minor parent.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8540.35 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Minor Parents ______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.35 F. Exemptions from Other Suitable Living Arrangements A minor parent is exempt from the residing in other suitable living arrangements when any of the following circumstances apply: 1. There is no living adult relative and there is no available adult-supervised supportive living arrangement that meets the needs of the minor parent and/or dependent child; or 2. The whereabouts of any adult relative are unknown and there is no available adult-supervised supportive living arrangement that meets the needs of the minor parent and/or dependent child; or 3. No adult relative will allow the minor parent and/or the dependent child to live in his or her home and there is no available adult-supervised supportive living arrangement that meets the needs of the minor parent and/or dependent child; or 4. No adult relative will assume or exercise responsibility for the care and control of the minor parent and there is no available adult-supervised supportive living arrangement that meets the needs of the minor parent and/or dependent child; or 5. The physical and emotional health or safety of the minor parent or dependent child would be jeopardized if they lived in the same residence with any available and willing adult relative and there is no available adult-supervised supportive living arrangement that meets the needs of the minor parent and/or dependent child. G. Minor Parents Who May Reside Alone Minor parents who are determined exempt from both the requirement to live with a parent, stepparent or legal guardian and the requirement to reside with an adult relative or in an adult-supervised supportive living arrangement may qualify to receive assistance on their own behalf and on behalf of their child as the caretaker relative.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 10-1-01 Transmittal: UP-04-7 8540.35 page 4 _______________________________________________________________________________

Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY _______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _________________________________________________________________ Subject: Minor Parents _______________________________________________________________________________ 8540.35 H. Requirement to Have a Parent/Authorized Representative 1. Minor parents are not considered to be individuals qualified to complete eligibility processes or to receive the assistance payment on their own behalf and on behalf of their child unless the minor parent is exempt from both the requirement to live with a parent, stepparent or legal guardian and the requirement to reside with an adult relative or in an adult-supervised supportive living arrangement. However, a minor parent may file an application as described at 8520.05. An authorized representative or a parent with whom the minor parent lives must complete the eligibility processes and act as representative payee to receive assistance payments on behalf of the minor parent and child unless the minor parent is exempt from both the requirement to live with a parent, stepparent or legal guardian and the requirement to reside with an adult relative or in an adult-supervised supportive living arrangement. (cross reference: 8520.15) I. Requirement to Participate in an Educational Activity 1. In addition to meeting the requirements described in section A. though H. above, an unmarried minor parent who is without a high school diploma and cares for his or her child who is at least 12 weeks old must participate in a high school program that will lead to a diploma, or in an educational program directed toward attaining a high school diploma or its equivalent. Participation must be at least 20 hours per week if available. A minor parent not participating in a program described in 1. above, is not eligible for assistance but his or her child may receive assistance. 3. The ineligible minor parent described in number 2. above, is a disqualified member of the assistance unit. The minor parent's income and the income of the minor parent's parent are deemed to the assistance unit.

Federal Eligibility Requirements To be eligible for TFA, funded with federal TANF funds, an individual must be either a United States citizen or a non-citizen who is a lawfully residing immigrant. A lawfully residing immigrant is one who: 1. is admitted to the U.S. as a refugee under section 207 of the Immigration and Nationality Act; or 2. is granted asylum under section 208 of such act; or 3. has his or her deportation withheld under section 243(h) of such act (as in effect immediately before the effective date of section 307 of division C of Public Law 104-208) or section 241(b)(3) of such act (as amended by section 305(a) of division C of Public Law 104-208); or 4. is lawfully residing in the state and is: a. a veteran (as defined in section 101, 1101, or 1301, or as described in section 107 of title 38, United States Code) with a discharge characterized as an honorable discharge and not on account of alienage and who fulfills the minimum active-duty service requirements of section 5303A(d) of title 38 U.S.C.; or on active duty (other than active duty for training) in the Armed Forces of the United States; or the spouse or unmarried dependent child of an individual described in subparagraph a. or b.; or the unremarried surviving spouse of a deceased individual described in subparagraph a. or b. if the marriage fulfills the requirements of section 1304 of title 38, U.S.C.; or 5. is granted status as a Cuban and Haitian entrant under section 501 (e) of the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980; or

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8540.45 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Residency ______________________________________________________________________________

8540.45 A. Establishing Residency

1. To qualify for assistance, the assistance unit must reside in Connecticut, with the intent to remain in the state permanently or for the foreseeable future.

2. There is no durational residency requirement, except for certain non-citizens as described in 8540.40.

3. An otherwise eligible assistance unit who resides in Connecticut is not required to dwell in permanent housing or to have a fixed mailing address.

B. Temporary Absence

1. A temporary absence does not constitute abandonment of residency or interrupt continuity if intent to return is indicated once the purpose of the absence has been accomplished.

2. The following conditions must be met:

a. The individual must maintain permanent housing or have a fixed address in Connecticut.

b. The individual must intend to return to Connecticut within thirty (30) days of leaving.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8540.50 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Concurrent Assistance

______________________________________________________________________________

8540.50 A. Prohibition Against Receiving Concurrent Benefits

1. Individuals may not receive TFA concurrently with the following programs:

a. Old Age Assistance;

b. Aid to the Blind;

c. Aid to the Disabled;

d. SSI;

e. AFDC.

2. Individuals receiving TFA as a member of one assistance unit may not receive TFA as a member of the same or of another assistance unit simultaneously.

B. Collecting Benefits From Two or More States

1. A person found to have fraudulently represented his or her place of residence in order to receive assistance simultaneously from two or more states is disqualified for a period of ten (10) years. For the purposes of this subject, assistance means benefits provided through the Aid to Families with Dependent Children, Temporary Family Assistance, Medicaid, Food Stamps, and Supplemental Security Income programs.

2. Such finding of fraudulent receipt has to have been made through a conviction in federal or state court based upon allegations of misrepresentation of place of residence in order to receive assistance from two or more states simultaneously.

3. The period of disqualification begins on the date the individual is convicted in federal or state court.

4. The preceding prohibition shall not apply with respect to a conviction of an individual for any month beginning after the President of the United States grants a pardon with respect to the conduct which was the subject of the conviction.

8540.50 B. Collecting Benefits From Two or More States (continued)

5. The disqualification applies to the individual only. The eligibility of the remaining members of the assistance unit is determined separately from the disqualified individual. The needs of the disqualified individual are not taken into account in determining eligibility or calculating benefit amounts for the remaining members of the assistance unit.

6. If the disqualified individual is a parent of a child in the assistance unit, his or her income is deemed to the assistance unit in accordance with the provisions of 8560.15, F, and his or her assets are deemed to the assistance unit as required by 8550.20, D.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8540.55 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Striker Status ______________________________________________________________________________

8540.55 A. The penalty for participating in a strike only applies to applicants of TFA who go on strike prior to applying for assistance and are still on strike on the date of application for TFA. It does not apply if the assistance unit was eligible for and receiving assistance the day before the strike.

B. A penalty is imposed if any of the following individuals are applying for TFA and are participating in a strike:

1. a parent residing with a child applying for assistance even if the parent is ineligible or disqualified from assistance; or

2. any other adult applicant who would be an eligible member of the assistance unit.

C. An individual applying for TFA is considered to be participating in a strike in one of the following ways:

1. the individual does not go to work because he or she is a member of a bargaining unit on strike; or

2. he or she is one of a group of employees in a concerted work stoppage as a result of expiration of a collective bargaining agreement or some other reason directly related to the individual's job; or

3. he or she does not go to work in sympathy with the striking bargaining unit.

D. An individual is no longer considered a striker when his or her job has been permanently filled or permanently eliminated.

E. An individual is not considered to be a striker if he or she refuses to cross a picket line due to fear of personal injury or death, when the strike is not by his or her collective bargaining unit.

F. Penalties due to participation in a strike apply to applicants of TFA as follows:

1. When the striker is a natural or adoptive parent living in the home, the assistance unit is ineligible. This includes minor parent caretaker relatives.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8540.55 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Non-Financial Eligibility Requirements TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Striker Status

______________________________________________________________________________

8540.55 F. (continued)

2. When the striker is a non-parent caretaker relative:

a. the individual striker is ineligible for TFA;

b. assistance is given for the child or children only.

3. When the striker is a child or minor parent who is not a caretaker relative, there is no penalty.

G. The ineligibility period ends when the striker returns to work.
