CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-97-19 8565.15 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Income Eligibility and Benefit Calculation TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Calculation of Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8565.15 A. General Provisions

1. The total earned income of an assistance unit which passes the income eligibility test in a given month is disregarded when calculating benefits for that month.

2. Benefits are adjusted by prorating when an assistance unit or a member of the assistance unit is not entitled to a full month's payment. This occurs when benefits are calculated for the initial month of eligibility and for the month in which a new member is added to the assistance unit.

3. Rounding is performed after all other calculations, including prorating, have been completed. The monthly amount of benefit payments is always rounded down to a whole dollar.

4. Benefit payments are not issued for any payment month in which the assistance unit's benefit level is less than $10.00.

5. Assistance units with a benefit level of less than $10.00 are put in to suspended status. This means they are certified as eligible with all the rights and responsibilities of an eligible assistance unit, but no benefit is issued.

6. Assistance units that are not entitled to a benefit due to the receipt of child support income are put into suspended status until a determination of ongoing eligibility is made.

a. If it is determined that ineligibility will not be ongoing, the assistance unit is kept in suspended status until they are again entitled to a benefit.

b. If it is determined that ineligibility will continue for an ongoing and indefinite period, eligibility is ended.

7. When previous overpayments of benefits are being recouped through a grant reduction plan, the monthly amount being recouped is subtracted from the unrounded benefits amount. The remaining amount is rounded and issued as a benefit payment to the unit.

8. Fill-the-gap budgeting as described in B, below, is used to calculate benefits of assistance units who are not subject to the time limit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-97-19 8565.15 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Income Eligibility and Benefit Calculation TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Calculation of Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8565.15 B. Benefit Calculation of Time Limited Assistance Units

Benefits of assistance units which are subject to the time limit are computed in the following manner:

1. Earned income is disregarded.

2. Countable unearned income is added together.

3. Any Special Needs for which the assistance unit qualifies are added to the appropriate Payment Standard which corresponds to the assistance unit's size.

4. The total countable unearned income is subtracted from the total of the amount computed in 3, above.

5. The total is the assistance unit's Temporary Family Assistance benefit.

C. Benefit Calculation of Assistance Units Exempt from the Time Limit

Benefits of assistance units who are not subject to the time limits are computed in the following manner:

1. Earned income is disregarded.

2. Countable unearned income that is subject to fill-the-gap budgeting is added together. All sources of unearned income are subject to fill-the-gap budgeting, except the following:

a. General Assistance;

b. SAGA;

c. child support;

d. public assistance from another state.

3. The total unearned income from 2, above, is subtracted from the Standard of Need of the appropriate region and which corresponds to the assistance unit's size.

4. The remainder of 3, above is multiplied times 73%.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-97-19 8565.15 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Income Eligibility and Benefit Calculation TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Calculation of Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8565.15 C. Benefit Calculation of Assistance Units Exempt from the Time Limit (continued)

5. Any Special Needs for which the assistance unit qualifies are added to the product of 3, above.

6. Non fill-the-gap income, as described in 2, above, is subtracted from the total of 5, above.

7. The remainder is the assistance unit's Temporary Family Assistance benefit.

8570 This chapter outlines the regulations governing the delivery of benefits to or on behalf of assistance units who have been determined eligible to receive assistance from the Department. Benefit issuance refers to the form, frequency and method of providing benefits, to restrictions on the use of benefits, to benefit replacement, and to payee and mailing address requirements.

This chapter does not discuss the issue of eligibility or any rules dealing with determination of the benefit level.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 11-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-12 8570.05 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Form and Method ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.05 A. Form

1. Benefits for basic needs are issued to, or on behalf of, eligible assistance units in the form of cash payments, unless an exception applies. Benefits may be paid directly to the assistance unit, to an authorized representative as a protective payment, or to a third party as a vendor payment.

2. When payable directly to the assistance unit or to a protective payee, cash payments are issued in one of the following ways at the Department's discretion:

a. by Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) into an individual's personal checking or savings account; or

b. by Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) into an account at a financial institution in which the Department deposits funds and which the individual gains access through a Department issued debit card.

B. Unrestricted Payment Method

1. Unless otherwise stated by the provisions of this section, cash benefits are provided by the Department in a manner that does not restrict the recipient's control over the management of the benefits.

2. Individuals receiving cash assistance are allowed the freedom to manage their own financial affairs.

C. Restricted Payments

1. When it determines it necessary, the Department may limit the control that an assistance unit has over the management of cash benefits by providing assistance through a restricted payment method.

2. Restricted payments may be issued as vendor payments or as protective payments.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.05 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Form and Method ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.05 D. Where Benefits are Mailed

1. Program benefits issued in check form are mailed to the assistance unit's place of residence, unless the Department determines that benefits should be mailed to another address.

2. The Department may issue benefits by certified mail or require in- person pickup in the Regional Office.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _____________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.10 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Restricted Payment Methods ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.10 A. General Provisions

The Department issues restricted payments in two ways. Restricted payments may be made directly to a provider as a vendor payment as described in B, below, or to a person authorized to act as protective payee for the assistance unit as described in C, below.

B. Vendor Payments

The Department issues vendor payments for basic needs, Special Needs and Special Benefits as described below.

1. Basic Needs

a. At the request of the assistance unit, vendor rent payments to the current housing provider are made on behalf of the assistance unit under the following conditions:

(1) the assistance unit is ending a period in which restricted payments were made due to financial mismanagement in a particular living arrangement; and

(2) the monthly rental obligation of the assistance unit is equal to or less than 30% of the total monthly needs of the assistance unit; and

(3) the housing provider confirms that the assistance unit will not be evicted for non-payment of current or back rent during the period these payments are vendored by the Department; and

(4) the assistance unit makes the request for the vendor rent in writing.

b. When basic need payments are issued for rent as described in 1. a, above, the following rules apply:

(1) Vendor payments may be issued for both current rent and any arrearage that may exist; and

(2) The maximum amount paid each month on an arrearage cannot exceed $30.00.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _____________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.10 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Restricted Payment Methods ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.10 B. 1. Basic Needs (continued)

c. An involuntary vendor payment for basic needs, as described in C, below, may be made in cases where the Department has made a determination of financial mismanagement as described at 8570.15.

2. Special Needs

a. Except as provided in b, below, payments for Special Needs, as described at 8562.25 through 8562.80, may be made directly to the assistance unit or, in the following circumstances, to the vendor:

(1) when the assistance unit voluntarily requests, in writing, that the Department issue a Special Needs payment to the vendor; or

(2) in cases where the Department has made a determination of financial mismanagement as described at 8570.15.

b. Special Need payments for Emergency Housing, as described at 8562.30, are always issued through the vendor payment method. Emergency Housing payments are never made directly to the assistance unit.

3. Special Benefits

All payments for Special Benefits, as described at 8590, are issued to the vendor, except when the payment is a reimbursement to the assistance unit for an expense which the unit has already paid out of its own funds. In that case, the payment is made to the assistance unit.

C. Protective Payments

1. Benefits may be issued in the form of protective payments in cases where the Department has made a determination of financial mismanagement as described at 8570.15.

2. Benefits for a minor parent and his or her child are paid to the minor parent's parent or authorized representative, unless the minor parent is exempted from the requirement of living with an adult relative or in an adult supervised supportive living arrangement and there is no other reason to require a protective payee. (cross reference: 8540.35)

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _____________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.15 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Cases Involving Financial Mismanagement ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.15 A. Determining Financial Mismanagement

1. The Department considers financial mismanagement to exist when, in the opinion of the Department, a caretaker relative has demonstrated such an inability to manage funds that:

a. payments to the relative have not been or are not currently being used in the best interest of the child; and

b. allowing the relative to continue to manage the TFA benefits represents a threat to the health or safety of the child.

B. Vendor Rent Payments

The following provisions are established for making vendor rent payments to the housing provider when mismanagement is determined.

1. Vendor rent payments are made to the permanent housing provider for the actual amount owed for the current month by the unit for housing, up to the lower of the following:

a. the total of thirty (30) percent of the basic need standard for an assistance unit of equal size with zero applied income; or

b. the amount of the unit's benefit.

2. Rent payments are vendored to the housing provider on the condition that the provider signs a statement agreeing:

a. to notify the Department of the initiation of eviction proceedings involving a unit for whom vendor payments are made;

b. not to evict a unit solely because of a delinquent payment of a vendor rent by the Department;

c. not to assess the recipient, either directly or through his or her agent, for late fees, legal fees or court costs pursuant to delinquent payments from the Department.

3. Vendor rent payments are diverted to someone other than the housing provider when there is a statute or court order authorizing it.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.15 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Cases Involving Financial Mismanagement ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.15 B. Vendor Rent Payments (continued)

4. This provision creates no rights for landlords. Vendor rent payments are made to landlords in accordance with the above provisions only if the assistance unit is eligible for assistance, resides in the unit and was subject to vendor rent.

C. Continuance or Discontinuance of Restricted Payments

1. Restricted payments may continue for a period not to exceed twenty-four (24) months.

2. Restricted payments are discontinued in less than twenty-four (24) months:

a. when the recipient demonstrates an increased ability to manage funds to such extent that the health or safety of the individual or child is no longer threatened; or

b. if a guardian or legal representative is appointed.

3. The Department may initiate and continue rental arrearage payments during a period of financial mismanagement upon written request of the assistance unit or the housing provider and continues the payments until:

a. there is a request to discontinue the payments from the assistance unit, legal representative, or conservator; or

b. the assistance unit moves from the permanent housing arrangement or there is a request from the housing provider to discontinue the payments for reasons other than non-payment of the vendor from the Department.

4. The Department continues payment for rental arrearage if requested by the assistance unit following a period of vendor payment due to mismanagement.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.15 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Cases Involving Financial Mismanagement ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.15 D. Selection of a Guardian or Legal Representative

The Department seeks judicial appointment of a guardian or conservator if:

1. the need for restricted payments will continue or is likely to continue beyond two (2) years because efforts have not resulted in a sufficiently improved ability of the recipient to manage funds; or

2. the physical or mental condition of the recipient is such that the appointment of a legal representative is immediately essential.

E. Notification

1. Assistance units are informed in writing of requests for vendor payments which are received by the Department from a creditor and are allowed a ten (10) day period in which to provide rebutting information.

2. Prior to making a restricted payment the Department informally notifies the assistance unit of its intention to initiate restricted payments and the reasons therefore. The assistance unit is given the opportunity to informally contest the proposed use of restricted benefit payments by making oral or written statements to Department. The Department considers any statement made by the assistance unit before issuing its formal determination regarding the restricted payments.

3. The Department provides written notification to the recipient when a decision is made to institute restricted payments or to continue such payments following a twelve (12) month review.

F. Fair Hearings

1. The Department may initiate or continue to make restricted payments while a Fair Hearing decision is pending on the restricted payment issue.

2. If a Fair Hearing decision rules that the individual did not mismanage his or her funds and rent was withheld from a landlord because the residence was uninhabitable, the Department issues a corrective payment to the assistance unit in the amount that was inappropriately diverted to the landlord.

8570.20 A. In most cases the payee is the adult caretaker relative of the assistance unit in whose name assistance is claimed. However, in some situations the payee may be someone other than the head of the assistance unit.

B. The Department has the authority to appoint a payee.

C. The following individuals are eligible payees of cash assistance payments:

1. the parent, guardian or other adult relative of a minor parent under this program when the minor parent lives with this individual.

2. the minor parent when:

a. he or she is exempt from the requirement of living in a specified living arrangement; (cross reference: 8540.35) or

b. when the Department determines that the parent, legal guardian, or other adult does not meet the requirements for protective payee.

3. the caretaker relative of a child or other adult member of the assistance unit;

4. a pregnant woman who is 18 years of age or older;

5. a vendor when payment for goods, services or other items is issued to the provider;

6. a protective payee.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.25 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Protective Payees in Restricted Payment Cases ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.25 A. Role of Protective Payee

1. A protective payee is an authorized representative of the assistance unit, as described at 8520.15, designated by the Department to receive and discharge cash benefits on behalf of an assistance unit in which he or she is not a member, a guardian, or a caretaker relative.

2. The protective payee has the responsibility to assure that assistance payments made on behalf of the assistance unit are used solely on behalf of and in the best interest of the assistance unit members.

3. The protective payee's responsibilities are defined in writing in a protective payment plan and a copy is given to both the payee and the recipient.

4. The protective payment plan must be signed by the protective payee and notarized.

B. Protective Payee Selection Criteria

1. Selection of a protective payee is made with the participation and consent of the recipient to the greatest extent possible. However, in the cases of financial mismanagement or when the assistance unit is headed by a minor parent, the Department may select the protective payee solely on the basis of its own determinations and to appoint a new protective payee when required. This is done when the caretaker relative is unwilling or unable to assist the Department in selecting a protective payee.

2. The protective payee must meet the following qualifications:

a. have an interest or concern in the welfare of the assistance unit other than ordinary friendship or neighborly concern;

b. possess the ability to manage funds in an effective manner;

c. be available to work with the head of the assistance unit in household planning, budgeting and home management problems;

d. be capable of establishing or maintaining a good working relationship with the assistance unit members;

e. be a responsible and dependable individual with good character reference.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.25 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Protective Payees in Restricted Payment Cases ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.25 B. Who may not be a Protective Payee

A protective payee may not be:

1. an employee of the Department, unless that employee is duly delegated to serve as a conservator by the Commissioner of the Department of Social Services (DSS);

2. a staff member of a public or private agency or organization who:

a. determines financial eligibility for the assistance unit; or

b. performs investigative or resource duties; or

c. handles fiscal processes related to the assistance unit;

3. landlords, grocers, or other vendors of goods, services or other items dealing directly with the assistance unit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 11-1-07 Transmittal: UP-07-14 8570.30 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Use of Cash Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.30 A. Expiration Date

1. Cash payments issued in check form expire three calendar months to the day following the date of the check.

2. Benefits checks cannot be transacted after the expiration date.

3. Benefits directly deposited into a personal account in a financial institution can be accessed at any time as long as the account in the financial institution has not been closed.

4. Benefits deposited into an EBT credit account in a financial institution can be accessed any time as long as the account has not defaulted to an inactive account.

B. Expunged Benefits

Benefits will be expunged 270 days after deposit if no withdrawals have been made during that period.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES

UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL

Date: 1-1-14 Transmittal: 14-05 8570.32

Section: Jobs First Type: POLICY

Chapter: Benefit Issuance Program: TFA

Subject: Restriction on Use of Cash Benefits

A. Definitions

For purposes of this section, the following definitions shall apply:

1. “Adult-oriented entertainment establishment” means a venue in which performers disrobe or perform in an unclothed state for the patrons’ entertainment and that restricts admission to adults;

2. “Casino, gambling casino or gaming establishment” means an off-track betting branch facility authorized pursuant to section 12-571a of the Connecticut General Statutes or a gaming facility as defined in section 30-37k(a)(2) of the Connecticut General Statutes, but does not include an establishment that offers casino, gambling or gaming activities incidental to the principal purpose of the business;

3. “Electronic benefit transfer transaction” or “EBT transaction” has the same meaning as provided in 42 USC 608(a)(12)(B)(iii); and

4. “Liquor store” means an establishment with a package store permit issued pursuant to subsection (a) of section 30-20 of the Connecticut General Statutes.

B. Restriction on Use of Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) Card

No person receiving cash assistance under the Temporary Family Assistance (TFA) program shall conduct an electronic benefit transfer transaction involving such cash assistance in a liquor store, adult-oriented entertainment establishment or casino, gambling casino or gaming establishment.

C. Penalties for Failure to Comply with Restriction

1. Any person receiving cash assistance through the TFA program who uses an EBT card in violation of section 8570.32 B shall be subject to the following penalties:

a. For the first violation, a warning that a prohibited transaction occurred;

b. For the second violation, a penalty in the amount of the EBT transaction that occurred at the prohibited location;

c. For the third violation, a penalty of one month’s suspension of the head of household’s TFA benefits, in addition to the amount of the EBT transaction that occurred in the prohibited location; and

d. For the fourth violation, the Department, at its discretion, may suspend the head of household’s TFA benefits for any length of time that the Department determines to be appropriate or may terminate the head of household’s TFA benefits permanently.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES

UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL

Date: 1-1-14 Transmittal: 14-05 8570.32 page 2

Section: Jobs First Type: POLICY

Chapter: Benefit Issuance Program: TFA

Subject: Restriction on Use of Cash Benefits

2. The Department shall construe all prohibited transactions that occur during the same calendar month as one cumulative transaction constituting a single violation.

3. For purposes of calculating a suspension penalty under section 8570.32 C.1.c or section 8570.32 C.1.d, the Department shall reduce the assistance unit size by one member for the period of time that the suspension is in effect.

4. Whenever a penalty is imposed under section 8570.32 C, the Department may appoint a protective payee pursuant to section 8570.25 of the UPM, based on financial mismanagement of TFA cash assistance, as described in section 8570.15 of the UPM.

5. The Department shall provide any person subject to a penalty under this section, which penalty causes a reduction, suspension or loss of benefits, with at least ten days advance notice before imposing such penalty.

6. Individuals who are notified that the Department intends to impose a penalty pursuant to this section, including a warning that a prohibited transaction has occurred, shall have the right to a hearing to contest the penalty in accordance with section 8525.05 of the UPM.

D. Notification of Policy

The Department shall provide TFA cash assistance recipients with information about the restrictions and penalties established in this section before imposing any of the penalties set forth in section 8570.32 C.1.

E. Enforcement of Penalty Provisions

The Department may audit the EBT transaction history of TFA recipients and such other evidence as necessary to ensure compliance with the restrictions set forth in this section.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.35 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Frequency and Composition ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.35 A. Frequency

1. The Department issues basic needs and recurring Special Needs benefits on a scheduled basis at regular intervals in accordance with a schedule of payments published by the Department and available to the public.

2. Non-recurring Special Needs are issued as supplemental payments as needed.

B. Composition

1. Payments which supplement basic and recurring Special Needs benefits may be issued as separate payments, or in combination as a consolidated scheduled or supplemental payment.

2. Benefits provided in the same form, but under different assistance programs, may be combined and issued as a consolidated payment.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.40 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Benefit Replacement ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.40 A. Conditions of Benefit Replacement

1. Subject to the limitations of this chapter, the Department authorizes the replacement of:

a. original or replacement benefit checks that have been issued to or on behalf of eligible assistance units, and which have been subsequently lost, stolen, destroyed, or mutilated (cross reference 8570.45, 8570.50 and 8570.52); or

b. EBT issued benefits that are considered stolen or lost (cross reference: 8570.45 and 8570.50); or

c. direct deposit benefits that were not deposited into a payee's electronic fund transfer account due to a technical error or problem and the financial institution has notified the Department that the non-deposited benefits will be credited to the Department; or

d. benefits which have been misused by the protective payee, rendering them unavailable to meet the needs of the assistance unit (cross reference: 8570.55).

2. No distinction is made with regard to whether the benefit check became unavailable prior to, or subsequent to, receipt. Benefit checks are subject to replacement in either case.

3. The Department does not provide replacement benefits for checks that have been:

a. cashed by the payee unless the payee was a protective payee who has misused benefits, or

b. endorsed by the payee prior to being lost or stolen.

4. The Department does not provide the replacement of EBT issued cash benefits that were received by an individual who was given the client's debit card and PIN unless the benefits were accessed by a protective payee and the protective payee has misused the benefits by not expending them on behalf of the assistance unit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-97-19 8570.40 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Benefit Replacement ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.40 B. Amount of Replacement Benefits

1. Unless otherwise stated, the amount of replacement benefits authorized is equal to the amount of the original benefit.

2. The Department replaces only those benefits that were correctly authorized and issued.

3. The Department does not offset the cost of replacement benefits against the balance of an outstanding claim against the assistance unit.

C. Receipt of Benefits

1. Benefit checks have been received as long as the payee, or an individual acting on behalf of the payee, had possession of the benefit at any time after it was issued by the Department.

2. Cash benefits are considered to have been received as long as they were deposited into the payee's electronic fund transfer account or an EBT account.

D. Request for Replacement

1. The date of the request for a replacement of a benefit is considered to be the date that an appropriate request for replacement benefits is received by the Department or its designee.

2. Requests for replacement of cash payments issued in check form must be made in writing using a notarized affidavit.

3. Requests for replacement of cash payments that are issued via direct deposit into a payee's electronic fund transfer account may be made by telephone.

4. Requests for replacement of lost EBT issued benefits may be made by telephone. Requests for replacement of stolen EBT issued benefits must be in writing using a notarized affidavit.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.40 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Benefit Replacement ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.40 E. Cost

The Department charges a fee equal to the cost of replacement of a Department issued debit card when replacement is requested because the original card was lost by the assistance unit.

F. In-Office Visit

1. Assistance units are required to appear in person at the appropriate Regional Office to complete an affidavit when requesting replacement of checks or cash benefits deposited into an EBT account in a financial institution that are considered to have been lost or stolen.

2. The requirement may be waived only if the payee is elderly or disabled, and unable to appear for an in-office visit because of severe incapacity.

3. If the requirement is waived, the Department may conduct a home visit or have the affidavit mailed and privately notarized.

4. If a home visit is selected, it is scheduled within three (3) business days of the date of the request.

5. The Department is not responsible for delays in issuing replacement benefits which are caused by waiver of the in-office visit requirement.

G. Who Requests Replacement

1. The following individuals are eligible to request replacement benefits:

a. the payee of the original benefit;

b. the head of the assistance unit if the original benefit was issued to a protective payee accused of misusing benefits.

2. If a new payee is appointed prior to the expiration date of the original benefit, the new payee can request replacement of the original benefits.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.40 page 4 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Benefit Replacement ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.40 H. Issuance of EBT Debit Cards

1. Debit cards are issued at the time the household is eligible to receive benefits.

2. Replacement of debit cards is limited to instances of:

a. loss;

b. theft;

c. mutilation or destruction;

d. demagnetization of magnetic stripe;

e. changes in the authorized representative;

f. changes in the head of household;

g. changes in the protective payee.

3. EBT debit cards are replaced with in three (3) business days following the day the Department is notified by the household that a new debit card is needed.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.45 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Replacement of Lost Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.45 A. TFA benefit checks are treated as lost benefits if:

1. the check is missing prior to receipt and there is no evidence that it has been stolen; or

2. the check was misplaced after receipt but before being cashed or endorsed.

B. EFT issued benefits are treated as lost benefits if they are not accepted into the client's electronic fund transfer account.

C. EBT issued cash benefits are treated as lost benefits if they are not accepted into an EBT account of an eligible client due to Department error or a malfunction of the electronic benefits transfer system.

D. Cash benefits that have been misused by a protective payee are considered to be lost benefits for replacement purposes.

E. Lost TFA benefits which have been replaced, but are later recovered, must be returned to the agency. If both the original and replacement benefits are used by the assistance unit, an overpayment exists which is subject to recoupment and possible intentional client error penalties. (cross reference: 8580)

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.50 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Replacement of Stolen Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.50 A. Provisions

1. TFA benefit checks are treated as stolen benefits if the Department or person authorized to use the benefits has knowledge or reason to suspect that the check has been misappropriated by someone other than:

a. the payee of the benefits;

b. an assistance unit member who was not the payee, or an authorized representative who continues to reside in the household after the benefits are stolen.

2. TFA benefit checks that are taken by an assistance unit member who leaves the household after misappropriating the benefits are treated as stolen benefits as long as the assistant unit member was not authorized to use them.

3. EBT issued cash benefits are treated as stolen benefits if the cash benefits are taken by someone other than the client, or the client's authorized representative between the time the Department's designee receives notice from a household regarding the need for card replacement and the time that the Department's designee deactivates the client's stolen or lost debit card.

4. The individual requesting a replacement of a stolen cash payment must file a police report as a condition of receiving a replacement.

B. Benefits Not Replaced

1. The Department does not provide replacement benefits if the original check is taken by the payee or other authorized person, or by an assistance unit member who continues to reside in the household. Such benefits are considered to have been properly received and are not subject to replacement.

2. The Department does not replace recipient benefits that have been correctly deposited into a client's personal account in a financial institution, except when such benefits have been accessed and misused by a protective payee. Such benefits are considered to have been properly received and are not subject to replacement except as provided in this chapter.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.50 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Replacement of Stolen Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.50 B. Benefits Not Replaced (continued)

3. The Department does not replace stolen cash.

4. The Department does not replace proceeds from a stolen check that was previously endorsed by the client.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES PRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.52 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Destroyed or Mutilated Benefits ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.52 A. Provisions

1. TFA benefit checks are treated as destroyed benefits if they are damaged in a natural or man-made disaster, such as a fire, flood or other event, and are rendered useless or unavailable.

2. TFA benefit checks are treated as mutilated benefits if:

a. They have been improperly manufactured; or

b. They are damaged by an event other than a natural or man-made disaster.

3. Mutilated TFA benefit checks must be recognizable. Checks mutilated to such extent that they are not identifiable are not considered as mutilated benefits for replacement purposes. However, they may be considered destroyed benefits if they meet the provisions of 1, above.

B. Documentation of a Disaster

No benefits may be issued until verification of the disaster is obtained through a collateral contact with a state, or local community organization, or through a home visit as a condition of replacement.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.55 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Replacement of Benefits Misused By a Protective Payee ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.55 A. What Constitutes Misuse

Benefits have been misused by the protective payee if:

1. benefits issued on behalf of the assistance unit have been withheld or used by the payee for a purpose other than to meet the financial obligations of the assistance unit; and

2. the benefits are not accessible to the assistance unit; and

3. the payee acted without the knowledge and approval of the assistance unit.

B. Investigating and Documenting the Allegation

1. Allegations of misuse of benefits by a protective payee must be documented in a sworn statement.

2. The Department conducts an investigation into the alleged misuse of benefits.

3. The protective payee is given the opportunity to refute the allegation or to make available the benefits in question.

C. Authorization of Replacement Benefits

1. Replacement benefits are authorized if:

a. the protective payee fails to produce evidence that refutes the allegation of misuse; and

b. evidence gathered during the investigation supports the allegation of misuse; and

c. it is determined that the protective payee acted without the knowledge and approval of the assistance unit in spending money in ways other than on behalf of the assistance unit.

2. Replacement benefits are issued directly to the assistance unit or to a newly appointed protective payee.

D. Limitations

Replacement benefits are authorized only for that portion of the cash payment that is misspent or is inaccessible.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.60 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Benefit Replacement - Dates of Filing and Processing Standards ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.60 A. Earliest Date for Filing Replacement Requests

1. The earliest date for requesting replacement due to non-receipt of a benefit check is the fourth post office working day after the mailing date.

2. The earliest date for requesting replacement due to non-deposit of a cash payment into an account in a financial institution is the same day as the benefits were scheduled to be available to the clients.

3. Requests for replacement of benefit checks can be filed immediately if the checks have been received and the checks are subsequently lost, stolen, destroyed or mutilated.

4. Requests for replacement of cash benefits can be filed immediately if benefits are stolen subsequent to the reporting of a lost or stolen debit card.

B. Last Date for Filing Replacement Requests

1. Replacement of benefit checks must be requested prior to the expiration date of the benefit check.

2. Replacement of benefits considered to be lost because they were not correctly deposited into an EBT account or an individual's account in a financial institution must be requested within three (3) months of the date the benefits should have been deposited.

3. Replacement of EBT issued benefits that are considered to be stolen because they were taken from the individual's EBT account between the time the individual reported a lost or stolen card and the time the Department's designee deactivated the individual's account, must be requested within three (3) months of the date a report is filed with the Department designee.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8570.60 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Issuance TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Benefit Replacement - Dates of Filing and Processing Standards ______________________________________________________________________________

8570.60 C. Processing a Request for a Benefit Replacement

1. A request for a benefit replacement is processed with reasonable promptness, depending on the circumstances of each case and time necessary for the Department to take the following action:

a. determine whether the initial benefit check has been cashed and, if so, the identity of the individual who cashed the check and his or her relationship (if any) to the payee of the check; and

b. put a stop payment order on the check;

c. make a preliminary investigation of possible client fraud, if warranted by the information available to the Department.

2. Notwithstanding the provisions of 1, above, the Department makes a determination of whether or not to issue a benefit replacement no later than fourteen (14) working days after the request for replacement.

8580 This chapter describes the process by which the Department corrects errors made in issuing benefits to an assistance unit. The process includes:

° General Principles

° Underpayments

° Overpayments

° Recoupment

° Treatment of Intentional Recipient Error

° Disqualification Periods and Penalties

body:
CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES PRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8580.10 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Error TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: General Principles ______________________________________________________________________________

8580.10 A. The Department determines the accuracy of all benefit payments.

B. The Department computes the amount of the error by comparing the amount of the benefits the assistance unit should have received to the amount of the benefits the assistance unit actually did receive for a particular month or series of months.

C. The Department notifies the assistance unit before taking any action to correct an error.

D. The Department attempts to correct the error as quickly as possible without causing undue hardship to the assistance unit.

E. If the error is an underpayment the Department issues a corrective payment to or on behalf of the assistance unit whether the case is active or closed.

F. If the error is an overpayment, the Department recoups by one or more methods, after discussing the overpayment with the assistance unit and obtaining an agreement from the unit as to the method of recoupment that will be employed, if possible.

G. The Department may recoup overpayments made under the AFDC program as well as those made under TFA from TFA assistance units.

H. The Department classifies errors as agency, recipient or provider caused.

1. Agency errors include, but are not limited to:

a. failing to take timely action on a reported change or failing to insure that the assistance unit fulfilled certain eligibility requirements;

b. making incorrect computations, data entries or other processing errors.

2. Recipient errors which cause overpayments are either intentional or unintentional.

a. Unintentional recipient error may occur when the assistance unit has good cause for failing to make a timely report. Good cause is a circumstance beyond the control of the assistance unit which reasonably prevents the assistance unit from making a timely report.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8580.10 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Error TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: General Principles ______________________________________________________________________________

8580.10 H. 2. b. Intentional recipient error occurs if:

(1) the assistance unit fails without good cause to report a change affecting eligibility in a timely manner; or

(2) the assistance unit knowingly misinforms the Department regarding information affecting eligibility; or

(3) the assistance unit commits an illegal act such as cashing a duplicate check after falsely claiming non-receipt of the first check; or

(4) the assistance unit or its authorized representative withdraws cash from the EBT account after they notify the Department that they need a new debit card and before the time the Department's designee deactivates the card.

I. The Department attempts to recoup all overpayments, regardless of when the overpayment occurred, and regardless of whether the assistance unit is still intact or receiving TFA.

J. If an overpayment is caused by the assistance unit, the Department makes a determination regarding whether the error was intentional or unintentional, and whether to pursue a legal action against the assistance unit on fraud charges.

K. The Department takes action against the provider, if benefits paid to the provider on behalf of the assistance unit are overpaid due to a provider error.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _____________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-97-19 8580.20 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Error TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Underpayments ______________________________________________________________________________

8580.20 A. If the Department discovers an underpayment has occurred the Department investigates the following before issuing a corrective payment:

1. whether the assistance unit has received an overpayment during the time period containing the underpayment; and

2. whether the unit has received any other documented overpayments which have not yet been recouped.

B. If an overpayment and an underpayment have occurred for the same assistance unit, the Department offsets the amount of the overpayment against that of the underpayment.

C. If the amount of the underpayment exceeds that of the overpayment, and the assistance unit is eligible for a corrective payment, the Department issues to the unit a corrective payment which is equal to the difference between the underpayment and the overpayment.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL _____________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8580.30 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Temporary Family Assistance POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Error TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Overpayments ______________________________________________________________________________

8580.30 Determination of an Overpayment

A. Upon discovery of an overpayment the Department takes one or more of the recoupment actions described at 8580.40.

B. If an overpayment and an underpayment have occurred for the same assistance unit, the Department offsets the amount of the overpayment against that of the underpayment.

C. If the amount of the overpayment is greater than that of the underpayment, the offset is used to reduce the amount the Department recoups from the assistance unit.

D. When the Department determines that an overpayment was a result of an intentional program violation, in addition to recoupment, the Department may initiate disqualification and/or refer the case for criminal prosecution and/or refer the case to the Office of the Attorney General for civil recovery.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8580.40 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Error TFA ____________________________________________________________ Subject: Recoupment ______________________________________________________________________________

8580.40 A. Subject of Recoupment Actions

1. Recoupment is recovery of benefits which were overpaid to an assistance unit. The Department recoups from any member of the assistance unit which received the overpayment.

2. If the Department is unable to recoup from the overpaid assistance unit, it recoups from:

a. another assistance unit if this unit now contains any individual who was a member of the overpaid assistance unit; or

b. an individual member of an overpaid assistance unit, regardless of whether this individual is now receiving benefits.

3. The amount of restitution ordered by a court in a criminal proceeding does not extinguish the assistance unit's obligation to repay the entire amount of the overpayment.

B. Recoupment Methods

The Department recoups by using one or more of the following methods:

1. Lump-Sum Recoupment

a. Lump-sum recoupment means collecting the total overpayment in one single payment from an assistance unit.

b. The Department recoups by this method if the assistance unit chooses and has income or assets sufficient to make the lump-sum payment.

2. Installment Recoupment

a. Installment recoupment means repayment of an overpayment according to a monthly schedule of payments at a set rate.

b. The Department recoups by this method if the assistance unit chooses this method of repayment.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8580.40 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Error TFA ____________________________________________________________ Subject: Recoupment ______________________________________________________________________________

8580.40 B. 2. Installment Recoupment (continued)

c. For an active assistance unit, the rate of the monthly installment payments cannot be greater than the rate determined in accordance with the provisions of D, below.

d. For a discontinued unit, the rate of the monthly installment payment is equal the rate determined in accordance with the provisions of D, below.

3. Grant Reduction Recoupment

a. Grant reduction recoupment means withholding a portion of ongoing TFA benefit payments at a given rate to repay an overpayment.

b. The Department generally recoups by this method for an active assistance unit that is unwilling or unable to repay by either of the other two repayment options.

c. If an active assistance unit fails to honor its agreement to repay the Department by either a lump-sum or installment payments, the Department recoups by grant reduction.

4. Other Methods of Recovery

Regardless of whether an individual is presently receiving TFA benefits, other lawful means of recouping an overpayment may be used, including the following:

a. referral to the Office of the Attorney General for collection action; and

b. withholding of a state tax refund as allowed by Section 12-742 of the Connecticut General Statutes.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8580.40 page 3 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Error TFA ____________________________________________________________ Subject: Recoupment ______________________________________________________________________________

8580.40 C. Factors Affecting Recoupment Rate

1. When the Department recoups, the amount of the monthly recoupment rate depends on factors such as the size of the assistance unit, the unit's income, and the unit's shelter costs.

2. For this purpose, the shelter costs considered are the assistance unit's actual rental or mortgage costs.

D. Maximum Monthly Rate of Recoupment

1. The Department recoups an overpayment at a monthly rate which allows the assistance unit to retain from its gross income (including the assistance payment) an amount equal to at least 90% of the unit's total income.

2. If a court orders the assistance unit to repay the Department at a rate higher than the rate determined by the Department, the Department accepts the rate set by the court.

E. Shelter Hardship

1. If the assistance unit's monthly shelter costs are less than 30% of the unit's gross monthly income (including the assistance payment) the rate of recoupment is the maximum allowed under paragraph D.

2. If the assistance unit's monthly shelter costs are equal to or greater than 30% of the unit's gross monthly income (including the assistance payment), the rate of the recoupment is reduced as follows:

% of Gross Monthly Income % of Total Income (PA plus other Used for Shelter Costs income) the Unit is Allowed to Retain At Least Less Than 30% 35% 92% 35% 40% 93% 40% 45% 94% 45% 50% 95% 50% 55% 96% 55% and over 60% 97%

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8580.40 page 4 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Error TFA ____________________________________________________________ Subject: Recoupment ______________________________________________________________________________

8580.40 F. Other Factors

The Department may further reduce the rate of recoupment if the assistance unit has an unusual expense over which it has no control, and which it has a legal obligation to pay.

G. Awards Less Than Ten Dollars

1. The assistance unit remains eligible, and the Department issues benefits to the assistance unit for the appropriate amount, if the unit's monthly award is reduced to less than ten dollars because of a recoupment action.

2. An assistance unit which is categorically eligible, but whose monthly deficit is less than ten dollars prior to a recoupment action, and is therefore not receiving a monthly cash award, is not credited with repaying the Department unless the unit actually makes a payment.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES PRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 02-01-04 Transmittal: UP-04-01 8580.50 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Error TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Treatment of Intentional Recipient Error ______________________________________________________________________________

8580.50 A. General Provisions

1. If the Department preliminarily determines that the overpayment resulted from an intentional recipient error, regardless of the dollar amount, the Department determines whether to disqualify the individual from assistance in accordance with the hearing procedures listed at B, below, to refer the case to the State Police or to a prosecuting authority for criminal prosecution, and/or to refer the case to the Attorney General for civil recovery.

2. The Department does not conduct an Administrative Disqualification Hearing to determine intentional program error for the assistance unit if the case has been referred to the court system and the court has ruled the assistance unit not guilty. Such cases are treated as unintentional recipient error.

3. The Department takes immediate action to initiate recoupment notwithstanding that the case may also have been referred to either the Division of Criminal Justice or to the Office of the Attorney General.

4. Administrative action to recoup the overpayment continues if the case is determined to be an unintentional recipient error.

B. Determining Intentional Recipient Error

1. The Department conducts Administrative Disqualification Hearings in certain instances to determine whether an individual has caused an overpayment by committing an intentional recipient error.

2. Such hearings are held in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 54 of the Connecticut General Statutes and the Department's rules of practice, Regulations of Connecticut Agencies (Social Services) Section 17-311-11 through 17-311-40 as modified by 7050.05 through 7050.25 and 7050.35 of the Uniform Policy Manual.

3. At the discretion of the hearing officer, the Department may consolidate a TFA hearing to determine intentional recipient error with any other administrative hearing with related factual or legal issues. Such other hearings may include, but are not limited to Food Stamp Administrative Disqualification Hearings.

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICESPRIVATE UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8580.60 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Error TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Disqualification Periods and Penalties ______________________________________________________________________________

8580.60 A. Disqualification

An individual is disqualified from receiving assistance if:

1. a court determines that he or she is guilty of a crime based upon the allegation of intentional receipt of benefits to which the individual was not entitled or grants the individual accelerated rehabilitation based upon such allegation; or

2. a determination of an intentional recipient error is made by the Department.

B. Disqualification Periods

An individual who is found to have committed an intentional recipient error is disqualified for the time period specified below unless this period is contrary to a court order:

1. six (6) months for the first offense;

2. twelve (12) months for the second offense;

3. permanently for the third offense.

C. Effective Date of Disqualification

1. An individual receiving assistance at the time of the finding of intentional recipient error is disqualified effective:

a. the date specified by the court order, if the court order specifies that an individual may not receive assistance for a period of time; or

b. the date set by the Department, but not later than forty-five (45) days from the date of the court order if the court does not specify the date; or

c. the month following the expiration of the advance notice period unless the person requests a Fair Hearing within ten (10) days from the date the notice of adverse action was mailed. (cross reference: 8525.10)

CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES UNIFORM POLICY MANUAL ______________________________________________________________________________ Date: 7-1-97 Transmittal: UP-98-3 8580.60 page 2 ______________________________________________________________________________ Section: Type: Jobs First POLICY ______________________________________________________________________________ Chapter: Program: Benefit Error TFA _______________________________________________________________ Subject: Disqualification Periods and Penalties ______________________________________________________________________________

8580.60 C. Effective Date of Disqualification (continued)

2. If the individual who is disqualified is not otherwise eligible for the program at the time the disqualification period is to begin, the disqualification period is effective as of the date the individual reapplies and is found otherwise eligible for benefits.

3. The period of disqualification, once it becomes effective, runs continuously without interruption for the length of the disqualification period regardless of other eligibility factors.

D. Effect of Disqualified Individual on Assistance Unit

1. The needs of the disqualified individual are not taken into consideration in determining eligibility or calculating benefits of the rest of the assistance unit.

2. As long as the disqualified individual resides with the assistance unit, his or her assets are deemed available to the assistance unit in accordance with 8550.20 and his or her income is deemed available in accordance with 8560.15.

3. If the disqualified individual moves into the home of another assistance unit, his or her income and assets may affect the eligibility of that assistance unit. (cross reference: 8550.20 and 8560.15)

4. Each member of the assistance unit from which the individual was disqualified is subject to recoupment action by the Department, as described in 8580.50, regardless of the unit's present eligibility for benefits.
